new_elements: Thermochromic heat cap (Caps turn opaque or color-coded when overheating.); Automatic thermal cutoff visual (Safety is shown, not configured.)
rationale: Overheating protection is shown visually without user setup.
judge_comment: Thermochromic indicators are plausible, but they show safety status rather than simplify operation, so they only loosely serve the need.

title: Hydrophobic Anti-Splatter Coating
new_elements: Hydrophobic cavity film (Oil and water sheet off instead of mica cover.); Splash-shedding liner (No cleaning ritual or replaceable mica.)
rationale: Splatter handling is passive coating, not a replaceable part to learn.
judge_comment: A hydrophobic liner could replace the mica cover and remove a maintenance step, but it does little for operation, and microwave-safe coatings are hard to make durable.

title: Capacitive One-Touch Panel
new_elements: Capacitive touch sheet (One flat sheet replaces knobs and door button.); Tap-to-heat panel (Press anywhere once to heat.)
rationale: One flat touch surface replaces knobs and mechanical buttons.
judge_comment: A single tap-to-heat panel directly cuts operating complexity and is easy to build, but touch panels are already common.

title: Passive Cooking Diffuser
new_elements: Fixed RF diffuser plate (Static ridges distribute waves without rotation.); Uniform passive heating (No turntable motor or speed knob.)
rationale: Uniform heating is passive, removing turntable and power-level learning.
judge_comment: A static RF diffuser is a real substitute (a stirrer) that removes the turntable and simplifies use, but it doesn't remove power-level choices on its own.

title: Auto-Stop Steam Vent
new_elements: Steam-trigger shutoff vent (Excess steam stops heating automatically.); Steam-done stop (User does not set exact time.)
rationale: Steam tells the microwave to stop, so exact timing is unnecessary.
judge_comment: Steam-triggered auto-stop removes the need to set a time, which directly serves zero-learning operation, though a steam sensor is a plausible but unreliable substitute for a timer.

title: Conductive Gel Interlock
new_elements: Door-gap conductive gel strip (Gel continuity replaces mechanical interlock contacts.); Gel-sensing safety (No switch alignment learning.)
rationale: Safety sensing becomes continuous and simple instead of switch alignment.
judge_comment: A gel-based interlock is a wild substitution but is invisible to the user, so it does little for ease of operation and raises safety concerns.

title: Universal Plugless Coupler
new_elements: Snap-fit wireless coupler (Power enters through a keyed base without plug.); No-plug safe power (No cord or standard voltage learning.)
rationale: Power connection is a single snap fit, no plug knowledge.
judge_comment: Wireless power at microwave levels is impractical and efficiency would be poor, and plugging in is not a learning barrier anyway.

title: Single Twist Ball Control
new_elements: Twist-to-start ball knob (Rotating ball selects time and power with one motion.); Ball-control cooking (One ball replaces knobs and door button.)
rationale: One ball combines time and power actions for intuitive control.
judge_comment: A single ball control is feasible and simplifies the interface, but combining time and power in one motion may still need some learning.

title: Field Monitor Glow
new_elements: Cooking field glow strip (Housing lights pulse to show heating is active.); Visible heating status (Users need no timer readout.)
rationale: A visible pulse tells users the microwave is cooking, no readout learning.
judge_comment: A glow strip is easy to build, but it only shows status and does not simplify how the user sets or controls cooking.

title: Door-Weight Safety Interlock
new_elements: Door weight sensor (Door position inferred from hinge force and mass.); Weighted safety logic (No separate microswitch logic to understand.)
rationale: Door safety is inferred from weight and motion instead of switches.
judge_comment: Inferring door state from weight is unreliable and risky for a safety interlock, and it does little to simplify the user's operation.

title: No-Light Projection Screen
new_elements: Internal projection screen (Projects cavity image on door surface, not light bulb.); Projected cooking view (View inside without seeing through holes.)
rationale: The projected view removes need to understand door light holes.
judge_comment: A projected cavity view is novel, but a projector inside a microwave cavity is impractical and does little for ease of use.

title: Child-Proof One-Press Lock
new_elements: Press-to-cook child lock (One deliberate press both locks and starts.); Locking simple start (Safe without complex interlock.)
rationale: Safety locking is merged with the single start action.
judge_comment: A single press that both locks and starts is simple and feasible, though the claim of safety without an interlock is dubious.

title: Automatic Stirring Plate
new_elements: Self-stirring cavity plate (Plate contains internal rotating parts driven by RF.); Auto stirrer assist (No manual stirring or turntable motor.)
rationale: The plate assists uniform heating without user stirring decisions.
judge_comment: A self-stirring plate removes the stirring decision, but RF-driven moving parts inside the cavity are hard to make safe and reliable.

title: Cordless Color Knobless Power
new_elements: Color-coded wireless power puck (Puck position and color set RF power.); Puck power selection (Power changes by sliding puck, no knob.)
rationale: Sliding a colored puck selects power visibly without a knob.
judge_comment: A slide-to-set color puck gives an intuitive, visible power control that needs no learning, and it is plausible with magnetic or position sensing.

title: Thermal Resonance Auto Time
new_elements: Thermal resonance sensor (Cavity acoustic resonance changes with cook time.); Resonance-set cook time (No dial timing, stop point sensed by material.)
rationale: Cook time is sensed by material resonance, not set by the user.
judge_comment: Auto-sensed cook end removes timing decisions, but acoustic resonance as a reliable doneness signal is dubious and food variability is huge.

title: Melt-In Door Seal Shape
new_elements: Melt-in door seal shape (Thermoplastic seal forms choke geometry during assembly.); Self-forming leak seal (No separate choke rim to install or learn.)
rationale: Seal geometry is formed automatically, avoiding user alignment learning.
judge_comment: A manufacturing-time seal change has little to do with user operation, and a melted seal is questionable for RF safety.

title: Aromatic Finish Cue
new_elements: Safe scent diffuser (Ends heating cycle with a neutral scent cue.); Aroma done signal (No bell timing or screen reading.)
rationale: A gentle scent cue signals finish without interpreting a bell or dial.
judge_comment: A scent cue is novel but it's only a done signal, may be unreliable, and arguably adds confusion with food smells.

title: Camera Mirror Viewing
new_elements: Door-mirror camera viewer (Tiny mirror shows cavity view in door glass.); Mirror-cooked view (No light bulb or door holes.)
rationale: Mirror viewing replaces light and holes with an instantly understandable reflected image.
judge_comment: A mirror view is simple, but it doesn't reduce the learning curve of operating the microwave and the 'camera' part is muddled.

title: Magnetron Soft-Start Switch
new_elements: Soft-start HV switch (Electronically ramps magnetron voltage.); Gradual microwave ramp (Power starts with one simple step.)
rationale: Starting RF becomes one smooth action, hiding complex voltage logic.
judge_comment: Soft-start is technically plausible and hides complexity internally, but it barely changes what the user must learn.

title: Self-Leveling Turntable
new_elements: Self-leveling turntable base (Motorized base aligns and rotates without manual glass.); Automatic plate leveling (No centering or turntable orientation.)
rationale: The plate positions itself, removing user centering learning.
judge_comment: Self-leveling base solves a minor issue (centering) rather than operation complexity, and the mechanism is vague.

title: Passive Power Limit by Mass
new_elements: Mass-sensing power limiter (Passive load resistor sets max watts from food mass.); Auto wattage by weight (No power level selection.)
rationale: Weight determines safe wattage and time automatically.
judge_comment: A passive load resistor setting wattage from mass is physically muddled, though auto power by weight does reduce choices.

title: No-Button Weight Start
new_elements: Weight-activated start tray (Tray starts safe heating when food is added.); Set-and-start cooking (No button or dial at all.)
rationale: Simply placing food on the tray starts cooking with no buttons.
judge_comment: Placing food to start removes all controls, but there are safety and intent concerns, and weight alone doesn't give the cook time.

title: All-In One Plate Sensor
new_elements: Integrated plate sensor (Plate measures moisture and weight and drives cycle.); One-place auto heating (Only action is putting food on plate.)
rationale: Plate sensing selects settings, so the user has no controls to learn.
judge_comment: A sensing plate that drives the cycle gives a zero-learning interface, but embedding moisture sensors in a microwave-safe plate is hard.

title: One-Action Cooking Capsule
new_elements: Insert cooking capsule (Capsule carries preset energy and opens at end.); Capsule auto cooking (User inserts capsule and closes door once.)
rationale: Capsule insertion and door closing are the only actions needed.
judge_comment: Capsule insert plus door close is a clear single-action flow that is plausible with coded packaging, though it needs a consumable ecosystem.

title: One-Button Heat
new_elements: One-Button Timer Cap (Single large press for 10-second steps.); Fixed 10s Interval Oscillator (Counts presses instead of a 30-min cam.); One-Push Heating (Start, add, and stop from one place.)
rationale: Replaces dial learning with one obvious button.
judge_comment: A single-button 10-second increment interface is simple and practical, but it is close to existing quick-start buttons and not radical.

title: Door-Close Cook
new_elements: Door-Close Cook Button (Cooking starts automatically when the door closes.); Magnetic Latch Encoder (Reads door state without a mechanical switch stack.); Close-and-Start (No separate start action is needed.)
rationale: The user learns nothing: shut the door, it cooks.
judge_comment: Auto-start on door close removes a step, but it has no way to set time or power and carries safety risks such as accidental starts or running empty.

title: No-Door Faraday Curtain
new_elements: RF Curtain Door (A hanging conductive curtain replaces a hinged door.); Conductive Mesh Curtain (RF-blocking woven sheet that self-closes.); Open-Front Cooking (Access without learning door mechanics.)
rationale: Removes door-button and latch confusion.
judge_comment: A curtain instead of a door is wildly novel, but it would leak RF and fail safety regulations, and it does not address operation complexity.

title: Transparent Microwave Body
new_elements: Clear Oven Shell (Whole casing is microwave-transparent glass.); Microwave-transparent Electrochromic Glass (Transparent shell that can tint for safety.); Full-View Cooking (User sees the cavity without opening anything.)
rationale: No lamp or window routine to learn.
judge_comment: A transparent shell is radical but unrealistic because it would not contain microwaves, and visibility does not simplify operation much.

title: Webcam Interior
new_elements: Interior Webcam (Camera looks through the waveguide shield.); RF-shielded CMOS Optics (Lens path that survives 2.45 GHz leakage.); Phone Live View (Live cavity video replaces peeking and guessing.)
rationale: Checking progress becomes passive, not learned behavior.
judge_comment: An interior camera is plausible with shielded optics, but it adds complexity via a phone and addresses monitoring, not operation simplicity.

title: Smartphone Dashboard
new_elements: Phone Dock Display (A cradle makes the phone the timer and display.); NFC Tap Timer (Phone-to-oven handoff by tap.); Tap-to-Set (No oven controls are needed.)
rationale: Uses familiar phone UI instead of new oven controls.
judge_comment: Phone use adds a pairing and app step, which is arguably more of a learning curve than a simple dial, and it is not a cheaper substitution.

title: Voice Single Sentence
new_elements: Hotword Button (One button wakes only a short oven phrase.); Offline Wake-word IC (Tiny chip listens for one command.); Speak-to-Start (Plain spoken time starts cooking.)
rationale: Learning a dial is replaced by saying a number.
judge_comment: A single-phrase offline wake-word chip is cheap and plausible, and saying a time needs almost no learning, though noise and accents are a risk.

title: Shape-Preset Timer
new_elements: Shape Knob (Physical shapes replace numbers and watts.); Shape Recognition Cam (Simple camera reads the shape angle.); Shape-Only Presets (Popcorn, plate, mug, soup only.)
rationale: Users choose familiar shapes, not unfamiliar settings.
judge_comment: Shape presets are intuitive, but a camera to read a knob angle is overengineered when a mechanical detent would do, and the shape-to-food mapping is unclear.

title: Weight-Based Cook
new_elements: Load-Cell Floor (Turntable floor measures food mass.); Auto Time-from-Weight Algorithm (Maps grams to simple time presets.); Weight Auto Time (No timer entry needed.)
rationale: Put food in and press one key.
judge_comment: A load cell is cheap and removes timer entry, but weight alone does not capture food type, so accuracy is limited.

title: Camera Auto Wattage
new_elements: Food Camera (Looks at food to pick power level.); One-Shot Image Classification (Tiny classifier for common foods.); Auto Power Pick (Replaces 5-step power knob.)
rationale: No need to understand wattage.
judge_comment: Camera classification removes the need to understand power levels, but cost, steam on the lens, and misclassification make it harder, and it is not a simplification of parts.

title: Turntable-Free Stirring
new_elements: Waveguide Stirrer (RF mode stirrer replaces rotating plate.); RF Field Chopper (Mechanically varies field distribution.); Static Cavity Heating (Food can be placed anywhere.)
rationale: No plate alignment learning curve.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are already common in microwaves, and removing the turntable only loosely improves ease of use, though it is a plausible substitution.

title: Gravity-Fed Turntable
new_elements: Ball-Bearing Turnplate (Plate rotates from door push and food motion.); Self-Rotating Bearing (Passive low-friction rotation.); No-Motor Turntable (Turns without a timed motor.)
rationale: Removes motor and gear confusion.
judge_comment: A passive bearing plate that turns from door push and food motion is unreliable and barely touches the no-learning-curve need.

title: Piezo Turntable
new_elements: Piezo Ring Drive (Flat ring under plate moves it silently.); Silent Ultrasonic Drive (Uses vibration instead of gears.); Flat Turntable Motion (Thin, quiet, maintenance-free rotation.)
rationale: No noisy motor or belt to interpret.
judge_comment: A piezo ring drive is novel, but moving a heavy plate this way is hard and the user benefit is marginal.

title: Passive Cooling Fan
new_elements: Thermal Fan (Fan that runs from cavity heat, not controls.); Thermo-EMF Fan (Temperature gradient powers airflow.); Self-Powered Cooling (Automatic heat removal.)
rationale: User never learns thermostat behavior.
judge_comment: A thermo-EMF fan is hidden from the user and would likely produce too little airflow to cool the magnetron.

title: Acoustic Burn Monitor
new_elements: Burn Microphone (Listening element inside cavity.); Acoustic Caramelization Model (Detects crackle as doneness signal.); Hear-Doneness Stop (Stops when the sound changes.)
rationale: No timer or power knowledge required.
judge_comment: Listening for doneness removes timer and power decisions, which serves the need directly, but acoustic detection is unreliable across foods.

title: Optical Color Stop
new_elements: Color Sensor (Optical sensor detects browning.); Narrowband Reflectance Detector (Sees food color change.); Browns When Done (Automatic stop at color target.)
rationale: Users learn a visual cue, not a setting.
judge_comment: Auto-stop on browning removes the need to set a time, but color sensing inside a microwave cavity is hard and many foods don't brown.

title: Anti-Superheat Steam Valve
new_elements: Micro-Perforated Steam Vent (Vent that releases nucleation risk automatically.); Capillary Boil Vent (Uses tiny pores to seed boiling.); Prevent Superheated Liquid (Stops eruptive boiling without user action.)
rationale: Hides liquid-heating risk from the user.
judge_comment: It addresses a safety concern invisibly, but it has little connection to simple operation or learning curve.

title: Porous Stirring Mug
new_elements: Porous Mug Insert (Ceramic sleeve that sits around cups.); Nucleation Porous Ceramic (Micro-pores trigger even boiling.); Safe Cup Heating (One mug shape works for everyone.)
rationale: No explanation needed for hot drinks.
judge_comment: A porous ceramic insert is plausible and simple, but it targets boiling safety, and an extra accessory doesn't reduce operating complexity.

title: One-Minute Inertia Timer
new_elements: Flywheel Timer (Wind up minutes by turning a weight.); Mechanical Flywheel Latch (Inertia sets coarse time.); Wind-and-Start (Winding starts cooking immediately.)
rationale: A single physical motion teaches itself.
judge_comment: A wind-up mechanical timer is intuitive and cheap, and it substitutes a simple part, though it is a familiar old-style mechanism with coarse control.

title: No Knob: Rotating Door
new_elements: Rotating Door Dial (Door edge doubles as time setter.); Door-as-Clock (Door rotation angle encodes minutes.); Spin Door to Set Time (Set time with the object being opened.)
rationale: No second control to discover.
judge_comment: A door that doubles as a time dial is a radical substitution of controls, but it is mechanically awkward and may conflict with door sealing and safety interlocks.

title: Color-Light Start
new_elements: RGB Start Ring (Glowing ring around door becomes start control.); Touch Color Selector (Touch color selects simple time.); Color to Time (Choose red, yellow, green, blue for presets.)
rationale: Uses visual color instead of technical settings.
judge_comment: Color presets with a glowing start ring simplify operation, but users must still learn what each color means in time or power.

title: Haptic Finish Alert
new_elements: Haptic Door Edge (Door frame vibrates when done.); Piezo Haptic Driver (Quiet buzz replaces bell.); Silent Done (Tactile completion signal.)
rationale: No need to learn audible codes.
judge_comment: A haptic done signal is plausible but only affects the end of cooking and is easily missed when nobody is touching the door.

title: Smell-Stop Sensor
new_elements: Volatile Gas Sensor (Detects cooking volatiles and steam.); Metal-Oxide Nose (Simple gas sensor for doneness and risk.); Smell-to-Stop (Stops at the first sign of overheat.)
rationale: Uses natural food cues instead of settings.
judge_comment: Gas-sensing auto-cook is a real approach (sensor cook) that removes settings, though it already exists in some models and the metal-oxide sensor is imprecise.

title: Laser Browning Module
new_elements: Infrared Browning Laser (Low-power IR array adds surface browning.); Solid-state Laser Heater (Laser spots replace crisp confusion.); Microwave-plus-Brown (One start button gives browned finish.)
rationale: User does not learn why crisp mode exists.
judge_comment: One-button browning is helpful, but IR lasers inside a microwave cavity are impractical and costly, and the idea does not truly simplify operation.

title: Air-Cooled HV Discharge
new_elements: Pneumatic Discharge Tube (Ionized air bleeds HV at shutoff.); Ionized Air Bleeder (No bleeder resistor to fail or learn about.); No-Charge Shutoff (Self-neutralizes stored energy.)
rationale: Removes dangerous knowledge after unplugging.
judge_comment: Aimed at servicing safety rather than user operation, and ionized air cannot realistically replace a bleeder resistor.

title: Plasma Lamp Discharge
new_elements: Plasma Bleed Lamp (Plasma path consumes HV as light.); Gas-Discharge HV Sink (Uses controlled glow to discharge.); Lighting Discharge (HV disappears visibly.)
rationale: Safety happens visibly without explanation.
judge_comment: A visible plasma discharge is a striking idea, but it barely affects ease of operation, and a glowing HV sink is questionable as a safety design.

title: Wireless Power Microwave
new_elements: Resonant Power Plate (Countertop pad supplies power without plug.); Qi-style 50 Hz Induction (Mains-frequency wireless coupling.); Cordless Cooking (No plug, socket, or cord learning.)
rationale: Removes plug and cord confusion.
judge_comment: Cordless operation removes the plug, but a 1 kW+ load over 50 Hz wireless coupling is highly impractical and the idea doesn't touch the controls.

title: Retractable Cord
new_elements: Self-Retract Cord (Cord stays tidy after use.); Spiral Motor Tether (Simple retract spool hides cable.); Tidy Cord (No storage learning.)
rationale: Students see no messy cable to manage.
judge_comment: A retractable cord is easy to build and commonplace, but it has little to do with a no-learning-curve interface.

title: Absorbing Choke Foam
new_elements: RF Foam Seal (Flexible absorber at door rim.); Carbon-loaded Silicone Foam (Broadband RF absorption for safety.); Foam Door Choke (Simpler sealing without quarter-wave precision.)
rationale: Fewer tricky door gaps to notice.
judge_comment: RF-absorbing foam on the door is plausible and does replace the choke, but users would never notice it, so it does little for ease of use.

title: Hydrophobic Mica Alternative
new_elements: Ceramic Splash Shield (Drop-in tile over waveguide.); Sacrificial Ceramic Tile (Cheap tile replaces delicate mica sheet.); Waveguide Protection (Keep splatter out without repair knowledge.)
rationale: Replace hidden part by simple disposable shield.
judge_comment: A ceramic tile instead of mica is feasible and concrete, but it concerns maintenance of a hidden part rather than operation.

title: No Interlock RF Shutter
new_elements: Motorized RF Shutter (Physical waveguide flap blocks RF.); Waveguide Flap (Shuts power path mechanically.); Shutter Safety (No switch sequence to learn.)
rationale: Safety becomes obvious blockage, not electronics.
judge_comment: A mechanical RF shutter is a plausible safety substitute, but users never operate interlocks anyway, so it barely serves the no-learning-curve need and adds cost.

title: Hall-Effect Door Safety
new_elements: Door Magnet Sensor (Magnet-on-door and sensor-on-frame.); Triple Hall Effect Voting (Three magnet readings replace microswitches.); Switchless Interlock (No moving switch contacts to trust.)
rationale: Eliminates complex switch behavior.
judge_comment: Hall sensors are technically feasible but invisible to the user, so they do nothing for ease of operation and may fall short of the redundant-interlock safety requirements.

title: Magnetic Pop Door
new_elements: MagPop Release (Magnet lever pops door without button.); Memory-Shaped Magnet Lever (Springless latch release.); One-Touch Open (Open door with natural handle touch.)
rationale: Handle is the control; no button to discover.
judge_comment: Opening the door by touching the handle removes the need to find a button, which is intuitive, though the shape-memory-magnet detail is vague.

title: Pop-Up Tray
new_elements: Lift Tray (Tray rises when cooked.); Shape-memory Alloy Lift (Wire actuator raises hot plate safely.); Eject Hot Plate (Food comes out without reaching in.)
rationale: Users learn nothing about handling hot interiors.
judge_comment: An ejecting hot tray is a striking idea that simplifies handling, but SMA actuation, cost and spill risk make it impractical.

title: Self-Aligning Plate
new_elements: Camming Ring (Ring guides plate into correct rotation.); Passive Plate Alignment (Shape matching replaces user aim.); No-Aim Plate (Drop plate anywhere and it seats.)
rationale: Removes fiddly turntable fitting.
judge_comment: A passive camming ring that seats the plate is cheap and removes a minor fiddly step, though it is a small gain for the need.

title: Transparent Turntable LEDs
new_elements: LED Turntable Rim (Glass plate has embedded light ring.); Optically Conducted Lighting (Edge lighting through glass.); Turntable Glow (Light follows the food, not cavity bulb.)
rationale: User sees without lamp behavior to learn.
judge_comment: Edge-lit glass plate is plausible but does little to remove learning and a rotating plate complicates powering the light.

title: Glow-in-Dark Cavity
new_elements: Phosphor Cavity (Interior coating glows after door closes.); Long-persistent Luminescence (No powered light needed.); No-Lamp Light (Cavity visibly active without bulb.)
rationale: Eliminates learning where the light comes from.
judge_comment: A phosphor coating is a clever substitute for the lamp, but it would not charge in a dark closed cavity and has little effect on ease of use.

title: Disposable Insert
new_elements: Paper Cavity Insert (Microwave-safe pulp tray lines cavity.); Microwave-safe Pulp Tray (Cheap paper liner replaces glass plate.); No-Metal Fear (User avoids plate and foil mistakes.)
rationale: Single obvious object removes plate rules.
judge_comment: A disposable pulp liner simplifies the plate rules, but it adds waste and recurring cost and it is unclear how it handles liquids.

title: No-Timer QR Menu
new_elements: QR Start Tag (Stick-on code tells oven what to do.); Offline Barcode Decoder (Tiny scanner reads preset instruction.); Scan-and-Cook (No time or power selection.)
rationale: Instruction is in the object, not learned.
judge_comment: Scan-to-cook removes the need to set time or power, and the technology exists, though it depends on tags being available.

title: Auto Stop at Boil
new_elements: Steam Valve Stop (Valve detects full boiling and cuts power.); Acoustic Boil Detector (Steam sound triggers safe stop.); Stop at Boil (No need to guess time.)
rationale: Boiling replaces timing knowledge.
judge_comment: Stopping automatically at boil removes the need to guess a time, but it only covers liquids and reliable detection is hard.

title: Temperature Target Dial
new_elements: Target Temp Knob (Set desired food temperature, not time.); IR Core Temp Loop (Infrared estimate drives heating.); Cook to Temp (User only picks warm or hot.)
rationale: No time-power conversion to learn.
judge_comment: Setting a target temperature removes the need to learn time and power settings, and IR sensing is plausible, though the estimate of core temperature is limited.

title: Crackle Power Control
new_elements: Crackle Mic (Sound sensor controls magnetron duty.); Sound-Triggered Duty Control (Loud crackle raises power, quiet lowers it.); Volume-to-Watts (Food tells oven how hard to heat.)
rationale: No wattage knob to understand.
judge_comment: Using sound to drive power is a wild idea, but it is unreliable and unrelated to a user's goal, and the user gets no clearer control.

title: Cavity Ion Shield
new_elements: Ionized Cavity Shield (Coated cavity suppresses accidental metal.); Faraday Coating Spray (Conductive but non-mesh coating.); Arc Suppression (Prevents sparks from common mistakes.)
rationale: User does not need to memorize metal rules.
judge_comment: Removing metal rules would help, but a coating that suppresses arcing in a microwave is physically implausible and unsafe.

title: Food Surface Sensor
new_elements: Surface Temp Patch (Thermal patch placed on food.); Thermochromic Crayon (Color changes when surface is done.); Brown Alert (User sees readiness without power knowledge.)
rationale: Readiness is shown by color, not settings.
judge_comment: A color-change indicator is simple and cheap, but it adds a consumable the user must handle and it does not directly simplify operation.

title: One-Second Shake Timer
new_elements: Shake-to-Add Timer (Shake the oven to add seconds.); Accelerometer Increment (Tiny sensor counts shakes.); Shake to Start (Physical gesture replaces dialing.)
rationale: A natural action teaches itself.
judge_comment: Shaking to add seconds is intuitive and cheap with an accelerometer, though accidental triggers and a shaking oven are concerns.

title: Door Handle as Power Knob
new_elements: Handle Dial (Door handle rotates to set power.); Twist-Handle Power Selector (Handle angle controls magnetron duty.); Turn Door to Set (One object controls two steps.)
rationale: Uses the obvious handle instead of hidden power knob.
judge_comment: Merging door and power setting is intuitive and substitutes a part, though it conflates opening with setting power and still needs a time input.

title: No-Magnetron Resistive Heater
new_elements: Graphite Heat Coil (Replaces HV path with simple hot surface.); Graphite Resistive Heater (High-temperature carbon heating.); Oven-like Heating (Familiar heating behavior without RF knowledge.)
rationale: Users understand heat from normal experience.
judge_comment: Resistive heating is plausible and familiar but basically turns the microwave into a slow toaster oven, losing speed, and doesn't directly simplify operation.

title: Self-Explaining Icons
new_elements: Icon Door Panel (Door has only food icons.); Pictogram Touch Overlay (Simple touch icons trigger presets.); Press Icon Cook (No numbers, words, or buttons.)
rationale: Pictures replace instructions.
judge_comment: Icon presets are very feasible and reduce learning, but they are common and not radical.

title: No-Bell Finish via Phone
new_elements: Phone Finish Notifier (Small tag sends done event to phone.); BLE Done Beacon (Low-energy beacon for completion.); Phone Rings (Familiar notification replaces oven bell.)
rationale: Uses existing phone alert habits.
judge_comment: Phone notification is feasible but adds a device dependency and doesn't simplify core operation.

title: Universal Food Insert
new_elements: One-Fit Plate Mold (Universal polymer dish holds any food.); Microwave-Shape Polymer (Deformable tray seals around containers.); Any Dish Fits (No container rules to learn.)
rationale: One physical object replaces many usage rules.
judge_comment: A universal deformable tray removing container rules is interesting but physically dubious and vaguely defined.

title: 01 One-Dial Start
new_elements: Single Rotary Start Dial (One knob sets time and starts cooking.); Dial Start Cook (Cook with one dial motion.)
rationale: One dial replaces two knobs, so users can start cooking without choosing power and time separately.
judge_comment: Single dial that sets time and starts is simple and feasible, but it already exists on many cheap microwaves and is not radical.

title: 02 Big Handle Start
new_elements: Integrated Handle Start (Door handle doubles as the start control.); Handle Start Cook (Begin heating by gripping the handle.)
rationale: One hand action on the handle starts the microwave, eliminating a separate button.
judge_comment: Handle-as-start is intuitive, but accidental starts and an empty cavity are safety concerns, and it conflicts with the need to open the door.

title: 03 Tap-Top Start
new_elements: Top Tap Sensor (A pressure pad on the top starts short cycles.); Tap Time Cook (Tap once for ten seconds and cooking begins.)
rationale: Tap once to add ten seconds, so no dial or keypad must be learned.
judge_comment: Tap-to-add-ten-seconds is very easy to learn and plausible, but it limits control for longer cooking.

title: 04 Weight-One-Button
new_elements: Weight Sensing Tray (The tray measures food weight before cooking.); Weight Auto Cook (Weight chooses duration and one button starts.)
rationale: Users only put food in and press one button, avoiding timer estimation.
judge_comment: Weight sensing with a single button removes time estimation entirely, though weight alone poorly determines the right heating time and it adds cost.

title: 05 Magnetic Door Seal
new_elements: Magnetic Door Seal (The door closes with magnets and no lever latch.); Magnetic Door Access (Open and close the cavity without a push button.)
rationale: Magnetic closing removes a latch button, making door use intuitive.
judge_comment: Magnetic closing only affects the door and has weak ties to operation learning, and microwave seal and safety interlock needs make it problematic.

title: 06 Transparent Faraday Shell
new_elements: Transparent Faraday Shell (A see-through microwave shield replaces the perforated door.); Safe See Through Cooking (Watch food without mesh or interior light.)
rationale: A clear shell lets users check progress directly, reducing guessing and button use.
judge_comment: A transparent Faraday shell is plausible with conductive transparent films, but it only helps visibility and does little for simple operation.

title: 07 Door Webcam Mirror
new_elements: Door Webcam Mirror (A tiny camera shows the cavity on a mirrored door surface.); No Bulb Visibility (See inside without an interior lamp.)
rationale: A built-in viewing mirror removes the need to guess whether food is ready.
judge_comment: A camera and mirror display is feasible but adds complexity and cost, and it does little to simplify operation.

title: 08 Hourglass Flip Timer
new_elements: Door Hourglass Switch (Flip a sealed hourglass to start a short cook.); Flip To Time (One physical flip sets duration.)
rationale: A flip motion is easier than rotating a numbered knob.
judge_comment: Flipping an hourglass to start a fixed cook is intuitive and mechanically simple, but it offers only one fixed duration.

title: 09 Color-Magnet Food Level
new_elements: Color Magnet Reader (A colored magnet on the tray sets power by reading.); Color Food Power (Color choice selects power without a dial.)
rationale: Match a food color to a tray color instead of learning power numbers.
judge_comment: Matching colors to power levels is novel, but it adds a mapping users must learn and extra parts to manage.

title: 10 Pull-Cord Time
new_elements: Pull-Cord Timer (One cord pull adds a preset cooking interval.); One Pull Time (Pull once to start a simple time cycle.)
rationale: A single pull mimics a familiar cord action and avoids knob calibration.
judge_comment: A pull cord that adds a preset interval is familiar, simple and cheap, and easy to implement electromechanically.

title: 11 Pedal Door Release
new_elements: Foot Pedal Release (A foot pedal opens the latch lever.); Pedal Door Access (Open the door without hand buttons.)
rationale: A foot pedal is easier than finding a small button when hands are full.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is practical and easy to use with full hands, but it only touches door opening and not the overall operation, and it is not very radical.

title: 12 Close-To-Start
new_elements: Door Set Start Interlock (The door closing completes a preset timing path.); Close To Start (Closing the door starts the previous simple cycle.)
rationale: The user closes the door and cooking starts, removing a separate start step.
judge_comment: Starting the cycle when the door closes cuts a step and is easy to feasibly build, though it risks accidental starts and depends on a preset.

title: 13 Static Stirrer Cavity
new_elements: Static Mode Stirrer (Fixed wave stirring removes the rotating plate.); Motorless Even Heat (Heat without aligning or cleaning a turntable.)
rationale: No turntable means fewer pieces to place, remove, and clean.
judge_comment: Static mode stirrers already exist in some microwaves and remove the turntable, which helps cleaning but does little for the learning curve of operating the machine.

title: 14 Magnetic Levitation Tray
new_elements: Magnetic Levitation Tray (The tray floats into place with magnetic guides.); Float Access (Insert food without wrestling a hinged door.)
rationale: A self-aligning floating tray reduces fumbling with hinges and latches.
judge_comment: A levitating tray is eye-catching but expensive and impractical, with unclear shielding, and it doesn't make operation simpler.

title: 15 Push-Tray Microwave
new_elements: Push Tray Doorless Cavity (A food tray pushes into a sealed slot.); Tray Insert Access (Access the cavity by inserting the tray.)
rationale: One push-in tray replaces opening, latching, and aligning a door.
judge_comment: A push-in tray in place of a door is a bold and intuitive concept, but sealing against microwave leakage and handling spills and liquids make it hard.

title: 16 Kettle Lever Control
new_elements: Kettle Lever Dial (A kettle-style lever sets time and power together.); Lift To Set (Lift one lever and press to cook.)
rationale: A single familiar lever avoids understanding two separate microwave dials.
judge_comment: Familiar kettle lever metaphor is plausible, but combining time and power in one lever is vague and may not reduce complexity much.

title: 17 Squeeze-Body Start
new_elements: Squeeze Body Sensor (The whole body senses a gentle squeeze to start.); Grip To Cook (Squeeze the microwave to begin cooking.)
rationale: A body squeeze uses an intuitive grip instead of learning microwave settings.
judge_comment: A squeeze-to-start body is wild but impractical and unclear on how time and power get set, and it risks accidental starts.

title: 18 Big Plus Ten Button
new_elements: Big Plus Ten Button (One oversized button adds ten seconds.); Plus Ten Time (Repeat a large press to extend cooking.)
rationale: A large plus button is easier than reading a small timer knob.
judge_comment: A single big +10s button is very simple and easy to build, but many microwaves already have similar quick-start buttons.

title: 19 Pull Chain Power
new_elements: Pull Chain Power (A pull chain selects one of three simple power paths.); Chain Power (Pull once for high, twice for medium, thrice for low.)
rationale: A lamp-style pull chain replaces abstract power dial numbers.
judge_comment: Pull chain with counts is concrete and cheap, but counting pulls is arguably less intuitive than a dial.

title: 20 Door Magnet Cutoff
new_elements: Door Magnet Cutoff (A magnet cuts power when the door opens.); No Latch Safety (Simple open-shut safety without latch parts.)
rationale: One magnet action is easier than managing a button-lever latch system.
judge_comment: This is a safety component swap that doesn't affect operation simplicity, and a magnet-only cutoff would fall short of safety interlock requirements.

title: 21 Flip Top Lid
new_elements: Flip Top Lid (The whole top flips up instead of a side door.); Flip Access (Open the cavity with one lid lift.)
rationale: A flip lid avoids finding a button and pulling a hinged door.
judge_comment: A top-lift lid is a novel form, but it only changes door access, not operation, and it adds the problem of spills and hot-steam exposure.

title: 22 Faraday Curtain Door
new_elements: Faraday Curtain Door (A microwave-safe curtain covers the cavity.); Curtain Access (Open by pulling aside a soft curtain.)
rationale: A curtain is softer and simpler than a latched rigid door.
judge_comment: A soft curtain is a wild idea, but it is unlikely to contain microwave leakage safely, and it does not simplify cooking operation.

title: 23 Bell Pull Cord
new_elements: Bell Pull Cord (A cord pull starts a timed cooking bell cycle.); Pull Done Signal (Pull once and wait for the bell.)
rationale: A bell-pull action is familiar and does not require setting a clock.
judge_comment: A single pull cord that starts a preset timed cycle is simple, familiar, and mechanically feasible, and it directly removes the learning curve.

title: 24 Food Card Slot
new_elements: Food Card Slot (A food card with magnetic dots sets power.); Card Food Power (Insert a card to choose a simple food mode.)
rationale: Inserting a labeled food card is easier than selecting power levels.
judge_comment: Insert-a-card food modes are intuitive, concrete, and feasible with magnetic sensing, though the user needs a supply of cards.

title: 25 Squeeze Handle Release
new_elements: Squeeze Handle Latch (Squeezing the door handle releases the latch.); Squeeze Door (Open the door by squeezing its handle.)
rationale: A familiar squeeze-to-open action replaces a small release button.
judge_comment: A squeeze handle is feasible and easy to use, but it only modestly simplifies opening the door and does not touch cooking operation.

title: 26 Two-Button Minus And Start
new_elements: Minus And Start Panel (Only a large minus button and a start button remain.); Two Action Control (Start cooking or shorten it with two buttons.)
rationale: Two large buttons are simpler than two numbered knobs.
judge_comment: Two-button minimal interface is very simple, though a minus-only time control is ambiguous about the starting time.

title: 27 Rotary Pulse Time Dial
new_elements: Rotary Pulse Time Dial (A rotary dial sends pulse timing like an old phone.); Dial Pulse Time (Dial a familiar digit to set duration.)
rationale: A rotary pulse dial uses an old familiar motion instead of microwave knob logic.
judge_comment: Rotary pulse dial is familiar to older users but would confuse younger ones, and it is not obviously simpler.

title: 28 Push-to-Open Soft Door
new_elements: Soft Push Door (The door opens when the whole front is pushed softly.); Push Door (Open without locating a button.)
rationale: Pushing any obvious front panel is easier than pressing a labeled latch.
judge_comment: Push-to-open removes the need to find a latch, but it only addresses door opening and risks accidental opening.

title: 29 Wind-Up Alarm Timer
new_elements: Wind Up Alarm Timer (A clock-style winding key sets mechanical time.); Wind Start (Wind and let go to cook.)
rationale: Winding an alarm is a familiar action that avoids reading microwave graduations.
judge_comment: A wind-up timer is intuitive and has a proven mechanism, and it mirrors classic microwave dials.

title: 30 Thermal Glow Door Indicator
new_elements: Thermal Glow Door (The door glows from heat instead of using an interior bulb.); Heat Glow Indicator (See hot progress without lights.)
rationale: A glowing door gives obvious done status without needing to open or inspect.
judge_comment: A door that glows from heat is implausible and unsafe, and it contributes little to ease of operation.

title: 31 Acoustic Done Beacon
new_elements: Acoustic Done Beacon (A small speaker emits different tones for done states.); Sound Done Signal (Learn one tone meaning instead of watching a timer.)
rationale: A single sound cue tells users when cooking is finished.
judge_comment: Microwaves already beep; different tones add little and may add something to learn rather than remove it.

title: 32 Sand Tube Timer
new_elements: Sand Tube Timer (A sealed sand tube triggers a switch when sand falls.); Sand Time (Turn the tube once to cook for its full duration.)
rationale: One flip of a tube is a visible, simple timer that removes dial reading.
judge_comment: A flip-to-cook sand timer is intuitive and a charming substitute for a dial, but a fixed duration limits flexibility and the sand-triggered switch is awkward.

title: 33 Variable Transformer Power
new_elements: Variable Transformer Power (A transformer supplies smoother power than simple on-off cycling.); Smooth Power (Power responds in one obvious direction.)
rationale: Smooth power feels easier than remembering which dial number means which heat.
judge_comment: A variable transformer gives smooth power in principle, but it is heavy and costly, and it doesn't clearly remove any learning.

title: 34 Sliding Tray Heating
new_elements: Linear Sliding Tray (A tray slides through a sealed slot instead of a door.); Slide Heating Access (Access by sliding food in and out.)
rationale: A simple slide removes hinge and latch confusion.
judge_comment: A sliding tray is simple to use, but sealing the microwaves against leakage is hard and the idea is underdeveloped.

title: 35 Shape Memory Door Pin
new_elements: Shape Memory Door Pin (A heated memory wire releases the door pin.); Memory Door (Door opens after a gentle signal.)
rationale: A self-releasing pin reduces force and precision needed to open the door.
judge_comment: A shape memory wire door release is a creative swap, but a mechanical latch already needs no learning, so the gain is marginal.

title: 36 Edge Time Ring
new_elements: Edge Time Ring (A ring around the cavity edge sets time and power.); Edge Time Power (Turn the whole edge to cook.)
rationale: The control is the edge of the microwave, so users need not look for knobs.
judge_comment: A rotating edge ring for time and power is intuitive but vaguely defined, and it is a modest substitution for the knob.

title: 37 Twist Handle Start
new_elements: Twist Handle Start (Twisting the door handle starts a default cycle.); Twist Door Start (Open or start by twisting one handle.)
rationale: A twist is a familiar door action and removes separate start buttons.
judge_comment: A twist handle that starts a default cycle is familiar and simple, and easily built, though the default cycle limits control.

title: 38 Capacitive Door Start
new_elements: Capacitive Door Touch (The entire door surface senses a touch to start.); Touch Door Start (Cook begins when the door is touched.)
rationale: The obvious action is touching the door, with no hidden controls to learn.
judge_comment: Touching the door to start is zero-learning but risks accidental starts, and capacitive sensing on a metal-mesh door is awkward.

title: 39 Fiber Optic Glow Window
new_elements: Fiber Optic Glow Door (Fibers bring outside light through the shielded mesh.); Fiber Visibility (See food without a lamp bulb.)
rationale: Glowing fibers make the door naturally bright, so users need not manage a light.
judge_comment: Fiber optic glow is a clever lamp substitute but barely affects operation simplicity, and light routing through the shield is questionable.

title: 40 Color Heat Plate
new_elements: Color Heat Plate (A thermochromic plate shows a simple heat target.); Plate Heat Target (Remove food when the plate reaches the color.)
rationale: A visible color target removes the need to estimate power levels.
judge_comment: A thermochromic plate gives a visual doneness cue that removes power guessing, but it is unreliable with uneven heating and does not control the microwave.

title: 41 Spring Hinge Auto Open
new_elements: Spring Hinge Auto Open (A latch release lets a spring hinge swing open.); Auto Open Door (Door opens by itself after release.)
rationale: A door that swings open for the user avoids pulling and fiddling.
judge_comment: Spring-open doors already exist on many microwaves, so it is plausible but only mildly helpful for ease of use and barely a substitution.

title: 42 External Weight Shelf
new_elements: External Weight Shelf (A front shelf senses dish weight before insertion.); Shelf Time (The shelf recommends the first cycle.)
rationale: Weighing outside lets users choose a preset instead of estimating time.
judge_comment: Weighing before insertion and suggesting a time cuts guesswork, but it adds cost and is not a simpler substitute.

title: 43 Phone Door Camera Sync
new_elements: Phone Door Camera Sync (A door camera sends the cavity view to a phone.); Phone Visibility (View food on a familiar screen.)
rationale: Using a phone camera screen makes checking food easier than interpreting a dark window.
judge_comment: A phone camera adds complexity and requires an app, which works against a no-learning-curve goal.

title: 44 Pin Chain Door Interlock
new_elements: Pin Chain Door Interlock (A simple pin and chain replaces complex latch levers.); Pin Chain Safety (Door stays closed but opens by pulling one pin.)
rationale: One pin pull is easier than coordinating a button-lever latch.
judge_comment: A pin and chain is a simple idea, but it is awkward and risky for a safety interlock and is not clearly easier to use.

title: 45 Pop-Up Done Flag
new_elements: Pop-Up Done Flag (A colored flag pops up when time finishes.); Flag Done Signal (See the done state without reading a dial.)
rationale: A raised flag is an unmistakable completion cue.
judge_comment: A mechanical done flag is cheap, simple, and clear, but it only addresses the completion cue and not operation.

title: 46 Squeeze Body Ten Seconds
new_elements: Squeeze Body Ten Seconds (Squeezing both sides starts exactly ten seconds.); One Squeeze Ten (One squeeze adds one familiar short cycle.)
rationale: Squeezing to add ten seconds is simpler than selecting time intervals.
judge_comment: Squeeze-to-add-ten-seconds is intuitive and needs no learning, though the squeeze mechanism on a microwave body is vague and risks accidental activation.

title: 47 Transparent Conducting Mesh Door
new_elements: Transparent Conducting Mesh Door (A clear conductive shield replaces perforated metal.); Clear Shield Window (See through a safe unperforated surface.)
rationale: A clear window makes checking food obvious, reducing repeated door opening.
judge_comment: Transparent conductive meshes exist, but this mainly improves visibility and only indirectly serves a no-learning-curve need.

title: 48 Door Pull Sensor Open
new_elements: Door Pull Sensor (A small pull force releases the door magnetically.); Pull Sensor Door (Open by pulling the edge gently.)
rationale: Pulling the door edge is easier than pressing an unlabeled button.
judge_comment: Pull-to-open is already the intuitive norm on many microwaves, so it is plausible and easy to use but not very radical.

title: 49 Phosphorescent Door Window
new_elements: Phosphorescent Door Window (The window stores light and glows when cooking.); Glow Window (Glow reveals cooking without a bulb.)
rationale: A glowing door gives simple visual feedback without controls.
judge_comment: Phosphorescent glow can't be reliably triggered by cooking and offers only weak feedback, with little effect on operation simplicity.

title: 50 Magnet Ball Power Selector
new_elements: Magnet Ball Power Selector (A rolling magnet ball selects a power track.); Ball Power (Move the ball to the desired heat spot.)
rationale: Moving a ball to a marked spot is more concrete than turning a numbered power knob.
judge_comment: A rolling magnet ball is a quirky, tangible selector, but it is imprecise, fragile, and no simpler than existing dials.

title: One Button Only
new_elements: i01_start_button_component (Replace all timer and power controls with one push button.); i01_one_press_cook_function (Starts a fixed safe heating cycle with one action.)
rationale: Users do not need to learn times, power levels, or buttons because a single press starts cooking.
judge_comment: Single start button is simple and very feasible, but a fixed cycle fits few foods and the idea is not radical.

title: Pull Cord Start
new_elements: i02_pull_cord_component (Replace electronic control buttons with a mechanical pull cord.); i02_pull_to_heat_function (Pulling the cord starts a fixed heating cycle.)
rationale: Pull cords are universally understood and remove the need to learn digital controls.
judge_comment: A pull cord is quirky and simple to understand, but it adds mechanical wear, is awkward on a countertop appliance, and still has a fixed cycle.

title: Close Door Auto Heat
new_elements: i03_door_autostart_component (Replace the start knob with a door sensor that detects food and closes.); i03_close_to_heat_function (Closing the door starts a default heating cycle.)
rationale: No control operation is needed; closing the door alone becomes the whole user interface.
judge_comment: Closing the door to start is zero-learning, but accidental starts and empty-run risks need safeguards such as food detection.

title: Say Start
new_elements: i04_voice_component (Replace buttons with a single-word voice trigger module.); i04_say_start_function (Says start and begins a safe default heating time.)
rationale: Speaking one common word is easier than interpreting dials or buttons.
judge_comment: A voice trigger is feasible, but it is a common approach, adds cost, and is unreliable in noisy kitchens or for accents.

title: QR Code Cooking
new_elements: i05_qr_component (Replace manual controls with a QR code on the door and a phone scanner.); i05_scan_to_heat_function (Scanning the code starts a preset heating cycle.)
rationale: One familiar phone scan replaces all microwave-specific settings.
judge_comment: Requiring a phone and scan adds steps and complexity, so it works against the no-learning-curve need and is not cheaper or simpler.

title: Transparent Camera Door
new_elements: i06_transparent_camera_component (Replace interior lamp and door holes with a transparent casing and camera view on a display.); i06_see_without_lamp_function (Lets the user see cooking progress without dedicated internal lighting or perforated viewing.)
rationale: Visual clarity is simplified by one camera feed instead of interpreting a dim window.
judge_comment: A camera feed replacing the lamp and door holes is novel, but it adds cost and complexity and does little for simple operation.

title: One Power Cam
new_elements: i07_fixed_power_cam_component (Replace the 5-step power knob with one fixed duty-cycle cam.); i07_one_power_level_function (Provides one safe output level for all common tasks.)
rationale: Eliminating power selection removes one major learning decision.
judge_comment: A single fixed power level removes a decision and is easy to build, though it limits cooking versatility, such as defrosting.

title: Fixed Tray
new_elements: i08_fixed_tray_component (Replace the rotating turntable motor and glass tray with a fixed flat tray.); i08_no_turntable_function (Holds food without requiring centering or rotating parts.)
rationale: No turntable setup or alignment step is needed, making use simpler.
judge_comment: A fixed tray is cheap and simple, and turntables already need little setup, so the usability gain is modest and heating may be uneven.

title: Magnetic Pull Door
new_elements: i09_magnetic_pull_door_component (Replace the push-release button with a magnetic latch pulled open by a handle.); i09_pull_door_function (Opening the door follows a universal pull action.)
rationale: Pulling a handle is easier to infer than learning a special door button.
judge_comment: A pull handle is intuitive and cheap, but it is a common, incremental change.

title: Vibration Instead of Bell
new_elements: i10_vibration_bell_component (Replace the mechanical bell with a small vibration motor.); i10_haptic_done_function (Signals completion through vibration.)
rationale: Vibration gives a simple non-verbal cue without extra sound interpretation.
judge_comment: Vibration is a plausible done-cue, but a microwave that sits still gives little feedback, and it does not clearly ease operation.

title: Pictogram Time Ring
new_elements: i11_pictogram_ring_component (Replace numeric dial markings with food pictures.); i11_read_icon_time_function (Sets cooking time by choosing an image instead of numbers.)
rationale: Pictures remove the need to understand minutes and numbers.
judge_comment: Food-picture dial removes number literacy, but mapping images to times is vague and somewhat imprecise.

title: Three-Click Knob
new_elements: i12_detent_knob_component (Replace full-range timer knob with a knob that clicks into only off, 1 min, stop.); i12_three_position_cook_function (Provides just one cooking interval and one stop action.)
rationale: Very few positions make operation obvious and eliminate dial guessing.
judge_comment: Extremely simple and feasible, but limited to one interval and not very radical.

title: Touch Anywhere
new_elements: i13_touch_anywhere_component (Replace the dedicated control panel with a simple capacitive touch surface.); i13_tap_surface_function (Tapping anywhere starts heating.)
rationale: Users need not locate a button; touching the appliance starts cooking.
judge_comment: Tap-anywhere start is simple, but accidental activation and safety with an empty or unready cavity are concerns, and it lacks time control.

title: Wave to Heat
new_elements: i14_handwave_sensor_component (Replace buttons with an infrared handwave sensor.); i14_wave_to_heat_function (Starting cooking by waving a hand.)
rationale: A natural gesture can replace a control panel interface.
judge_comment: Wave-to-start is intuitive but not self-evident, risks false triggers, and doesn't address time setting.

title: Barcode Heat
new_elements: i15_barcode_scanner_component (Replace timer settings with a scanner that reads food barcodes.); i15_scan_food_to_heat_function (Looks up or applies preset time and starts heating.)
rationale: Users already understand scanning barcodes, so no microwave expertise is needed.
judge_comment: Scan-to-heat removes settings entirely and is concrete, though it depends on a barcode database and only works for packaged foods.

title: Kettle Lever
new_elements: i16_kettle_lever_component (Replace electronic buttons with a simple kettle-style lever.); i16_lift_to_heat_function (Lift starts cooking and drop stops or pauses.)
rationale: A familiar lever action removes the need to learn button sequences.
judge_comment: Familiar lift-to-heat lever is intuitive, but it needs a way to set time or power and may feel awkward for long cooks.

title: Stop When It Rolls
new_elements: i17_steam_sound_stopper_component (Replace the timer knob with a sound detector for boiling.); i17_stop_when_rolling_function (Ends heating automatically when boiling sound is detected.)
rationale: The user only starts cooking; the machine decides when it is done.
judge_comment: Auto-stop on boiling sound is clever and hands-off, but it only suits liquids and the sound detection is unreliable in a noisy microwave.

title: Weight Sets Time
new_elements: i18_weight_auto_time_component (Replace the timer dial with a load cell under the food tray.); i18_weight_to_heat_function (Chooses a safe heating time based on food mass.)
rationale: Putting food inside is enough; no time calculation is needed.
judge_comment: A load cell is concrete and removes the need to choose a time, though weight alone poorly predicts the right heating time for different foods.

title: NFC Tap
new_elements: i19_nfc_tap_component (Replace control buttons with an NFC reader on the door.); i19_tap_to_heat_function (A phone or card tap starts a preset heating cycle.)
rationale: One familiar tap gesture replaces complex microwave programming.
judge_comment: NFC is easy to build, but it needs a phone or card with presets, which adds a learning step and moves away from simple operation.

title: Color Sticker Cooking
new_elements: i20_color_sticker_sensor_component (Replace settings with colored stickers and a color sensor.); i20_color_to_heat_function (Selected color maps to a fixed heating preset.)
rationale: Color matching is easier than numeric time selection.
judge_comment: Color stickers with a sensor are simple and playful, but users must still choose and apply the stickers, and the presets are rigid.

title: Arrow Stop Instruction
new_elements: i21_arrow_engraving_component (Replace printed labels with a single engraved arrow on the stop control.); i21_follow_arrow_stop_function (Shows users where to move or press to stop.)
rationale: A simple arrow removes confusion during urgent stopping.
judge_comment: A simple engraved arrow on the stop control is easy to build and mildly helpful, but it is incremental rather than radical and covers only the stop action.

title: Two Button Power
new_elements: i22_two_button_power_component (Replace 5-step power knob with only Full and Defrost buttons.); i22_simple_power_switch_function (Limits power choice to two clear tasks.)
rationale: Two buttons are easier to understand than five power levels.
judge_comment: Reducing power choice to Full and Defrost buttons cuts complexity and is easy to build, though it is an obvious simplification.

title: Wind Up Timer
new_elements: i23_wind_up_spring_timer_component (Replace electronics with a mechanical wind-up spring starter.); i23_spring_to_heat_function (Winding once stores a fixed cooking duration.)
rationale: A toy-like wind action is intuitive and avoids digital menus.
judge_comment: A mechanical wind-up timer is intuitive and plausible, as many microwaves already use mechanical timers, but a fixed duration limits flexibility.

title: Audible Tick Timer
new_elements: i24_audible_tick_timer_component (Replace visual display with a mechanical ticking indicator.); i24_count_to_done_function (Lets users know time remaining without reading numbers.)
rationale: Simple ticking removes the need to interpret displays.
judge_comment: A ticking sound gives a rough sense of time left but is less clear than a display and does not simplify operation much.

title: Hand Spin Plate
new_elements: i25_hand_spin_tray_component (Replace turntable motor with a manually rotatable plate on the door.); i25_manual_spin_function (Allows simple even heating without electronics.)
rationale: A direct physical action is easier to understand than automatic settings.
judge_comment: A manual spin plate on the door is odd, adds a user task rather than removing one, and is awkward to build safely given microwave shielding and the door.

title: Fixed Waveguide Aperture
new_elements: i26_fixed_waveguide_aperture_component (Replace power modulation with a fixed waveguide opening.); i26_constant_power_function (Delivers one stable heating output.)
rationale: One constant output eliminates power-level choices.
judge_comment: A fixed aperture removes power choices, but a passive waveguide can't really set power and it doesn't address time or start, so the benefit is partial.

title: Flip Sand Timer
new_elements: i27_sand_timer_component (Replace electronic timer with a built-in one-minute sand timer.); i27_flip_to_heat_function (Flipping it triggers a fixed heating interval.)
rationale: A familiar kitchen timer gesture makes use instantly understandable.
judge_comment: A familiar flip gesture is very intuitive, though a fixed one-minute interval limits flexibility and it needs a mechanical-to-electrical trigger.

title: Gravity Start Knob
new_elements: i28_gravity_start_knob_component (Replace buttons with a knob that starts cooking when upright.); i28_upright_to_heat_function (Uses a gravity switch to start the appliance.)
rationale: Positioning a part is simpler than reading controls.
judge_comment: A gravity switch is cheap and feasible, but 'upright to start' is not obviously discoverable and does not set the time.

title: Self Tuning Magnetron Power
new_elements: i29_magnetron_current_auto_power_component (Replace power knob with current-sensing power regulation.); i29_self_tuning_power_function (Adjusts microwave output automatically based on load.)
rationale: The appliance decides power, removing another user learning task.
judge_comment: Automatic load-based power removes a decision, but current sensing alone is a weak proxy for food state and it leaves the other controls in place.

title: Door Only Control
new_elements: i30_door_only_control_component (Replace all separate controls with door interlock logic.); i30_door_only_cook_function (Close to start, open to pause, and fully open to stop.)
rationale: The door itself becomes the entire interface, reducing learning to one action.
judge_comment: Using the door as the only interface leaves almost nothing to learn and is easy to build from existing interlocks, though cook duration still needs a default or sensing.

title: Glow in Dark Interior
new_elements: i31_glow_dark_coating_component (Replace the lamp with a non-toxic glow coating inside the cavity.); i31_no_interior_lamp_function (Provides basic visibility without electrical lighting.)
rationale: Users need no switch or light check; visibility is passive.
judge_comment: Passive glow coating barely helps operation and gives weak visibility, and it doesn't address the learning curve.

title: Steam Whistle Done
new_elements: i32_steam_whistle_component (Replace bell with a steam-driven whistle.); i32_whistle_done_function (Signals completion when steam pressure activates the whistle.)
rationale: A classic kettle sound is immediately understandable as ready.
judge_comment: A whistle is an intuitive done signal, but steam pressure in a microwave cavity is unreliable and doesn't simplify operation.

title: Done When Steam
new_elements: i33_pressure_sensor_done_component (Replace manual timer with a cavity pressure sensor.); i33_done_when_steam_function (Stops heating when steam release indicates readiness.)
rationale: No time setting is needed because readiness is detected automatically.
judge_comment: Auto-detecting doneness removes time setting, which serves the need well, though a pressure sensor in a vented cavity is hard; humidity sensors already exist.

title: Big Red Start
new_elements: i34_big_red_start_button_component (Replace small controls with one oversized red button.); i34_press_to_heat_function (Pressing the big red button starts cooking.)
rationale: A large obvious control eliminates discovery and decision complexity.
judge_comment: A single oversized start button is easy to use and very feasible, but fairly obvious and the heating duration is unspecified.

title: Preset Cup Slot
new_elements: i35_preset_cup_slot_component (Replace cavity flexibility with a shaped slot that accepts one standard cup.); i35_cup_slot_heat_function (Inserting the cup starts a preset heating time.)
rationale: Physical compatibility with one cup removes all choices.
judge_comment: A shaped cup slot that auto-starts a preset removes all decisions, but it is highly limited in what it can heat.

title: Foot Pedal Start
new_elements: i36_foot_pedal_component (Replace hand controls with a foot pedal linked to a mechanical switch.); i36_step_to_heat_function (Stepping starts a fixed heating cycle.)
rationale: One foot action can start cooking even while hands are full.
judge_comment: Hands-free start is intuitive, but a fixed cycle limits cooking variety and the pedal only replaces the start button rather than the whole learning curve.

title: Done by Aroma
new_elements: i37_smell_sensor_done_component (Replace timer settings with a gas sensor tuned to common cooked-food aromas.); i37_done_when_aroma_function (Stops heating when the expected aroma appears.)
rationale: Users need not know time or power; the appliance detects readiness.
judge_comment: Auto-detecting doneness removes all settings, but aroma sensing is unreliable across foods and risks under- or overheating.

title: On Off Only
new_elements: i38_on_off_binary_switch_component (Replace all microwave settings with one on/off toggle.); i38_binary_heat_function (Turns heating on or off with no other options.)
rationale: Binary switching is the simplest possible control language.
judge_comment: Extremely simple and buildable, but not very radical and users must still judge time themselves.

title: Sticker Shows Ready
new_elements: i39_temp_sticker_component (Replace a display with a temperature-reactive sticker on the door.); i39_visible_done_function (Changes color to signal when contents are hot.)
rationale: One glance at a familiar color change replaces digital readouts.
judge_comment: Color-change sticker is a familiar cue, but door surface temperature poorly reflects food temperature, and it doesn't control operation.

title: Single Lever
new_elements: i40_single_lever_component (Replace knob plus button with one lever that has start and stop detents.); i40_one_lever_function (Moves from off to one preset heating mode.)
rationale: One lever position makes operation as simple as flipping a switch.
judge_comment: A single lever with a preset mode is simple and practical, but it is an incremental control swap.

title: Auto Temp Probe Stop
new_elements: i41_auto_temp_probe_component (Replace manual timing with a built-in temperature probe in the tray.); i41_stop_when_hot_function (Ends heating when a safe target temperature is reached.)
rationale: The user only starts cooking; the appliance decides completion.
judge_comment: Probe-based auto-stop removes timing decisions entirely, though a tray-embedded probe in a microwave is technically tricky and existing sensor cooking is similar.

title: Door Handle Twist Timer
new_elements: i42_door_handle_twist_component (Replace the timer knob by linking a door handle twist to a fixed time cam.); i42_twist_one_minute_function (Twisting the handle starts one minute of heating.)
rationale: One familiar twisting motion replaces separate timer settings.
judge_comment: A twist-to-start one-minute cam is simple and mechanical, though the fixed duration limits flexibility.

title: Recipe Icons Panel
new_elements: i43_recipe_icons_component (Replace numbers with a small set of food icons on a rotary panel.); i43_pick_food_icon_function (Selects a preset heating program based on picture match.)
rationale: Picture selection is easier than interpreting minutes and power levels.
judge_comment: Icon-based presets are intuitive and easy to build, but are fairly common and not radical.

title: Rocking Plate
new_elements: i44_rocking_plate_component (Replace turntable rotation with a gentle rocking tray.); i44_rock_even_heat_function (Improves heat spread without motor control.)
rationale: Simpler mechanical motion reduces parts and control complexity.
judge_comment: Rocking tray is novel but barely addresses ease of operation, and its heating benefit is doubtful.

title: Closed Lid Heat
new_elements: i45_lid_trigger_component (Replace appliance controls with a container lid switch.); i45_closed_lid_heat_function (Closing the container lid starts a fixed microwave cycle.)
rationale: The normal food preparation action becomes the cooking command.
judge_comment: Using a container lid closure as the start command is radical and zero-learning, but needs a safe lid-sensing mechanism and a wireless or mechanical link to the oven.

title: Shake to Heat
new_elements: i46_shake_sensor_component (Replace buttons with an accelerometer that triggers heating after a shake.); i46_shake_to_heat_function (Shaking the appliance starts a preset time.)
rationale: A physical shake is playful and needs no labels or menus.
judge_comment: Shaking a microwave is playful and label-free, but a preset time doesn't suit varied foods and shaking a heavy appliance is awkward and possibly unsafe.

title: External Timer Link
new_elements: i47_kitchen_timer_link_component (Replace microwave timer with a link to a common mechanical kitchen timer.); i47_external_timer_cook_function (The old timer’s end signal stops heating.)
rationale: Users can use an object they already understand instead of new microwave controls.
judge_comment: It uses a familiar object, but it adds a second device and the link mechanism is vague, so the interface isn't actually simpler.

title: Size Sets Power
new_elements: i48_auto_power_size_component (Replace power knob with a cavity volume sensor.); i48_size_to_power_function (Selects a default output based on item size.)
rationale: The appliance handles power level automatically, removing user decisions.
judge_comment: It removes the power decision, but volume is a poor proxy for the right power, and time still has to be set.

title: Plug and Wait
new_elements: i49_plug_and_wait_component (Replace controls with a fixed two-minute start after plugging in.); i49_plug_to_heat_function (Power connection alone begins cooking.)
rationale: The only required user action is connecting power, which is already familiar.
judge_comment: It is technically simple and radical, but heating on power-up with a fixed time is unsafe and impractical, and gives no control.

title: Drop Food to Start
new_elements: i50_drop_food_to_heat_function_component (Replace buttons with a tray sensor that detects food insertion.); i50_drop_food_to_heat_function (Putting the correct container on the tray starts heating.)
rationale: Loading food becomes the complete control interface with no extra learning step.
judge_comment: Placing the food as the only interaction is intuitive, but detecting the correct container and choosing the cook time are unclear, and accidental starts are a risk.

title: 1 Single Dial Cook
new_elements: Single Dial Cook (One dial sets mode and starts by pressing.); One-action cook selection (Rotates or pushes to set time and power together.)
rationale: Replaces two knobs with one obvious action, removing choice paralysis for elderly or novice users.
judge_comment: Single dial is simple and plausible, but many microwaves already use dials, so it is not radical.

title: 2 Auto-Start Button
new_elements: One Big Start Button (Large button starts a safe default heating cycle.); Default auto timing (Applies standard time and power without user settings.)
rationale: Turns operation into a single press with no dial interpretation.
judge_comment: One-press start is extremely simple, though a fixed default may not suit all foods and it is hardly a wild idea.

title: 3 Weight-Adjusted Cook
new_elements: Load Cell Start Pad (Cavity floor senses food weight when starting.); Weight-based cook time (Derives duration from mass instead of user entry.)
rationale: Eliminates guessing time for different portions, making heating self-explanatory.
judge_comment: A load cell that sets time from weight removes the need to enter anything, but weight alone is a weak predictor of heating needs and the sensor adds cost.

title: 4 Steam-Stop Cook
new_elements: Humidity Cap (Simple vent cap detects steam rise during heating.); Done-at-steam stop (Ends heating when target moisture condition is reached.)
rationale: Removes manual timing by stopping when the food shows readiness.
judge_comment: Steam-sensing auto-stop already exists in sensor-cook models, but it does remove timing decisions.

title: 5 Food Barcode Defaults
new_elements: Barcode Read Door (Door window briefly scans a food label to infer defaults.); Scan food preset (Sets time and power from package information.)
rationale: Replaces manual controls with one familiar action: scanning or showing the food.
judge_comment: Scanning barcodes is novel, but it depends on label data and database coverage, and many foods have no package; it also adds a scanning step.

title: 6 Color-Preset Dial
new_elements: Preset Color Wheel (Dial positions are color-coded for common foods.); Color preset cooking (Color alone implies time and power.)
rationale: Uses intuitive color association instead of numerical settings.
judge_comment: Color-coded food presets are intuitive and easy to build, but similar to existing preset buttons and not radical.

title: 7 Squeeze Door Start
new_elements: Squeeze Door Start (Squeezing the door edge opens the latch and starts heating.); Grip-to-start open (Combines access and start into one natural grip.)
rationale: Turns the door interaction into the operation itself, eliminating separate start controls.
judge_comment: Merging open and start into one grip is elegant, though it raises safety interlock concerns and risks accidental starts.

title: 8 Transparent Faraday Door
new_elements: Clear Faraday Door Film (Solid transparent conductive film blocks microwaves without holes.); See-through safe cavity (Provides clear viewing while satisfying shielding.)
rationale: Removes confusing perforated mesh and internal light cues, making the cavity naturally understandable.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive film shields microwaves in principle, but it has little effect on operational simplicity and is hard to make at microwave-grade shielding.

title: 9 Gravity Auto Door
new_elements: Gravity Latch Door (Door falls open when latch is lightly released.); Push-to-open gravity latch (Gravity and a light push replace a dedicated release button.)
rationale: Users discover opening by simply pushing, without learning a latch mechanism.
judge_comment: A gravity-drop door is simple and discoverable, but it only covers opening and may be a safety or damage risk.

title: 10 Pull-Cord Timer
new_elements: Pull Cord Start (Cord pull cycles coarse timers like a lamp.); Pull-to-set time (Each pull adds a preset duration.)
rationale: Reuses familiar household behavior, reducing learning compared with a clock dial.
judge_comment: A pull cord that adds preset durations is familiar and cheap, but it is awkward and imprecise for cooking.

title: 11 Door Angle Power
new_elements: Angled Door Sensor (Door opening angle selects a rough power mode.); Open-angle power setting (A partially open door indicates lower heat.)
rationale: Replaces an abstract knob with a visible physical position that maps to gentle or full heating.
judge_comment: Door angle as a power selector is novel and intuitive in concept, but the door must stay ajar, which defeats the interlock safety and makes it impractical.

title: 12 Push-Time Repeats
new_elements: Repeated Push Timer (Big pad adds time each time it is pressed.); Push adds time (No rotation or number entry is required.)
rationale: Makes time setting a simple repeatable physical action.
judge_comment: Add-time-per-press is already common (e.g., the +30 sec button), but it is very easy to use and easy to build.

title: 13 Single Big Red Start
new_elements: Big Red Start (Large tactile button starts safe full-cycle defaults.); One press full-power default (Selects a universal short heat without choices.)
rationale: The affordance is unmistakable: press the large button.
judge_comment: A single start button is extremely simple, but a fixed default can't suit different foods and the idea is obvious.

title: 14 No-Lamp Transparent Cavity
new_elements: Clear Faraday Cavity (Cavity panels use solid microwave-safe transparent shielding.); Passive see-through cavity (Visibility is achieved without lamps or holes.)
rationale: Eliminates need to interpret lighted windows or buttons.
judge_comment: A transparent shielding cavity is hard to achieve and only loosely relates to ease of operation, since existing mesh doors already give visibility.

title: 15 Thermochromic Finish Door
new_elements: Thermochromic Door Ring (Door ring changes color when heating target is reached.); Color-done indicator (Visual completion replaces reading a timer.)
rationale: Users learn only that color change means done.
judge_comment: A color-change completion cue is intuitive, but a door ring can't sense the food's temperature and heating the ring itself is a questionable proxy.

title: 16 Tactile Time Buttons
new_elements: Three Big Time Buttons (Only 1, 5, and 10 minute press controls remain.); 1/5/10 min press (Coarse preset timing without a clock dial.)
rationale: Reduces cognitive load to three obvious choices.
judge_comment: Three big buttons are very easy to understand and simple to build, but the idea is incremental and coarse timing limits what users can cook.

title: 17 Wave-to-Start
new_elements: Wave Sensor Lid (Simple infrared gesture over the lid starts default heating.); Gesture start (No button or knob is touched.)
rationale: Turns start into one intuitive non-contact motion.
judge_comment: Wave-to-start is simple to use but is not a cheaper substitute, and accidental triggering and a lack of safety confirmation are concerns.

title: 18 Auto-Power by Time
