new_elements: Fiber-Optic Glow Panel (Ambient glow lights the cavity without a bulb.); passive cavity visibility (Soft glow shows interior without a switch.); incandescent lamp (Legacy lighting part to replace.)
rationale: It avoids a lamp control or maintenance step while preserving visibility.
judge_comment: Fiber-optic lighting swaps a bulb, but it barely affects operation simplicity.

title: 04 Handle-Dial Start
new_elements: Rotating Start Handle (The door handle is the timer and start control.); twist-to-start (Turning the handle starts a proportional run.); timer knob (Legacy separate knob to replace.)
rationale: It folds starting and timing into one familiar grip action.
judge_comment: Merging the handle and timer into a twist-to-start action is intuitive and novel, with moderate engineering challenges for safety and the door.

title: 05 QR Auto-Run
new_elements: QR Auto-Run Scanner (A scanner reads a package code to choose settings.); scan-to-cook (Scanning automatically sets time and power.); mode buttons (Legacy selection buttons to replace.)
rationale: Users learn nothing beyond a package code already provided.
judge_comment: Scanning a package code automates settings, but it depends on packaging and codes, and many foods lack them, which limits it as a no-learning solution.

title: 06 Emoji Path
new_elements: Emoji Guidance Screen (Pictures replace words and symbols.); emoji mode path (Icons show the next step without text.); text panel (Legacy written instructions to replace.)
rationale: It eliminates reading and menu interpretation.
judge_comment: Icon-based guidance lowers the reading burden, but it is still a menu-driven screen and not very radical.

title: 07 Door-Close Auto
new_elements: Door-Close Start Latch (Closing the door begins a default run.); close-to-start (Door closure triggers cooking.); start button (Legacy manual start control to replace.)
rationale: The most natural action already starts the appliance.
judge_comment: Closing the door to start is very intuitive, but a default run risks accidental or unsafe starts, such as running empty.

title: 08 Weight Ring
new_elements: Weight-Sensing Ring (A base ring detects plate mass.); weight-aware default (Mass sets an appropriate cooking intensity.); power knob (Legacy manual power selection to replace.)
rationale: It chooses power from the load instead of from a learning step.
judge_comment: Weight sensing sets power automatically, but mass alone poorly indicates food type or the time needed.

title: 09 Color Time Bar
new_elements: Color Time Bar (A single bar changes color as time passes.); color countdown (Color alone communicates remaining time.); digital display (Legacy numeric display to replace.)
rationale: It replaces numbers with an instantly readable visual cue.
judge_comment: A color bar is easy to read, but it only shows progress and does not simplify setting the time.

title: 10 Aroma Stop
new_elements: Aroma Stop Sensor (A cavity sensor detects ready food aromas.); scent completion (Cooking stops when expected aroma appears.); timer knob (Legacy time-setting control to replace.)
rationale: It removes time guessing and makes completion automatic.
judge_comment: Stopping on aroma would remove all settings and is a bold idea, but reliable scent sensing across foods is hard.

title: 11 Silent Pulse Pad
new_elements: Silent Pulse Pad (A soft pulse surface signals completion.); silent pulse completion (Gentle vibration replaces a loud bell.); bell (Legacy audible alert to replace.)
rationale: It signals completion without surprising users or needing setup.
judge_comment: A vibration pad replacing the bell is feasible, but it barely helps operation, and the microwave is not a device people hold, so the alert is easy to miss.

title: 12 Auto-Power Modulator
new_elements: Auto-Power Modulator (Electronics adjust power from cavity feedback.); adaptive wattage (Power changes automatically during cooking.); 5-step power knob (Legacy manual power selector to replace.)
rationale: It removes power-setting decisions entirely.
judge_comment: Automatic power adjustment removes a real decision and directly serves zero-learning-curve use, though cavity feedback sensing is hard to do well and similar sensor-cooking features already exist.

title: 13 Turntableless Antenna
new_elements: Stirring Antenna (A rotating waveguide stirs energy without moving food.); static-plate cooking (Food remains in place while energy is steered.); glass turntable (Legacy rotating plate mechanism to replace.)
rationale: It eliminates alignment and plate-rotation steps.
judge_comment: Stirrer-based turntable-free microwaves already exist and work, so it is feasible and concrete, but it only loosely helps ease of use by removing plate alignment.

title: 14 Bag Support Clip
new_elements: Bag Support Clip (A simple clip holds microwave bags upright.); bag-only cooking (Bags cook without plate rotation.); glass turntable (Legacy rotating support to replace.)
rationale: It makes one common task obvious without moving parts.
judge_comment: A clip is simple and cheap, but it serves a narrow task and does not remove the need to learn the controls.

title: 15 Hydrophobic Skin
new_elements: Hydrophobic Inner Skin (A coated cavity resists sticking and splatter.); no-manual wipe (Surface finish reduces cleaning effort.); manual wiping (Labor task previously required.)
rationale: It lowers maintenance so the product feels simpler over time.
judge_comment: Easy-clean coatings are practical and exist already, but they address maintenance rather than operating simplicity.

title: 16 Mug-Shape Shelf
new_elements: Mug-Shape Shelf (A shelf guide accepts mugs only.); mug default (Placing a mug triggers a simple drink heat.); button modes (Legacy mode selection to replace.)
rationale: Physical form tells the user what the default does.
judge_comment: A mug-shaped shelf that auto-selects a drink heat removes mode choice and signals the default through its form, though it limits other uses.

title: 17 Long-Press Stop Ring
new_elements: Long-Press Stop Ring (Holding the start area stops the run.); press-to-halt (One sustained touch pauses cooking.); stop button (Legacy separate stop control to replace.)
rationale: It keeps one control surface and one intuitive action.
judge_comment: Hold-to-stop on the start area is simple and feasible, but it is a modest change and may be less discoverable than a dedicated stop button.

title: 18 Foot-Pedal Door
new_elements: Foot-Pedal Door Lever (A pedal opens the door without hands.); hands-free open (Foot contact releases the door.); door push-release (Legacy hand-button release to replace.)
rationale: It avoids searching for a door release when hands are busy.
judge_comment: A foot pedal helps when hands are full, but it adds a new thing to learn and has little to do with operating the controls.

title: 19 Phosphor Interior
new_elements: Phosphor Glow Interior (A phosphor lining emits gentle light after activation.); after-dark visibility (Interior remains visible without a lamp.); incandescent lamp (Legacy bulb to replace.)
rationale: It provides visibility without controls or replacement effort.
judge_comment: A phosphor lining replaces the lamp, but it has little effect on operation, and phosphor in a microwave cavity is questionable.

title: 20 Squeeze Handle
new_elements: Squeeze Start Handle (Squeezing the handle starts a default cycle.); squeeze-to-go (Grip pressure launches cooking.); start button (Legacy push button to replace.)
rationale: It turns start into a natural grab gesture.
judge_comment: Squeezing the handle to start is intuitive and replaces the start button with a natural gesture, though accidental starts and the empty-run risk need handling.

title: 21 Bell-Countdown
new_elements: Bell-Countdown Timer (A simple bell sequence signals remaining time.); listen-to-timer (Sound patterns communicate progress.); digital display (Legacy numeric display to replace.)
rationale: It removes reading and provides one obvious audio state.
judge_comment: Audio countdown is easy to build and removes reading, but microwaves already beep and it does not address how to set time or power.

title: 22 Ambient Light Clock
new_elements: Ambient Light Clock (A sensor ties countdown brightness to room light.); daylight countdown (Visible intensity shows remaining energy.); clockwork timer (Legacy mechanical timer to replace.)
rationale: It replaces dial numbers with a passive visible signal.
judge_comment: Tying countdown brightness to room light is odd and ambiguous, so it may add confusion rather than reduce the learning curve.

title: 23 Wave-Guide Panel
new_elements: Wave-Guide No-Button Panel (A smooth panel routes waves without visible controls.); no-button cooking (The panel hides controls and defaults to one mode.); button panel (Legacy control panel to replace.)
rationale: It removes option anxiety by presenting only a calm surface.
judge_comment: A single-mode, no-button surface is very simple, but it sacrifices control and does not say how the amount of heating is determined.

title: 24 Thermal Food Film
new_elements: Thermal Food Film (A disposable heat film guides energy around food.); film heat guide (The film reduces uneven results without user settings.); food plate (Legacy plate placement task to replace.)
rationale: It gives a simple pre-set physical helper instead of user decisions.
judge_comment: A disposable heat film adds a consumable and a step, and thermal guiding of microwave energy is questionable, so it works against simplicity.

title: 25 Plateless Ceramic Base
new_elements: Plateless Ceramic Base (A stationary ceramic base replaces the rotating plate.); drop-and-start (Food can be placed anywhere without alignment.); glass turntable (Legacy rotating mechanism to replace.)
rationale: It removes the need to know how to position the plate.
judge_comment: A stationary base removes the plate-positioning concern and is plausible, though even heating without rotation needs a stirrer or similar, and it is only a partial answer to ease of use.

title: 26 Smart Mug Sensor
new_elements: Smart Mug Sensor (A base sensor detects a ceramic mug.); mug-aware time (Time adjusts to mug mass and material.); manual time setting (User guessing replaced by sensing.)
rationale: It hides time selection behind an invisible default.
judge_comment: Sensing the mug to set the time removes the time-selection step, but mass alone cannot tell what food is inside, so results would be unreliable.

title: 27 Dialless Ring
new_elements: Dialless Ring (A ring with no numbers sets cooking by gesture.); single-ring time (One ring controls all timing.); timer and power knobs (Legacy separate dials to replace.)
rationale: It condenses many controls into one familiar circular motion.
judge_comment: One ring replacing the dials is simple in principle, but gesture control with no numbers may add its own learning curve.

title: 28 Touch-Anywhere Glow
new_elements: Touch-Anywhere Glow (The exterior glows at the place to press.); any-surface start (A glowing area starts a default cycle.); physical buttons (Legacy labeled buttons to replace.)
rationale: It tells users where to act without labels or legends.
judge_comment: A glowing press-here area guides users, but a touch-anywhere start risks accidental activation and the mechanism is vague.

title: 29 Push-Start Handle
new_elements: Push-Start Handle (Pushing the door handle starts a simple cycle.); push-to-run (Handle pressure launches cooking.); start button (Legacy start control to replace.)
rationale: It uses the natural door-handling action as the command.
judge_comment: Pushing the handle to start is intuitive and cheap, but it may start the unit unintentionally or without the door properly closed.

title: 30 Knobless Door Magnet
new_elements: Knobless Door Magnet (Magnetic latch releases when pulled.); knobless door (Door opens by simple pulling.); door push-release (Legacy release button to replace.)
rationale: It removes the step of finding and pressing a release.
judge_comment: A magnetic pull-open door is simple and feasible, though it is an incremental change that does little for operating the cooking controls.

title: 31 Auto-Humble Finish
new_elements: Auto-Humble Finish (A cycle eases power down as food nears ready.); auto low-power finish (The appliance avoids overheating without user choice.); defrost mode (Legacy special mode to replace.)
rationale: It hides a tricky mode inside an automatic safe default.
judge_comment: Automatic power taper-off is plausible and removes the need to choose a mode, but it is vague and hardly radical.

title: 32 Green Start Dot
new_elements: Green Start Dot (One glowing green dot is the only control.); green-to-go (Pressing green starts a default run.); multiple buttons (Legacy button clutter to replace.)
rationale: It uses a universal color cue instead of reading.
judge_comment: A single green start control is about as zero-learning as a microwave gets and is easy to build, though not very novel.

title: 33 Vibration Surface
new_elements: Vibration Timer Surface (The shell pulses gently during countdown.); vibe countdown (Vibration communicates time without a bell.); bell (Legacy audible alert to replace.)
rationale: It provides a calm completion signal that requires no interpretation.
judge_comment: Vibration as a countdown cue is novel but does little for operation simplicity, and a vibrating shell near a microwave is awkward and unreliable.

title: 34 Pre-Set Shelf
new_elements: Pre-Set Food Shelf (Physical shelves correspond to common food defaults.); shelf-based defaults (Shelf location chooses a safe cycle.); mode selector (Legacy mode control to replace.)
rationale: It substitutes menu choice with spatial placement.
judge_comment: Choosing the cycle by shelf position is an intuitive spatial idea, but it needs food or position sensing and makes cooking mechanically complex.

title: 35 Heat-Glow Interior
new_elements: Heat-Glow Interior (Thermal paint glows softly with cavity temperature.); thermal visibility (Heat level is visible without a lamp.); incandescent lamp (Legacy bulb to replace.)
rationale: It replaces lighting with a natural read of heat activity.
judge_comment: Thermal paint glow is eye-catching, but it offers weak operational simplicity, and cavity temperature would not show food readiness while the light is also needed.

title: 36 Wave-Stir Fan
new_elements: Wave-Stir Fan (A dielectric fan pattern mixes microwave fields.); fan-stirred even heat (Even heating occurs without plate rotation.); glass turntable (Legacy rotating plate to replace.)
rationale: It hides distribution behind motionless internal field stirring.
judge_comment: A field-stirring fan replaces the turntable, but it does little for operation simplicity and a dielectric fan pattern is vague; metal stirrers already exist.

title: 37 Thermal Stop Sensor
new_elements: Thermal Stop Sensor (A safe surface sensor detects ready temperature.); heat-based stop (Cooking ends when target heat is reached.); timer knob (Legacy time-setting control to replace.)
rationale: It removes the need to know time settings.
judge_comment: Stopping at target temperature removes the need to know cook times and fits the need well, though sensing food temperature on a surface is hard to do reliably.

title: 38 Magnetic Ring Start
new_elements: Magnetic Ring Start (A magnetic ring on the handle starts a default run.); magnetic ring start (Ring contact triggers cooking.); timer and power knobs (Legacy manual controls to replace.)
rationale: It turns start into a playful physical connection.
judge_comment: A magnetic one-touch start is simple and feasible, but the default run may suit few foods and it needs safety interlocks.

title: 39 Color-Shift Door
new_elements: Color-Shift Door (The door tint changes with cooking state.); color-shift done (A door color change signals completion.); bell and display (Legacy alert parts to replace.)
rationale: It provides completion information from a distance without controls.
judge_comment: A color-changing door is a distinctive way to show state, but it only helps with completion feedback, not operation, and it is not a real control substitute.

title: 40 One-Mode Board
new_elements: One-Mode Board (A simple board accepts only a default cycle.); one-mode cooking (All input reduces to one mode.); mode selector (Legacy selection control to replace.)
rationale: It eliminates learning by offering only one safe path.
judge_comment: A single-mode device has no learning curve and is easy to build, but it is limited in function and not very radical.

title: 41 Voiceless Tags
new_elements: Voiceless Food Tags (RFID tags on food indicate the simple cycle.); tag-to-cook (Tag detection sets defaults without user input.); dials and buttons (Legacy manual interface to replace.)
rationale: It replaces control with passive recognition.
judge_comment: RFID food tags remove all input, but they require tagged packaging across the food supply, which limits real-world use; the idea is clear and the mechanism is plausible.

title: 42 Scent Shelf
new_elements: Scent Shelf (A shelf releases a familiar cue when a default is ready.); scent shelf defaults (Smell guides the user through the simple mode.); button modes (Legacy selection controls to replace.)
rationale: It uses a natural signal to explain a default operation.
judge_comment: Scent as a signal is unusual, but it is ambiguous, hard to control, and doesn't clearly reduce operating steps.

title: 43 Glow Ring Timer
new_elements: Glow Ring Timer (A ring shrinks its light to show time.); glow ring countdown (Ring light replaces numbers and bell.); display and bell (Legacy output parts to replace.)
rationale: It shows progress through an easy-to-read ring.
judge_comment: A shrinking light ring is simple, intuitive, and easy to build, although similar timer displays already exist.

title: 44 One-Strip Door
new_elements: One-Strip Door (A fabric or silicone strip replaces a mechanical latch.); strip-open door (Pulling the strip opens the door simply.); door push-release (Legacy button latch to replace.)
rationale: It makes opening an obvious pull rather than a hidden button.
judge_comment: A pull strip makes door opening obvious, but a safe seal and a reliable interlock are hard to achieve with fabric.

title: 45 Shape-Aware Door
new_elements: Shape-Aware Door (Door indentations fit common food shapes.); shape-aware defaults (Shape guides the user to the correct default.); mode buttons (Legacy menu controls to replace.)
rationale: It uses physical form to avoid menu selection.
judge_comment: Shape-matched indentations are a creative way to pick a default, but food varies too much and the mapping is unreliable.

title: 46 Color Plate
new_elements: Color Plate (A colored plate identifies a safe default.); color-coded defaults (Plate color matches the simplest cycle.); dial presets (Legacy preset choice to replace.)
rationale: It transfers operation learning into a matching physical color.
judge_comment: A colored plate that matches a default cycle is easy to build but vague, and it still leaves the user to decode colors, so it only partly removes the learning curve.

title: 47 Time-By-Wave
new_elements: Time-By-Wave Antenna (Wave strength shapes the cooking envelope.); wave-timed cooking (The energy pattern handles timing.); timer knob (Legacy time control to replace.)
rationale: It hides time logic inside field behavior.
judge_comment: Having the field pattern handle timing would remove the timer, but the mechanism is implausible and underspecified, since a microwave cannot sense doneness from antenna strength alone.

title: 48 Auto-Stop Plate
new_elements: Auto-Stop Plate (A passive plate changes state when food is done.); plate-based completion (The plate signals completion without electronics.); timer and bell (Legacy controls and alerts to replace.)
rationale: It moves completion feedback to the food itself.
judge_comment: A passive plate that changes state at doneness would give intuitive feedback, but a reliable thermochromic or mechanical indicator across different foods is hard, and it does not stop the heating.

title: 49 Hand-Free Door Glow
new_elements: Hand-Free Door Glow (A glow marks the hand-free door action.); glow-guided open (The glowing area shows where to open.); door button and lamp (Legacy release and lighting to replace.)
rationale: It tells users what to do without labels or buttons.
judge_comment: A glow showing where to open the door is simple and feasible but addresses only a minor part of operation, and the hand-free mechanism is unclear.

title: 50 One-Slide Dial
new_elements: One-Slide Dial (A single sliding ring starts and times.); slide-to-cook (One slide replaces all setup.); timer and power knobs (Legacy dual controls to replace.)
rationale: It condenses configuration into one obvious slide.
judge_comment: A single sliding ring that starts and sets time is intuitive, mechanically plausible and directly cuts the controls, though it is a modest departure from a dial.

title: 1 One-Pull Timer Ring
new_elements: One-pull timer ring (Break-off colored pull tabs replace the mechanical timer knob with fixed 1-, 3-, and 10-minute selections.)
rationale: The user pulls one visible tab and needs no numbers, dials, or explanation.
judge_comment: Break-off tabs give fixed times with no learning, but they are single-use, which makes them impractical, and pulling a tab must still trigger the timer.

title: 2 Color-Tab Preset Strip
new_elements: Color-tab preset strip (A strip of color-coded pull tabs replaces both time and power knobs with one-touch presets.)
rationale: One colored tab selects a common cooking condition, collapsing two knobs into zero knobs.
judge_comment: Color presets remove the need to choose time and power, but disposable pull tabs are wasteful and hard to reset.

title: 3 Squeeze-To-Go Door Handle
new_elements: Squeeze-to-go door handle (A squeezable door handle opens the door and starts a short default cycle, replacing the separate push button.)
rationale: One intuitive hand motion accesses food and starts cooking without button learning.
judge_comment: A handle that opens the door and starts a cycle is intuitive but risks accidental starts and conflicts with safety interlocks, since opening should stop heating.

title: 4 Big Single Button
new_elements: Big single-button controller (One oversized tactile button starts, pauses, and stops a fixed default heating program, replacing knobs and buttons.)
rationale: The whole operation reduces to pressing the biggest object on the machine.
judge_comment: A single start button is highly usable and easy to build, but it is a familiar idea, and a fixed program limits what it can cook.

title: 5 Wax-Duration Timer Knob
new_elements: Wax-duration actuator (A wax pellet melts at a predictable rate to drive a mechanical stop after a chosen heat level.); Wax thermal timer knob (A knob filled with phase-change material replaces the clockwork timer with a self-ending thermal mechanism.)
rationale: The user turns a knob less like a clock and more like a simple physical fuse that ends itself.
judge_comment: A wax-based thermal timer is wild and concrete, but its accuracy, repeatability and reset are doubtful, and a knob is not clearly simpler to use.

title: 6 Gravity Sand Timer Bulb
new_elements: Gravity inversion switch (An inverted bulb triggers a start and ends cooking when a fixed ball falls.); Gravity sand timer bulb (A visible hourglass-like bulb replaces the mechanical timer with a drop-weight start action.)
rationale: Turning the microwave upside-down for one second becomes the entire operation.
judge_comment: Flipping a microwave upside-down is wildly impractical and unsafe (heavy appliance, food spills), though the one-action concept is memorable.

title: 7 Door-Latch Power Cam
new_elements: Door-latch power cam (A cam behind the door latch selects low, medium, or full power according to how firmly the door is closed.)
rationale: Closing the door sets the heat level, so the power knob disappears completely.
judge_comment: Door-closing force setting power is mechanically plausible but unintuitive and unreliable, so it adds a hidden learning curve.

title: 8 Weight-Only Power Plate
new_elements: Weight-select power plate (A spring-loaded turntable base chooses one of three fixed power levels from the weight of the food container.)
rationale: The user simply puts the plate on the microwave; weight decides the cooking energy.
judge_comment: Weight-based power selection is feasible with load cells, but weight poorly correlates with the needed heat and there is no time control.

title: 9 Transparent Full Casing
new_elements: Transparent Faraday glass (A visible-light-transparent conductive mesh ceramic glass blocks microwaves without a perforated door window.); Fully transparent microwave casing (The entire cooking chamber becomes see-through, removing the dark interior and lamp.)
rationale: Seeing through the whole body makes the appliance feel like a visible glass box rather than a dark appliance with controls.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive-glass chamber is interesting, but it does little for operational simplicity and has shielding and heat challenges.

title: 10 Webcam Viewing Door
new_elements: Webcam door panel (A low-cost camera embedded in the door transmits an exterior view of the food to a phone or display.); View cavity without lamp (Provides internal food visibility electronically rather than through a perforated window and incandescent bulb.)
rationale: The user sees the food clearly without remembering dark window apertures or checking through holes.
judge_comment: A door camera is feasible but adds phone/display complexity and doesn't address simple operation.

title: 11 Phosphorescent Glow Cavity
new_elements: Phosphorescent cavity liner (A safe glow-capture coating stores ambient light and illuminates the cavity after the door closes, replacing the bulb.); Visible interior without bulb (Makes the inside of the microwave visible without electrical lighting components.)
rationale: The interior lights up passively, so the user has no bulb-related mystery to understand.
judge_comment: Phosphorescent glow is a clever bulb substitute, but it barely affects operation learning and would be dim and fade between uses.

title: 12 No-Door Cooking Envelope Slot
new_elements: Waveguide envelope slot (A short RF-shielded drawer accepts sealed cooking pouches, replacing the entire hinged door and release button.)
rationale: Food is simply slid in like an envelope, eliminating the door as a learned interface.
judge_comment: A slot for sealed pouches is radical and simple in concept, but it limits cookware, and RF leakage and sealing are difficult.

title: 13 Magnetic Pull Door Latch
new_elements: Magnetic pull door latch (A permanent magnet latch releases with a gentle outward pull instead of a small push button.)
rationale: Pulling feels natural to every hand shape, unlike pressing a tiny button.
judge_comment: A magnetic pull latch is practical and intuitive, but it is an incremental change that only touches door opening.

title: 14 Living-Hinge Door
new_elements: Living-hinge door (A single molded piece with integral flex hinges replaces stamped separate door hinges.)
rationale: A one-piece door removes rattly mechanics and visible hinge learning.
judge_comment: A living-hinge door is a manufacturing simplification with little effect on user learning, and it is questionable for heat and shielding durability.

title: 15 Slide-Top Faraday Door
new_elements: Slide-top Faraday door (A sliding microwave-shielded top cover opens with one hand instead of a hinged front door.)
rationale: Sliding a panel up is a simpler mental model than understanding a hinged appliance door.
judge_comment: A slide-top shielded cover is a plausible and fairly intuitive alternative, though a top-opening design is awkward for spills and for access to food.

title: 16 Auto-Run Door Interlock
new_elements: Auto-run door interlock (Closing the door automatically starts a default one-minute cycle, eliminating the start control.)
rationale: The user only puts food in and closes the door; there is no start step to learn.
judge_comment: Closing the door starts a default cycle, which removes a step. It is simple, but it risks accidental runs, such as an empty microwave, and a fixed one-minute cycle does not fit every food.

title: 17 Pull-Chain Start/Stop
new_elements: Pull-chain start/stop (A large hanging chain starts, pauses, or stops cooking, replacing knobs and small buttons.)
rationale: Pulling a visible chain is an ancient, almost language-free appliance action.
judge_comment: A pull chain is easy to understand and cheap to build, but it is awkward in a kitchen and does not say how long to cook.

title: 18 Foot-Pedal Start
new_elements: Foot-pedal start (A low pedal beside the microwave starts and stops the default cycle, leaving hands free.)
rationale: For users with weak grip or busy hands, a simple foot press beats fiddling with controls.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is simple and keeps hands free, but it is an unusual placement and a single default cycle is limiting.

title: 19 Passive Wristband Start
new_elements: Low-energy presence sensing (A passive RFID-like wrist tag triggers the microwave when a known user approaches.); Wristband presence start (A reader ring near the door starts cooking when the user's passive wristband is detected.)
rationale: The appliance recognizes the user and starts the default action without any visible control to operate.
judge_comment: Starting on presence detection needs no user action, but it risks unintended starts and needs a wristband, which is more complicated than a button.

title: 20 Heat-Until-Done Sensor
new_elements: Closed-loop thermal stop (A simple surface temperature sensor stops heating when the food reaches a preset target.); Heat-Until-Done sensor (A rugged infrared or contact sensor replaces the user's need to choose time and power.)
rationale: The user no longer learns time or power; the microwave stops when the plate feels done.
judge_comment: Stopping at a target temperature removes the need to pick time or power, which serves the no-learning goal well, though sensing food temperature reliably inside a microwave is hard.

title: 21 Humidity Vent Stop
new_elements: Humidity vent stop (A hydrophobic membrane on the vent closes a switch when steam reaches a safe level.)
rationale: Cooking ends when steam appears, giving an obvious physical cue without timers.
judge_comment: Steam-sensing auto-stop removes any setting, but a membrane switch is unreliable for dry foods and risks overheating or underheating.

title: 22 Picture Food Selector
new_elements: Picture food selector (A molded panel of large pictures replaces knobs with image-based food choices such as soup, drink, plate, and potato.)
rationale: Images of familiar foods communicate action better than abstract power levels.
judge_comment: Pictorial food buttons are very easy to use and simple to build, but are common on existing microwaves and not radical.

title: 23 Magnetic Recipe Wheel
new_elements: Magnetic recipe wheel (A detachable magnetic wheel of simple meal presets aligns two cams for time and power.)
rationale: The wheel lets the user pick one familiar dish instead of adjusting two unrelated dials.
judge_comment: A detachable cam wheel with dish presets is a tangible mechanical substitute for dials, though it is limited in flexibility and the wheel could get lost.

title: 24 Icon-Only Rotary Dial
new_elements: Icon-only rotary dial (One large dial with pictures replaces both time and power knobs with a combined preset motion.)
rationale: One dial with pictures is easier to learn than two abstract knobs.
judge_comment: A single icon dial is intuitive and cheap, but is an incremental simplification.

title: 25 More/Less Touch Bars
new_elements: MoreLess touch bars (Two large physical bars labeled with sun or clock symbols increase or decrease the default heating condition.)
rationale: A more/less bar is a human-scale adjustment that avoids numeric learning.
judge_comment: More/less bars are simple and need no numbers, but the default heating condition is vague and the idea is only moderately novel.

title: 26 Number-of-Plates Timer
new_elements: Stack-count sensing (A stack of plates or containers in the cavity is counted by height and weight.); Number-of-plates timer (The cavity height sensor converts the number of stacked items into a default cooking time.)
rationale: The user can simply put one, two, or three plates in and let the appliance infer duration.
judge_comment: Inferring time from plate count is intuitive and zero-learning, but stack height poorly predicts the heating needed for different foods.

title: 27 Food-Color Power Sensor
new_elements: Food-color power sensor (A tiny color detector reads the dominant food hue and selects one of a few fixed power patterns.)
rationale: The user does not choose power; the appliance reads a simple visual property of the food.
judge_comment: Removes the power choice, but food color is a weak proxy for the right heating pattern and the cavity is a hostile environment for a color sensor.

title: 28 Time-Capsule Lever
new_elements: Color-melt time capsule (A sealed dye bead changes color through a fixed time window when placed in the door lever.); Time-capsule lever (A lever accepts a small colored bead that physically indicates how long to wait.)
rationale: A visible bead gives a non-numeric time cue that is easy for children and elders alike.
judge_comment: A bead that changes color over a fixed time is a quirky non-numeric cue, but it adds consumables and a fixed time fits few foods.

title: 29 Power-Line Signaling Start
new_elements: Power-line cooking signaling (A wall switch encodes simple cooking programs by short power-line pulses.); Power-line start receiver (The microwave receives one, two, or three power pulses and selects a preset program.)
rationale: The user can use a familiar wall switch instead of learning the microwave itself.
judge_comment: Wall-switch pulse coding is radical, but counting pulses is itself a learned code, and it is unsafe and unreliable to implement.

title: 30 External Smart Plug Timer
new_elements: External smart plug timer (A simple plug-in timer replaces the mechanical microwave timer and can be used with any 230 V/120 V model.)
rationale: A visible plug-in dial is already a known object, so the microwave itself can have no timer knob.
judge_comment: A plug-in dial timer is simple and feasible, but it is an obvious substitution, and cutting power to the unit is crude for microwaves with electronics.

title: 31 Fixed Full-Power Only Mode
new_elements: Fixed full-power control (The duty-cycle power knob is deleted and the magnetron runs only on its default full-power cycle.)
rationale: Removing the power knob leaves one thing to do: put food in and run.
judge_comment: Removing the power control simplifies operation and is easily built, but it is an obvious feature deletion and risks poor results with some foods.

title: 32 Static Stirrer Instead of Turntable
new_elements: Static microwave stirrer cavity (A fixed cavity with passive field stirrer replaces the glass turntable and its centering requirement.); Uniform heating without rotating plate (Provides usable even heating without making the user place the plate exactly centered.)
rationale: The user avoids the invisible rule that plate must be centered and turntable must be installed.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers already exist in microwaves, so it is feasible and removes the centering rule, but it is a modest substitution and does not directly simplify the controls.

title: 33 Power-by-Turntable Speed
new_elements: Power-by-turntable-speed (The turntable motor speed itself is the only power selector: slow, medium, fast plate rotation.)
rationale: The moving plate gives a visible clue about heat level, replacing an abstract knob.
judge_comment: Coupling turntable speed to power is novel and visible, but it makes little physical sense, since rotation speed does not change power, and it adds confusion.

title: 34 Door-Open Stop Auto-Resume
new_elements: Door-open stop auto-resume (Opening the door pauses, and closing it resumes the same default cycle without user settings.)
rationale: The physical door becomes the stop and start switch, removing control learning.
judge_comment: Using the door as the start and stop switch is intuitive and easy to build, though auto-resume has safety and overcooking questions.

title: 35 Single Time-Power Lever
new_elements: Single time-power lever (One lever moves from gentle to intense and from short to long along the same axis.)
rationale: One lever expresses intensity as a single easy-to-learn motion.
judge_comment: One lever for time and power merges two controls, which is simple, but it couples the two variables and reduces precision.

title: 36 Palm-Touch Start Plate
new_elements: Palm-touch start plate (A large flat plate near the handle starts a default cycle when touched by the palm.)
rationale: A big touch area is easier than small buttons for older or stiff hands.
judge_comment: A palm plate that starts a default cycle is simple and needs no learning, though accidental starts and an empty-run risk need handling.

title: 37 Glove-Conductive Door Button
new_elements: Glove-conductive door button (A door release coated in a fabric-friendly conductive surface can be operated by a normal kitchen glove.)
rationale: The user does not have to remove gloves or fumble with a small button.
judge_comment: It helps gloved users, but it is a niche convenience and only marginally reduces the learning curve.

title: 38 Faraday Curtain Door
new_elements: Faraday curtain door (A flexible metalized curtain with overlapping RF baffles replaces the rigid hinged door and latch.)
rationale: A curtain opens like a shop door and removes the latch/button choreography.
judge_comment: A flexible curtain door is radical and removes the latch, but a flexible barrier cannot reliably block microwave leakage, so it is a safety problem.

title: 39 Clear Door Without Lamp
new_elements: Transparent conductive door glass (A clear conductive-coated panel shields RF leakage while preserving full window view.); Clear RF-transparent door (A door window made without holes or internal bulb lets the user see the food directly.)
rationale: A normal clear window removes the puzzling perforated glass and dark bulb behavior.
judge_comment: A clear conductive-coated window is plausible, but it is close to existing mesh and coated glass and has little effect on operation.

title: 40 Acoustic Doneness Beeps
new_elements: Acoustic doneness beeps (A mechanical bell sequence or simple speaker replaces visual checking with obvious audible cues.); Indicate doneness without looking (Signals that cooking is finished or near finished through sound instead of an interior view.)
rationale: A familiar bell removes the need to inspect the dark interior for mistakes.
judge_comment: Audible cues are easy to build and intuitive, but microwaves already beep, so it adds little and does not simplify operation.

title: 41 Slot-Conveyor Microwave Body
new_elements: Slot-conveyor microwave body (A narrow conveyor slot accepts a food carrier from one side and returns it from the other, replacing the door.)
rationale: Food simply goes through a visible opening, making the door mechanism unnecessary.
judge_comment: Radical conveyor slot removes the door, but RF leakage through an open slot is a serious safety problem and it is unclear how it simplifies operation.

title: 42 One-Hand Push-Close Door
new_elements: One-hand push-close door (A weighted magnet door snaps shut when pushed, while a broad pull handle releases it.)
rationale: A self-closing door removes precise latch alignment and button pressing.
judge_comment: Easy and plausible, with a clear benefit for simple use, but it is an incremental door tweak rather than a radical idea.

title: 43 Sticker-Read Timer
new_elements: Sticker-read timer (A simple barcode or color sticker on the door sets the default time when pressed, replacing the timer knob.)
rationale: A sticker is a familiar physical object that can communicate cooking time without numbers.
judge_comment: Scanning a sticker to set the time removes number entry and is feasible, though it depends on stickers being supplied.

title: 44 Mains-Frequency Bell Clock
new_elements: Compensating mains-frequency clock (A counting mechanism uses mains cycles and switches between 50/60 Hz calibration to set duration.); Mains-clock timer (A simplified clock replaces the mechanical cam timer with a frequency-counting bell switch.)
rationale: The timer becomes a simple visible bell clock rather than a multi-number mechanical knob.
judge_comment: A mains-frequency counter is a cheap timer substitute, but it does little to remove the learning curve for users.

title: 45 Self-Powered Magnetron Timer
new_elements: Self-powered timing cam (The magnetron's own operating energy winds or releases a timing cam during cooking.); Magnetron-driven timer (A cam timer that starts when power is applied and ends when energy storage releases a latch.)
rationale: The machine times itself from its own activity, removing a user-visible clockwork control.
judge_comment: Self-timing from the magnetron's own energy is clever but technically doubtful, and it does not clearly make use simpler.

title: 46 Food-Slot Power Trigger
new_elements: Food-slot power trigger (Inserting a food tray into a shielded slot sets default power and opens RF access without a conventional door.)
rationale: The food tray becomes the control object, so the user does not operate the appliance directly.
judge_comment: Inserting a tray to start is intuitive, but a doorless RF-safe slot is hard to shield and a default power fits few foods.

title: 47 Weight-Only One-Touch Timer
new_elements: Weight-only one-touch timer (The cavity scale infers duration from plate weight and starts one default program when any button is touched.)
rationale: The appliance infers cooking time from weight, leaving the user only one touch to confirm.
judge_comment: A weight-inferred time with one-touch confirm is simple and buildable, though weight is a weak proxy for cook time.

title: 48 Magnetized Door-Start
new_elements: Magnetized door-start (A magnet in the door trips a reed switch and starts a fixed cycle when the door latches.)
rationale: A magnet makes closing the door a complete command, removing start-button learning.
judge_comment: Closing the door to start is very simple and feasible, but it's close to existing designs and a fixed cycle limits usefulness, with some safety concern about accidental starts.

title: 49 Pull-and-Go Cooking Trolley
new_elements: Pull-and-go cooking trolley (The whole microwave body is a rolling cart that opens by pulling a handle and starts from its position alone.); Carry and start without door controls (The user moves food in by pulling a cart-like microwave instead of manipulating a door and knobs.)
rationale: The appliance behaves like a familiar cart, so pulling and waiting replaces all microwave learning.
judge_comment: A rolling cart microwave is wild, but mobility doesn't clearly reduce learning and the mechanism is vague.

title: 50 Disposable Waveguide Cooking Envelope
new_elements: Disposable waveguide cooking envelope (A single-use RF-concentrating pouch and narrow slot let food be cooked without any door, knob, or user timing.); Single-slot cooking without controls (The pouch geometry and slot insertion alone set the heating environment.)
rationale: The user simply inserts a pouch into a slot, making the entire microwave control surface disappear.
judge_comment: A disposable waveguide pouch removes the controls entirely and is radical, but it is technically dubious and wasteful and needs a consumable.

title: Single Food Dial
new_elements: C_SingleFoodDial (One mechanical knob sets food type, time, and power.); T_StackedFoodCam (Stacked cams translate one knob into timer and duty-cycle presets.); F_OneDialCooking (Set cooking program in one twist.)
rationale: One dial removes almost all control decisions, making operation almost reflexive.
judge_comment: A single food dial with stacked cams is plausible and simple, though it resembles existing presets and is not very radical.

title: Push Once Dial
new_elements: C_PushOnceDial (Pushing the dial starts a preloaded countdown and the dial returns by itself.); T_SpringReturnCam (Spring-loaded cam releases after push and rewinds during operation.); F_PushStart (Start the microwave with one push.)
rationale: The user never has to learn knob ranges because a single push starts cooking.
judge_comment: A push-to-start dial with spring return is very easy to use, but a fixed preload limits flexibility and the mechanism is only moderately detailed.

title: Picture Power Knob
new_elements: C_PicturePowerKnob (Power knob shows foods such as soup, bread, butter, and meat instead of numbers.); T_PrintedPowerCam (Molded icon ring and cam set safe power presets for each food.); F_PicturePowerSet (Select heating level by choosing a picture.)
rationale: Replacing power numbers with food pictures lets users choose without reading scales.
judge_comment: Food icons in place of power numbers are easy to mold and understand, but the idea only changes the power control, not the whole operation.

title: One Button Cook
new_elements: C_OneButtonPanel (A single mechanical start button runs a safe default cycle.); T_FixedPresetCam (Cam stops after one fixed 60-second or 120-second preset selected by insert.); F_OnePressCook (Cook using only one press.)
rationale: A single button removes all setup choices for the simplest possible use.
judge_comment: One button gives the most minimal operation and is easy to build, but fixed cycles are restrictive and the idea is fairly obvious.

title: Color Start Button
new_elements: C_ColorStartButton (Colored buttons start fixed cook modes such as green for reheat and red for hot.); T_ColorCamButton (Mechanical buttons select color-coded preset cams.); F_ColorStart (Start cooking by recognizing color rather than text.)
rationale: Color buttons give elderly users an immediate visual start choice with no learning curve.
judge_comment: Color-coded start buttons help elderly users, but users still have to learn what each color means, so it is less radical than the other ideas.

title: Pull Cord Start
new_elements: C_PullCordDial (Pulling a cord starts a fixed mechanical timer cycle.); T_CordWoundTimer (Cord pulls a cam and releases it to count down.); F_PullCordStart (Start cooking by pulling a cord.)
rationale: Pulling a cord is a familiar physical action and avoids numeric dials.
judge_comment: A pull cord is a familiar action, but a fixed-cycle timer gives little control and the mechanism is vague.

title: Wind Up Timer Toy
new_elements: C_WindUpTimer (The timer knob is wound like a toy and automatically unwinds to cook.); T_FrictionClock (Friction clock mechanism controls cook time by release speed.); F_WindUpSet (Set time by amount of winding.)
rationale: Winding feels intuitive and avoids reading time increments.
judge_comment: Wind-up timers are proven and intuitive; mechanical timers already exist in microwaves, so it is less radical.

title: Mug Slot Start
new_elements: C_MugSlotGuide (A physical slot guides the user to choose a mug-sized or bowl-sized preset.); T_TactileMugSlot (Molded slot positions trigger different mechanical power cams.); F_AutoSizePower (Set power by physical container size.)
rationale: Matching controls to the physical food vessel makes power selection almost automatic.
judge_comment: Matching the control to vessel size is clever, but detecting container size with slot cams is physically questionable and restrictive.

title: Low Power Dial
new_elements: C_LowHighDial (Two-position dial replaces five power levels with Low and High.); T_TwoStepCam (Cam switch provides only two safe power presets.); F_TwoPowerLevels (Choose between two easy heating modes.)
rationale: Reducing five power choices to two lowers learning and decision complexity.
judge_comment: Easy to build and simplifies choices, but it is an obvious reduction rather than a radical idea.

title: Color Cavity
new_elements: C_CodedColorCavity (Interior color cues indicate done state without reading a display.); T_PhosphorescentCoating (Coating glows when timer nears zero and fades after bell.); F_ColorGoal (Know when cooking is nearly finished by cavity glow.)
rationale: A glowing cavity provides an effortless visual cue for when to check the food.
judge_comment: A glow cue is novel, but it addresses completion feedback rather than operation, and phosphorescent coatings in a microwave cavity face durability and heat issues.

title: Webcam Door
new_elements: C_WebcamDoor (Door window becomes a small webcam feed to a phone or external screen.); T_Webcam (Low-cost optical sensor streams interior view.); F_ExternalView (See the food without opening or peering at the door.)
rationale: A webcam gives a clearer view than a dim perforated window and avoids awkward bending.
judge_comment: A webcam adds complexity and needs a phone or screen, so it works against the no-learning-curve need, and it is not really a substitution that simplifies anything.

title: Transparent Casing
new_elements: C_TransparentMicrowaveShell (Whole casing uses transparent microwave-shielding material instead of a dark window.); T_TransparentConductiveFilm (Conductive film blocks leakage while allowing visible light through.); F_NoApertureView (See food from every side without holes or lamps.)
rationale: Full transparency removes door-window interpretation and makes checking food trivial.
judge_comment: A fully transparent shielded casing is radical, but it is hard to make safe and cheap, and seeing the food does little for simple operation.

title: Side Window
new_elements: C_SideViewWindow (A side viewing window lets the user check food at table height.); T_BorosilicateSideGlass (Borosilicate glass forms a microwave-transparent safe side window.); F_EyeLevelView (View the cavity without stooping.)
rationale: Side visibility makes checking food easier and less physically demanding.
judge_comment: A side window is easy to understand, but the borosilicate glass would need metal shielding, and the benefit to operation is marginal.

title: Handle Door
new_elements: C_PullDoorHandle (Door opens by pulling a handle instead of pressing a hidden release button.); T_LeverHandleMech (Handle directly drives latch lever through a simple linkage.); F_PullOpen (Open door with a natural pull.)
rationale: A pull handle is more obvious than a button and requires no explanation.
judge_comment: A pull handle is intuitive, cheap and proven, and it clearly removes confusion over opening the door, though it is hardly radical.

title: Magnetic Flap Door
new_elements: C_MagneticFlapDoor (Door becomes a magnetically held flap that opens with a light pull.); T_MagnetLatch (Magnetic detent holds door while allowing soft-open latch.); F_FlapOpen (Open door by moving the flap without releasing a button.)
rationale: A flap opening is visually obvious and avoids tiny release buttons.
judge_comment: A magnetic flap door is intuitive and replaces the release button, but the magnets must still seal the door safely and survive heat.

title: Auto Open Door
new_elements: C_AutoOpenDoor (Door slightly opens when cooking time finishes.); T_MemoryMetalLatch (Heat-actuated latch releases after timer completes.); F_AutoOpen (Door opens itself when finished.)
rationale: The product does the final action for the user and removes manual door-release steps.
judge_comment: Auto-opening door is plausible and already exists on some appliances, but it only removes one minor step and does little for the no-learning-curve need.

title: Vibrate Done
new_elements: C_VibrationDone (Whole countertop vibrates gently when cooking ends.); T_VibrationCam (Mechanical timer trips an unbalanced rotor for vibration.); F_VibrateDone (Signal completion by vibration instead of bell.)
rationale: A felt vibration is an unambiguous finish cue for users with hearing loss.
judge_comment: A vibration cue is workable and accessibility-minded, but it is mostly a completion signal and does not simplify operation.

title: Aroma Done
new_elements: C_AromaDoneEmitter (Finishes cycle releases a familiar food-scent cue.); T_AromaCam (Timer trips a sealed scent cartridge release.); F_ScentDone (Indicate completion by smell.)
rationale: Scent completion signals are memorable and require no new learned meaning.
judge_comment: A scent cue is novel, but cartridges are impractical, the scent may be ambiguous, and it does not simplify operation.

title: Phone Notify
new_elements: C_WirelessDoneNotifier (Cooking completion is sent to a simple wireless pager or phone.); T_LowPowerRadio (One-button radio transmitter sends only a done signal.); F_PhoneDone (Alert the user remotely when cooking ends.)
rationale: Remote notification lets users walk away safely without watching the timer.
judge_comment: Easy to build, but phone notification is common and it adds a device rather than simplifying operation.

title: Thermochromic Window
new_elements: C_ThermochromicWindow (Door window changes color when food reaches a useful temperature range.); T_ThermochromicFilm (Heat-sensitive film shifts color with cavity temperature.); F_WarmColorView (See readiness by window color.)
rationale: Color change gives an intuitive readiness cue without reading displays.
judge_comment: A thermochromic window is an intuitive readiness cue, but sensing food temperature through cavity film is unreliable and microwave conditions are harsh.

title: Continuous Power Dial
new_elements: C_SolidPowerKnob (Knob sets smooth magnetron power instead of stepped on/off cycling.); T_SolidStatePowerControl (Simple inverter drives magnetron continuously at variable power.); F_ContinuousPower (Set heating power smoothly and safely.)
rationale: Smooth power removes guesswork caused by on/off cycling and simpler heat behavior.
judge_comment: Inverter-style continuous power is real (Panasonic) and smooths heating, but a power dial still asks users to choose a level, so it adds little to zero-learning-curve operation.

title: Warm Hot Switch
new_elements: C_WarmHotSwitch (A two-position switch replaces all power levels with Warm and Hot.); T_TwoPositionCam (Cam switch provides safe average-power presets.); F_TwoModeHeat (Select heat using only two modes.)
rationale: Two plain-language modes are easier for elderly users than numeric power levels.
judge_comment: Two plain-language modes cut choices and are easy to build with a cam, but the idea is incremental rather than radical.

title: Full Power Only Switch
new_elements: C_FullPowerOnlySwitch (Removes power selection and always runs a safe full-power short cycle.); T_NoDutyCam (Duty-cycle cam fixed to full power for simple cooking.); F_FullPowerCook (Cook with only one power behavior.)
rationale: Eliminating the power knob entirely removes one source of confusion.
judge_comment: Removing power selection is very simple and cheap, but it risks overcooking and is an obvious reduction, not a wild idea.

title: Temp Probe Auto Stop
new_elements: C_TempProbeAutoStop (A reusable probe stops cooking when target temperature is reached.); T_ThermistorProbe (Low-cost thermistor reads food temperature and cuts timer.); F_AutoTempStop (Stop cooking by food readiness rather than guessed time.)
rationale: Automatic temperature stopping removes the need to estimate correct time.
judge_comment: A probe that stops cooking at target temperature removes time guessing, but users must insert it and set a target, and probes in microwave cavities raise safety and arcing issues.

title: Weight Auto Timer
new_elements: C_WeightAutoTimer (Turntable base senses food weight and chooses a simple default time.); T_LoadCell (Load cell converts mass into mechanical preset selection.); F_WeightTime (Set cooking time from food weight.)
rationale: The product estimates time from weight, so users do not need to learn timing rules.
judge_comment: Weight-based automatic time is plausible with a load cell and removes timing rules, though weight alone is an imperfect proxy for food type and needed time.

title: Door Close Start
new_elements: C_DoorCloseStart (Closing the door starts a safe short heating cycle.); T_NormallyOpenDoorSwitch (Door latch switch triggers timer only on closure.); F_CloseToCook (Start cooking by closing the door.)
rationale: Cooking begins with the familiar action of closing the door, not pressing controls.
judge_comment: Close-to-start is very intuitive and simple to build, though a fixed short cycle limits control and risks accidental starts.

title: Pull Turntable Start
new_elements: C_TurntablePullStart (Pulling the turntable winds the timer and starts it.); T_PullCam (Turntable linkage drives a mechanical timer cam.); F_PullRotateStart (Set and start cooking by pulling the plate.)
rationale: Using the existing plate as the timer control makes interaction feel natural.
judge_comment: Using the plate as a mechanical timer is a creative substitution, but linking a turntable to a timer cam is awkward and it may be hard to make it robust.

title: Static Plate
new_elements: C_NoSpinPlate (A stationary shallow plate replaces rotating glass and motor.); T_GeometricWaveguide (Cavity shaping heats without needing rotation.); F_NoRotationCook (Cook without a turntable.)
rationale: Removing the turntable reduces parts and makes placement of food simpler.
judge_comment: Removing the turntable simplifies placement, but it barely affects operation and the claim of even heating with no rotation is shaky.

title: Induction Pad
new_elements: C_InductionCookPad (Replace microwave cavity with a simple induction cooking pad and pot.); T_InductionHeating (Induction coil heats compatible pots directly.); F_PotBoil (Boil or warm food using pot heat instead of cavity cooking.)
rationale: A pot on a pad is more familiar than a microwave cavity and avoids door and timer learning.
judge_comment: Induction is feasible and familiar, but it abandons the microwave function and does not remove the learning curve.

title: Food Tag Reader
new_elements: C_FoodTagReader (Reader detects tagged reusable food markers and starts preset programs.); T_RFIDReader (Low-cost RFID chooses one of several mechanical presets.); F_TagAutoProgram (Start cooking by detecting a food tag.)
rationale: A tag tells the microwave what to do, so the user does not learn controls.
judge_comment: Tag-triggered presets remove controls entirely, but they require tagged containers and extra setup, which makes the design less simple.

title: Big Buttons
new_elements: C_BigPhysicalButtons (Replace knobs with very large mechanical buttons for each preset.); T_LargeCamButtons (Big buttons move simple cams for start and power presets.); F_BigButtonSelect (Select cooking preset by pressing a large button.)
rationale: Large buttons are easier for older hands and clearer than small knobs.
judge_comment: Big one-touch preset buttons directly cut the learning curve, but the idea is incremental and not very radical.

title: Braille Dial
new_elements: C_BrailleDial (Knob has raised braille markings and tactile detents for each preset.); T_MoldedBraille (Molded rubber braille and notch positions give touch feedback.); F_TactileBraille (Choose mode by touch.)
rationale: Tactile markings reduce visual demands and help users find modes without reading.
judge_comment: Tactile braille detents help accessibility and are easy to mold, but they only partly address the general no-learning-curve need.

title: High Contrast Sticker
new_elements: C_HighContrastSticker (Knob face uses very high-contrast simple icons.); T_PrintedLabel (Low-cost screen-printed high-contrast overlay.); F_ClearLabeling (Read control settings easily.)
rationale: Simple high-contrast labels reduce visual effort and learning.
judge_comment: A cheap, clear label helps readability but is very obvious and barely innovative.

title: Weighted Knob
new_elements: C_WeightedTimerKnob (Timer knob is heavier and has strong detents to prevent slipping.); T_InertialKnob (Inertial mass and detents give precise mechanical time setting.); F_StableGrip (Set timer with confident hand control.)
rationale: A stable knob prevents accidental time changes for shaky-handed users.
judge_comment: A weighted detented knob improves control for shaky hands but does little to reduce the learning curve.

title: Lockable Knobs
new_elements: C_LockableKnobs (A small key switch locks preset positions once selected.); T_MechLock (Mechanical lock prevents knob drift during operation.); F_ChildLock (Keep selected settings unchanged.)
rationale: Locking settings removes fear that someone will accidentally change the cooking mode.
judge_comment: A key lock adds a step and complexity, working against simple operation with no learning.

title: Remote Panel
new_elements: C_RemoteControlPanel (Controls move to a detachable panel near the user's chair.); T_PlugCable (Cable connects simple mechanical or electrical controls to oven.); F_PanelSelect (Operate microwave from a seated control panel.)
rationale: A nearby panel avoids standing and bending while keeping controls simple.
judge_comment: A detachable wired panel is plausible, but it mainly addresses posture rather than learning curve and is not very radical.

title: Phone App Control
new_elements: C_BluetoothController (A one-tap phone button starts preset cooking.); T_BLE (Bluetooth link carries only start and stop presets.); F_PhoneSelect (Start the microwave from a phone.)
rationale: If the app is reduced to one large start button, phone control can be easier than knobs.
judge_comment: Easy to build, but a phone app adds setup and pairing steps, which works against zero learning curve, and it is already common.

title: RF Key Fob
new_elements: C_RFKeyFob (A car-garage-style fob starts cooking and stops it.); T_RFReceiver (Receiver decodes simple two-button RF commands.); F_FobStart (Start or stop cooking with a large fob button.)
rationale: A familiar large fob button removes tiny appliance controls entirely.
judge_comment: A two-button fob is very simple to use and feasible, but you lose the fob easily and it does not choose the food program.

title: NFC Card Pad
new_elements: C_NFCTouchPad (Tapping a food card starts a preset cycle.); T_NFCTag (Passive tags encode one of several simple programs.); F_CardStart (Start cooking by tapping a card.)
rationale: Tapping a card is a single gesture and hides all technical settings.
judge_comment: Tapping a food card gives a single-gesture, no-settings experience with cheap passive tags, though cards must be managed.

title: QR Recipe Reader
new_elements: C_QRRecipeReader (A printed recipe card QR code starts the correct preset.); T_QRCamera (Low-cost camera scans QR code and selects mechanical preset.); F_ScanStart (Start cooking by scanning a card.)
rationale: Scanning a familiar recipe card can be easier than operating knobs.
judge_comment: Scanning a recipe card is workable, but a camera is costlier and more fiddly than NFC for the same function.

title: Egg Shape Timer
new_elements: C_EggShapeKnob (Timer knob is a large egg-shaped grip.); T_ErgonomicCam (Egg shape provides torque and orientation cues.); F_EggGrip (Turn timer by gripping a recognizable object.)
rationale: A familiar shape improves grip and makes time setting less abstract.
judge_comment: An easy-to-grip egg-shaped knob is plausible and mildly helpful, but it barely changes how time is set and is not radical.

title: Whistle Done
new_elements: C_SteamWhistleDone (Cooking completion releases a tea-kettle-style whistle.); T_MechWhistle (Timer trips a small steam or air whistle.); F_WhistleDone (Signal completion with a familiar whistle.)
rationale: A whistle is a universally understood completion signal requiring no learning.
judge_comment: A whistle is an intuitive completion cue, but it only covers the end of cooking, and a steam or air whistle in a microwave is awkward to build.

title: Pop Up Flag
new_elements: C_FinishFlagPop (A small flag pops up when cooking ends.); T_SpringFlag (Spring-loaded flag is released by the timer cam.); F_PopupDone (Show completion by popping a flag.)
rationale: A physical pop-up provides an obvious silent completion cue.
judge_comment: A mechanical pop-up flag is simple, cheap and clear, and it replaces the electronic beep, though it does not help with operation itself.

title: Bioluminescent Light
new_elements: C_BioluminescentLight (A sealed living-light panel illuminates the window without electricity.); T_AlgaeLight (Encapsulated bioluminescent organisms emit steady visible light.); F_SelfGlow (Light the cavity without a bulb or switch.)
rationale: Self-glow removes the need to learn when to use a lamp or inspect a dark cavity.
judge_comment: Living bioluminescent light is wild, but it is impractical (it needs heat tolerance and keeping organisms alive) and has little bearing on ease of operation.

title: Hidden Mesh Glass
new_elements: C_HiddenMeshGlass (Door looks like clear glass with an invisible microwave mesh.); T_TransparentEMICoating (Micro-scale transparent conductive layer blocks RF while passing light.); F_GlassView (See clearly while meeting shielding constraints.)
rationale: A clear-looking door makes checking food feel obvious instead of hidden by mesh.
judge_comment: A transparent RF-blocking door would improve visibility, but it is technically hard, and it contributes only indirectly to simple operation.

title: Touchless Knob
new_elements: C_UltrasonicDial (A wave gesture over the control area sets a fixed preset.); T_UltrasonicSensor (One ultrasonic sensor detects only a short wave gesture.); F_GestureDial (Start cooking without touching a dirty knob.)
rationale: A single obvious gesture avoids complex button sequences.
judge_comment: A wave gesture with a fixed preset is simple, but it is not obviously discoverable, and it replaces a knob with something that may be less intuitive.

title: Voice Prompt Speaker
new_elements: C_SpeakerPrompt (Speaker says simple one-line instructions only when needed.); T_SimpleAudioPrompt (Pre-recorded voice prompts guide one-step operation.); F_VoiceGuide (Give audio guidance without reading labels.)
rationale: Spoken one-step guidance removes the need to understand unfamiliar symbols.
judge_comment: Voice prompts are very feasible and reduce the learning curve, but talking appliances are a familiar idea and the prompts add parts rather than substitute cheaper ones.

title: Recipe Card Slot
new_elements: C_RecipeCardSlot (A physical recipe card is inserted to set time and power.); T_SlottedCam (Card cutouts drive mechanical preset cams.); F_CardProgram (Select cooking program by inserting a card.)
rationale: Using a familiar recipe card turns operation into a simple insert-and-go action.
judge_comment: Insert-and-go recipe cards with mechanical cams are a concrete, intuitive and fairly novel substitution for the keypad, though they limit flexibility.

title: Door Push Start
new_elements: C_PushDoorStart (Pushing the door closed starts the selected preset.); T_DoorLinkCam (Door latch action triggers timer cam through linkage.); F_PushDoorStart (Start cooking by pushing the door.)
rationale: Making the door itself the start control reduces separate operations.
judge_comment: Using the door close as the start action removes a step and is mechanically plausible, but it risks accidental starts and depends on a preset already being selected.

title: Food Cap Start
new_elements: C_AutonomousFoodCap (A reusable food cap starts the correct preset when placed on the cavity.); T_PhaseChangeTimer (Mechanical phase-change element sets safe time from food type.); F_CapProgramStart (Start cooking with a food-aware cap.)
rationale: The food package or cap selects settings, leaving the user only to place it.
judge_comment: A food-aware cap that sets the program is radical and needs little user input, but the phase-change timer mechanism is implausible and food-type sensing is unclear.

title: 01 One-Press Auto Stop
new_elements: One-press auto-stop function (RF absorption and steam sensing decide when heating stops.)
rationale: The user presses once and the microwave decides completion, removing settings learning.
judge_comment: A single press with sensor-based auto-stop directly removes the need to learn settings, and steam sensors already exist, though the substitution of parts is loose.

title: 02 Single Dial Cook All
new_elements: Single-dial cook-all function (One knob position automatically selects time and power pattern.)
rationale: Replaces multi-step power and timer choice with a single familiar dial action.
judge_comment: A single dial is familiar and easy to build, but it is a common, non-radical approach and the auto time and power selection is vague.

title: 03 Transparent Chamber Door
new_elements: Transparent chamber viewing function (See food without interior lamp or perforated door.)
rationale: Makes checking food obvious and requires no learned procedure.
judge_comment: A transparent chamber door is only loosely connected to ease of operation and is hard to do given the need for microwave shielding.

title: 04 Webcam Door
new_elements: Webcam door preview function (A door-mounted camera shows the cavity image to the user.)
rationale: Replaces indirect inspection with a direct, intuitive visual feedback path.
judge_comment: A door camera is feasible but adds complexity and does little to reduce the learning curve.

title: 05 Plug Timer
new_elements: Plug-mounted time control function (Moves basic timing to the mains plug instead of oven controls.)
rationale: Uses an everyday plug-style timer to reduce unfamiliar microwave controls.
judge_comment: Moving the timer to the plug is wild and a simple substitution, but it is awkward in use and has safety and practicality issues.

title: 06 Air-Flow Tray
new_elements: Airflow turntable function (Replaces the rotating tray motor with passive airflow rotation.)
rationale: Removes a mechanical control and makes operation simpler and cheaper.
judge_comment: Passive airflow rotation is physically implausible in a microwave, and removing the motor does little for operational simplicity.

title: 07 Stirrer Cavity
new_elements: RF mode stirrer function (Uses a random RF stirrer instead of a glass turntable.)
rationale: Eliminates turntable alignment and cleaning steps for a simpler use.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers already exist in commercial microwaves and work, but the user-facing simplicity benefit is modest and the idea isn't radical.

title: 08 Nano Waveguide Cover
new_elements: Self-cleaning waveguide cover function (Replaces mica with a nonstick microwave-transparent liner.)
rationale: Reduces maintenance knowledge by making splatter less visible and less critical.
judge_comment: A nonstick waveguide liner is a plausible maintenance tweak but barely affects operation or the learning curve.

title: 09 Soft Choke Door
new_elements: Soft RF-absorbing door choke function (Replaces the quarter-wave metal rim with a flexible RF gasket.)
rationale: Simplifies door handling because the seal is forgiving and easier to close.
judge_comment: An RF-absorbing gasket is plausible, as flexible chokes exist, but the link to easier operation is weak.

title: 10 Hand-Presence Door
new_elements: Hand-presence safety door function (Replaces mechanical interlock switches with capacitive hand detection.)
rationale: Makes door use more natural by sensing intent rather than relying on latch precision.
judge_comment: Capacitive hand sensing for door interlock is novel and aligns with intuitive use, but replacing redundant mechanical safety interlocks is risky and unlikely to be approved.

title: 11 Thermal Model Guard
new_elements: Current-signature overheat guard function (Replaces a bimetal thermostat with electrical-signature heat protection.)
rationale: Automatically prevents overheating without user monitoring.
judge_comment: Automatic overheat protection helps safety, but it is invisible to the user and barely touches the operation learning curve.

title: 12 Bleeder Magnetron
new_elements: Magnetron bleeder discharge function (Adds automatic high-voltage discharge to reduce safety procedure needs.)
rationale: Makes shutdown safer and easier because the user learns no capacitor discharge ritual.
judge_comment: Bleeder discharge is a service-safety feature that users never perform, so it has almost no bearing on simple operation.

title: 13 Voice Clock
new_elements: Spoken remaining time function (Replaces the bell with speech such as one minute left.)
rationale: Gives status in ordinary language instead of learned beeps.
judge_comment: Spoken time remaining is easy to understand and very feasible, though talking appliances are not new.

title: 14 Pull Start Door
new_elements: Pull-to-start door function (Pulling the door handle starts cooking after a short confirmation.)
rationale: Turns door closure itself into the primary start action.
judge_comment: Using the door pull as the start action is intuitive and radical, but it needs a defined default time or power to work without a learning curve.

title: 15 Foot Pedal Start
new_elements: Foot-pedal start function (Starts cooking with a simple foot switch when hands are occupied.)
rationale: Adds an instinctive physical control for busy single-person users.
judge_comment: A foot switch is simple and feasible, but it is a niche accessory that adds a device and does not remove the learning needed for time and power settings.

title: 16 Recipe Chip
new_elements: Insertable recipe chip function (A food-package chip tells the microwave one-button settings.)
rationale: Turns complex recipe learning into a simple package-level operation.
judge_comment: A package chip that sets one-button cooking removes recipe learning, though it needs packaging ecosystem adoption and doesn't clearly substitute a cheaper part.

title: 17 Cavity Glow Power
new_elements: Color-coded cavity glow function (The interior light color shows active power level without menus.)
rationale: Makes power state glanceable instead of abstract.
judge_comment: Color-coded cavity light is easy to build and glanceable, but it only displays state and doesn't simplify input.

title: 18 Gravity Latch
new_elements: Gravity-assisted auto latch function (The door closes and latches using weighted geometry.)
rationale: Removes learned push-button timing from door operation.
judge_comment: A gravity-assisted latch is mechanically plausible and replaces a button mechanism, but it addresses a minor part of operation.

title: 19 Phosphor Cavity
new_elements: Phosphorescent cavity light function (Replaces the bulb with a glow material charged by outside light.)
rationale: Keeps the oven simple by removing bulb failure and light-switch knowledge.
judge_comment: A phosphorescent cavity light is a bold substitution, but glow material won't be bright enough or heat- and microwave-stable, and it is only loosely tied to ease of use.

title: 20 Steam Timer
new_elements: Steam-dose timer function (Counts emitted steam or condensation as the cooking amount.)
rationale: Avoids precise short-time learning by using a natural food signal.
judge_comment: Using steam or condensation as a cooking-done signal is radical and removes time-setting, but sensing is unreliable across different foods.

title: 21 Mood Buttons
new_elements: Mood preset function (Three buttons only: warm, hot, ready-to-eat.)
rationale: Replaces numeric controls with life-style labels a beginner understands.
judge_comment: Directly removes numeric controls for a beginner-friendly interface, though simplified presets already exist and it is not very radical.

title: 22 Magnetic Cavity
new_elements: Magnetic detachable cavity function (The cavity snaps out with magnets instead of screws or latches.)
rationale: Cleans and inspects easily without learning disassembly.
judge_comment: Easy cleaning is a benefit, but it barely affects operation learning and a removable cavity raises microwave-leakage and safety concerns.

title: 23 Low-Voltage RF
new_elements: Low-voltage RF generator function (Replaces the high-voltage diode and doubler with safer RF electronics.)
rationale: Reduces scary electrical details and makes the product feel simpler.
judge_comment: A radical solid-state RF source is a real direction, but it is invisible to the user and does little for operational simplicity.

title: 24 Fiber Optic Light
new_elements: Fiber-optic cavity lighting function (Daylight or LED light is piped into the cavity without internal bulb.)
rationale: Provides viewing without heat, replacement, or switch learning.
judge_comment: Fiber-optic lighting is a clever substitution, but it only marginally helps ease of use, and piping daylight is impractical.

title: 25 Food Probe Done
new_elements: Food-probe auto stop function (A simple insertable probe stops heating when the food is done.)
rationale: Turns time and power guessing into one direct doneness signal.
judge_comment: A doneness probe replaces time and power guessing with one signal, but metal probes in a microwave need special design.

title: 26 One Push Minute
new_elements: Single-minute button function (Each press adds thirty seconds, then automatically runs.)
rationale: Uses the repeated physical action of pressing instead of menu navigation.
judge_comment: Directly simplifies operation to a single button, but it's close to existing quick-start buttons and is not a radical substitution.

title: 27 Electro-Seal Door
new_elements: Electromagnetic door seal function (Magnetically holds the door closed instead of hooks and switches.)
rationale: Door operation becomes a natural open-push feel with fewer latch tricks.
judge_comment: Door operation is already simple, and an electromagnetic seal raises safety and RF containment concerns, so it only weakly serves the need.

title: 28 Conformal Waveguide Liner
new_elements: Conformal waveguide liner function (A molded microwave-transparent liner replaces flat mica.)
rationale: Removes a fragile part and the knowledge needed to keep it clean.
judge_comment: A plausible part substitution, but it mostly affects maintenance rather than operating simplicity.

title: 29 Leakage Temp Sense
new_elements: RF-leakage thermal model function (Detects unsafe temperature rise from RF leakage patterns.)
rationale: Handles overheating invisibly so the beginner never has to diagnose heat.
judge_comment: Detecting leakage by temperature is dubious and vague, and it has little link to ease of operation.

title: 30 Vibrating Base
new_elements: Vibration-mixed base function (Gentle base vibration distributes heat without a turntable motor.)
rationale: Removes turntable centering and motor-related care steps.
judge_comment: Replacing the turntable with vibration is a bold substitution that removes a user step, but it is technically doubtful with liquids and heavy food.

title: 31 Transparent Glass
new_elements: Transparent touch glass function (Control icons fade in only when the user touches the glass.)
rationale: Reduces visible complexity until the user is ready to act.
judge_comment: Hidden-until-touched controls reduce clutter and are plausible, though hidden controls can hurt discoverability.

title: 32 Buzz Done
