rationale: A self-testing door hides electrical safety complexity behind one simple closing action.
judge_comment: A single self-testing magnetic door switch is plausible and tidy, but users already operate doors without any learning, so it adds little for this need.

title: BreakfastButton
new_elements: A21BreakfastButton (One button replaces timer and power knobs for morning drinks.); A21OnePressDrink (Press once to produce a ready drink.)
rationale: A single breakfast button removes the need to recall drink heating settings.
judge_comment: A simple one-press drink button is easy to use and very feasible, but it is a preset button and barely radical, and it only covers drinks.

title: UniversalWarmButton
new_elements: A22UniversalWarmButton (Warm button replaces all manual settings.); A22OnePressWarm (One press heats a standard plate to a comfortable warm level.)
rationale: A single warm button captures the most common reheating intent without settings.
judge_comment: A single warm button is simple, but a standard plate is vague and results will vary with food type and quantity.

title: SoundReadinessDetector
new_elements: A23SoundReadinessDetector (Microphone in vent replaces mechanical timer by listening for boiling, popping, or sizzling.); A23AcousticAutoStop (Sound patterns decide when cooking is complete.)
rationale: Listening for cooking sounds lets the appliance decide time instead of the user.
judge_comment: Acoustic detection of popping and boiling is novel and removes timing decisions, but it works only for a few food types and the sensor must cope with noise.

title: ColorReadinessCamera
new_elements: A24ColorReadinessCamera (Small camera replaces user-set timer and lamp, detecting food color changes.); A24CameraAutoStop (The appliance learns completion visually, so user does not.)
rationale: Visual food readiness is detected by the microwave, so the user needs no timing knowledge.
judge_comment: A camera that judges doneness removes the need for any user input and is plausible, though steam, splatter and the range of foods make reliability hard.

title: ThermalDoorDisplay
new_elements: A25ThermalDoorDisplay (Thermal imaging panel replaces lamp and mesh view.); A25HeatViewNoLight (Readiness appears as a heat map, requiring no interpretation.)
rationale: Heat colors make readiness intuitive instead of requiring learned light or dial cues.
judge_comment: A thermal heat-map door display is eye-catching, but it adds interpretation work for the user, and thermal imaging through a shielded door is costly and hard to build.

title: ConveyorTunnel
new_elements: A26ConveyorTunnel (Continuous belt replaces door, button, and latch mechanics.); A26BeltNoDoor (Load at one end, take cooked item from the other with no door learning.)
rationale: A conveyor tunnel removes door mechanics from the cooking gesture.
judge_comment: A conveyor tunnel removes door handling and is radical, but it raises serious problems with microwave leakage, shielding, size, and cost, and it doesn't address how long to heat.

title: SqueezeHandleTimer
new_elements: A27SqueezeHandleTimer (Handle squeeze replaces knob timer and power dial.); A27SqueezeToSetCook (How long the handle is squeezed sets automatic time.)
rationale: Squeezing a handle is a natural gesture that avoids learning numeric timers.
judge_comment: Squeezing a handle to set the time is intuitive and easy to build, though it can be tiring for longer cook times and gives imprecise control.

title: FootStartPedal
new_elements: A28FootStartPedal (Foot pedal replaces door release button for hands-free start.); A28HandsFreeStart (Opening or closing the cavity requires no learned hand sequence.)
rationale: A foot pedal gives an obvious separate action for starting when hands are occupied.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is simple to build, but it adds a separate control without simplifying time or power, so it does little for learning.

title: SelfContainedPot
new_elements: A29SelfContainedPot (Sealed pot with built-in heating chamber replaces cavity door and knobs.); A29PotOnlyCook (User just puts food in pot and presses pot.)
rationale: Cooking becomes a pot action instead of learning microwave-specific door and knob steps.
judge_comment: A sealed pot with its own heating chamber is a bold substitution, but it is essentially a different appliance and the 'press the pot' interaction is vague.

title: DoItAllButton
new_elements: A30DoItAllButton (Big button replaces all knobs and modes.); A30UniversalProgram (One press runs an all-purpose heating logic.)
rationale: The only button on the appliance does the most common thing, removing learning almost entirely.
judge_comment: A single universal button removes almost all learning and is easy to implement, though it is an obvious idea and one program can't suit every food.

title: PlateAwareNoDisplay
new_elements: A31PlateAwareNoDisplay (Tray sensor reads plate size, material, and fullness instead of showing controls.); A31PlateTypeAutoProgram (Food preparation starts by sensing the plate, not by user setup.)
rationale: Sensing the plate removes visible controls, so the user learns nothing to operate the appliance.
judge_comment: Plate sensing to auto-start removes controls, but sensing food type and fullness through a tray is technically hard and the cook result is unreliable.

title: ShapeRecognitionLens
new_elements: A32ShapeRecognitionLens (Lens in door replaces lamp and knobs by recognizing food shape and volume.); A32ShapeAutoProgram (Appliance selects time and power automatically from shape.)
rationale: Recognizing food shape decides the program, replacing learned time and power selection.
judge_comment: A camera-based food recognizer is plausible and does eliminate the learning curve, though camera inside a microwave must survive heat and steam, and similar ideas already exist.

title: HeatColorPlate
new_elements: A33HeatColorPlate (Turntable changes color when food is ready, replacing lamp and timer.); A33ReadyByColor (Color indicates done state without dial learning.)
rationale: A color-changing plate tells readiness instantly, removing interpretation of lights and dials.
judge_comment: A color-changing plate is intuitive for readiness, but it covers only the done state, and a reliable reversible thermochromic material on a turntable is hard.

title: GestureStart
new_elements: A34GestureStart (Gesture sensor replaces buttons and knobs with a wave or palm press.); A34WaveToCook (A natural gesture starts a safe automatic cycle.)
rationale: A simple wave or touch gesture replaces learning physical dial positions.
judge_comment: Gesture start is easy to build, but it doesn't solve how long or how hot to cook, and it is not very radical.

title: SingleMagneticDoor
new_elements: A35SingleMagneticDoor (Magnet-toothed door replaces latch, push button, choke rim, and interlocks.); A35SelfAligningSafeClose (The door can only be closed in the correct way, so users learn nothing.)
rationale: A magnetic door makes the correct motion obvious and prevents unsafe door states.
judge_comment: A self-aligning magnetic door simplifies closing, but it doesn't address operating the cook settings, and replacing the interlocks and choke rim is a safety concern.

title: AutoThermoVent
new_elements: A36AutoThermoVent (Thermosiphon louvre replaces cooling fan and fan motor.); A36PassiveNoLearningCooling (Cooling needs no user adjustment or maintenance choice.)
rationale: Passive cooling removes a component that could generate confusing noises or errors.
judge_comment: Passive thermosiphon cooling is a real substitution, but a user never operates the cooling fan, so it barely helps ease of use, and it is thermally doubtful for magnetron cooling.

title: SelfDischargeDoor
new_elements: A37SelfDischargeDoor (Door closure triggers capacitor discharge, removing voltage-discharge knowledge.); A37ZeroVoltageWhenClosed (The appliance is electrically inert whenever the door is closed.)
rationale: Automatic discharge eliminates the need to learn hidden high-voltage waiting steps.
judge_comment: Automatic capacitor discharge on door closure is plausible and aids safety, but users already don't need to know about discharge, so the link to simple operation is weak.

title: UnifiedThermalFuse
new_elements: A38UnifiedThermalFuse (One composite thermal fuse replaces two bimetal cutouts and main fuse.); A38OneSafeFuseLogic (Protection resets invisibly, so users need no troubleshooting knowledge.)
rationale: Unified protection reduces error states that otherwise teach users complicated troubleshooting.
judge_comment: Consolidating the protection devices is feasible and cheap, but thermal fuses don't reset, so the claim of invisible reset is inconsistent and the benefit to the user is minor.

title: AromaSensor
new_elements: A39AromaSensor (Vent aroma sensor replaces bell and timer knob by detecting cooked food smell.); A39SmellAutoReady (The appliance knows ready by scent, requiring no user timing skill.)
rationale: Smell-based readiness replaces the need to learn cooking durations.
judge_comment: Detecting doneness by smell directly removes the need to set times, which is the main learning hurdle, though the sensor's reliability across foods is uncertain.

title: DoorScreenMirror
new_elements: A40DoorScreenMirror (Reflective smart door replaces window, lamp, and fascia controls.); A40OutsideCookingDisplay (Door surface shows only a simple ready cue, hiding all settings.)
rationale: The whole door becomes one simple display, eliminating the need to look for knobs and lights.
judge_comment: A door that shows only a ready cue simplifies the interface, but a reflective smart door that must also shield microwaves and still let users see the food is technically hard.

title: DepthSensingTurntable
new_elements: A41DepthSensingTurntable (Optical depth sensor on turntable replaces knob timer by estimating volume.); A41VolumeAutoTime (Food volume sets the cycle automatically.)
rationale: The turntable estimates volume and chooses time, so users need not learn portion-size formulas.
judge_comment: Auto-timing from sensed volume directly removes the need to set a timer, though it is not truly a cheaper substitution and food type matters as well as volume.

title: ReversibleTurntableMotor
new_elements: A42ReversibleTurntableMotor (Bidirectional motor replaces one-way turntable motor to remove spot alignment issues.); A42AutoSwapRotation (Rotation automatically avoids standing-wave hot spots without user intervention.)
rationale: Automatic reversal removes the learned trick of stopping and repositioning uneven food.
judge_comment: A reversing motor is plausible and cheap, but it only slightly reduces user effort and doesn't change the core operation.

title: ActiveChokeDoor
new_elements: A43ActiveChokeDoor (RF-canceling rim replaces quarter-wave choke and mesh window.); A43NoVisibleSealContainment (Containment is automatic and requires no user cleaning or alignment learning.)
rationale: Active sealing hides maintenance-sensitive RF containment from the user.
judge_comment: Active RF cancellation is hidden from users, so it barely affects ease of operation, and it raises safety concerns versus a passive choke.

title: PlasmaMicaCover
new_elements: A44PlasmaMicaCover (Plasma-coated waveguide window replaces removable mica sheet.); A44SelfShieldingCover (Splatter protection is invisible, so users need no replaceable-part knowledge.)
rationale: A non-removable waveguide cover prevents the user from needing to know about mica replacement.
judge_comment: A non-removable cover avoids a maintenance concern, but the 'plasma-coated' part is vague and it has little bearing on operation.

title: AutoVoltageCord
new_elements: A45AutoVoltageCord (Smart cord replaces fixed HV transformer taps for regional mains variants.); A45OnePlugAllRegions (Users do not need to know voltage settings.)
rationale: One plug adapts automatically, so users learn no mains-region configuration.
judge_comment: Voltage adaptation is a setup matter for manufacturers or regions and does not address the user's operating experience.

title: PhoneDockOneTap
new_elements: A46PhoneDockOneTap (Docked phone screen becomes the only microwave control, replacing knobs and buttons.); A46TapPhoneToStart (One tap on a familiar device launches automatic cooking.)
rationale: Users already understand tapping a phone, so the microwave needs no new control language.
judge_comment: Phone as sole control is plausible and familiar, but it requires owning and docking a phone and is not very radical.

title: BioluminescentCavityCoating
new_elements: A47BioluminescentCavityCoating (Self-lighting cavity coating replaces interior lamp.); A47BulbFreeWatch (The cavity glows passively, removing lamp maintenance and status learning.)
rationale: A passive glow removes lamp interpretation and bulb-replacement confusion.
judge_comment: A glowing cavity coating barely affects operation simplicity and would struggle in a microwave environment.

title: MagneticRollerlessTray
new_elements: A48MagneticRollerlessTray (Magnetic levitation track replaces roller ring, coupler, and motor.); A48FloatingSilentRotation (Rotation is silent and needs no tray alignment.)
rationale: A floating tray removes rattling parts and alignment steps that confuse beginners.
judge_comment: Maglev tray is radical, but it adds cost and complexity and only marginally helps ease of use.

title: SmartDoorHandleThermal
new_elements: A49SmartDoorHandleThermal (Heated door handle replaces lamp and bell as readiness cue.); A49TouchWarmReady (Touching the handle tells readiness without looking for sound or light.)
rationale: A warm handle gives one tactile cue instead of learning multiple light and bell states.
judge_comment: A warm handle gives a simple tactile readiness cue, but it is a safety concern and addresses only one part of operation.

title: UniversalCookingCap
new_elements: A50UniversalCookingCap (Sensored food cap replaces cavity controls by containing heat and steam.); A50CapAutoCook (User closes the cap and cooking automatically completes.)
rationale: The cap on the food becomes the intuitive interface, removing microwave-specific controls.
judge_comment: A sensor cap that auto-cooks when closed is an intuitive, radical interface, though it demands heavy engineering and has microwave-safety challenges.

title: 01 Single Start Button
new_elements: SingleCookButton01 (One large start button with no timer or power dial.); OneTouchStart01 (Starts a default safe cooking cycle from a single press.)
rationale: One press removes timer and power choices so first-time users learn nothing.
judge_comment: Very simple and easy to learn, but a single default cycle is rarely right for all foods and similar one-button microwaves already exist.

title: 02 Food-Shaped Preset Keys
new_elements: FoodShapedKeys02 (Physical buttons shaped like soup, drink, popcorn, and plate.); PresetFoodTouch02 (Pressing a food shape starts its matching safe preset.)
rationale: Users operate by recognizing the food rather than reading numbers or menus.
judge_comment: Recognizing food shapes is intuitive and easy to build, though fixed presets limit flexibility and the concept is incremental.

title: 03 Dish Sensor Slot
new_elements: DishSensorSlot03 (Slot that reads an RFID or shape tag embedded in the dish.); AutoDishTime03 (Assigns time and power automatically from the dish identity.)
rationale: The dish becomes the control so the user never has to set anything.
judge_comment: Dish-as-control removes all settings, but it requires special tagged dishes and RFID near the microwave cavity, which is a practical barrier.

title: 04 Weight Sensing Turntable
new_elements: WeightTurntable04 (Turntable with load cells that estimate food mass.); MassBasedTiming04 (Calculates cooking time from the measured load.)
rationale: A simple close-door-and-start action replaces manual time guessing.
judge_comment: Load cells are plausible and remove time guessing, but mass alone doesn't capture food type, so the cook result is imprecise.

title: 05 Steam Stop Sensor
new_elements: SteamStopSensor05 (Humidity and steam sensor inside the cavity.); SteamCompletionStop05 (Stops cooking when steam indicates the food is done.)
rationale: The microwave finishes by sensing the food, not by the user setting a time.
judge_comment: Steam sensing is proven in sensor-cook models and gives true close-and-go use, though it is not very radical.

title: 06 Close Door to Cook
new_elements: DoorCloseAutoStart06 (Sensor that begins cooking as soon as the door closes.); CloseToCook06 (Turns closing the door into the only operating action.)
rationale: Users understand door closing immediately, so there is no control to learn.
judge_comment: Closing the door as the only action is very intuitive, but it risks accidental starts (especially when empty) and gives no control over time or power.

title: 07 Color Detent Knob
new_elements: ColorDetentKnob07 (Knob with colored clicks but no printed times or power steps.); ColorOnlyStart07 (Selects a safe preset using color instead of numbers.)
rationale: A color click is easier than interpreting minutes and power percentages.
judge_comment: Color-coded detents are simple to build, but users must still learn what each color means, and the knob offers little precision.

title: 08 One Power Switch
new_elements: OnePowerSwitch08 (Simple two-position switch labeled full or soft.); FullOrSoft08 (Collapses five power steps into one intuitive choice.)
rationale: Fewer choices make the first operation obvious and reduce learning.
judge_comment: A full/soft switch is easy to build and understand, but it is an obvious simplification with no timing solution.

title: 09 Voice Hot Command
new_elements: VoiceHotCommand09 (Microphone that accepts one word such as hot or go.); SingleVoiceStart09 (Starts a default cycle from one spoken command.)
rationale: A natural single-word command is simpler than dialing settings.
judge_comment: A single spoken word is easy to use, but noisy kitchens, a default cycle that suits only some foods, and a microphone's cost and privacy concerns weaken it.

title: 10 Phone Tap Start
new_elements: PhoneTapStart10 (NFC or wireless receiver near the door.); TapToWarm10 (A phone tap launches the default cooking cycle.)
rationale: A tap gesture is already familiar and needs no appliance-specific learning.
judge_comment: Requiring a phone adds a step and a dependency, which is arguably harder than pressing a button, and the benefit is marginal.

title: 11 NFC Tag Container
new_elements: NFCTagContainer11 (Reusable tag attached to common food containers.); TagDefinedCooking11 (Tag tells the microwave the best preset for that container.)
rationale: The container carries the instructions so the user does not learn them.
judge_comment: Tags on containers let the microwave pick the preset automatically, though users must buy and attach tags and the method assumes consistent food in each container.

title: 12 QR Sticker Start
new_elements: QRStickerStart12 (Scanning surface that reads printed QR labels.); ScanToCook12 (QR code directly maps food to time and power.)
rationale: Reading one label is easier than remembering menu steps.
judge_comment: Scanning a QR label is easy to build, but it adds a step and a scanning action, so it is not truly zero-learning.

title: 13 Barcode Door Reader
new_elements: BarcodeDoorReader13 (Barcode scanner built into the door frame.); PackagedFoodAutoStart13 (Recognizes frozen or convenience packs and starts them.)
rationale: Food packaging becomes the instruction so no new skill is required.
judge_comment: Reading the barcode on packaged food is practical and removes input, but it only covers packaged items and is similar to existing smart-appliance ideas.

title: 14 RFID Tray
new_elements: RFIDTray14 (Tray with embedded RFID that detects the loaded food type.); TrayCookingProfile14 (Loads the correct cooking profile without manual input.)
rationale: Users only place and close, which is already intuitive.
judge_comment: Place-and-close is intuitive, but RFID in a tray only detects tagged items and does not identify arbitrary food, and it has to cope with heat and microwave fields.

title: 15 Thermal Camera
new_elements: ThermalCamera15 (Infrared camera that watches food surface temperature.); SurfaceTempStop15 (Ends cooking when the food reaches its expected hot state.)
rationale: The appliance judges doneness, so users need not learn times.
judge_comment: Thermal sensing that judges doneness removes the need to learn times and is the most radical, though surface-only readings and the camera in a microwave cavity pose challenges.

title: 16 Transparent Cavity
new_elements: TransparentCavity16 (Clear microwave-safe shell replacing opaque walls and interior lamp.); NoLightView16 (Shows the food directly without a dedicated viewing light.)
rationale: Direct visibility reduces the need to interpret indicators or open the door.
judge_comment: A transparent cavity doesn't simplify operation much, and a see-through shell would leak microwaves unless it had a shielding mesh, so it is barely feasible.

title: 17 Webcam AI Done
new_elements: WebcamAIDone17 (Internal camera plus classifier recognizing common dishes.); SeeInsideAuto17 (Starts or stops based on what the camera sees.)
rationale: Users point to food instead of choosing settings.
judge_comment: A camera that recognizes the food and picks the cooking program removes nearly all learning, and similar products already exist, though the concept is not very detailed.

title: 18 Aroma Sensor
new_elements: AromaSensor18 (Gas sensor tuned to burnt or done food scents.); SmellDone18 (Stops or adjusts the cycle based on aroma.)
rationale: Smell is a natural doneness signal that the machine can interpret.
judge_comment: Gas sensors that detect doneness or burning are real, and automatic stopping removes the need for settings, but they are less reliable for judging doneness than for detecting burning.

title: 19 Moisture Probe
new_elements: MoistureProbe19 (Simple probe that reads food moisture during cooking.); ProbeAutoStop19 (Ends the cycle when moisture reaches a target.)
rationale: The user inserts one item and the probe carries the complexity.
judge_comment: Probes can't be used safely inside a microwave cavity because metal arcs, and having the user insert one adds a step, so the idea is only moderately useful.

title: 20 Turntable Cycle Timer
new_elements: TurntableCycleTimer20 (Sensor that counts turntable revolutions as the time source.); RotationCountTimer20 (Replaces a separate clock with motion counting.)
rationale: Using motion to stop the appliance removes a separate dial to understand.
judge_comment: Counting turntable revolutions as a timer is quirky and cheap, but the user still has to set a duration, so it doesn't simplify operation.

title: 21 Push Pop Knob
new_elements: PushPopKnob21 (Knob that pushes in to start and pops out when done.); PopUpTimer21 (Makes the physical pop the only status signal.)
rationale: One push and a pop are more intuitive than reading numbers.
judge_comment: A push-in, pop-out knob is intuitive and mechanically simple, but a pop as the only status signal and no duration control limit it.

title: 22 Haptic Twist Start
new_elements: HapticTwistStart22 (Single knob with force feedback but no display.); TwistToCook22 (One twist starts a safe adaptive cycle.)
rationale: The gesture feels familiar and does not require menu knowledge.
judge_comment: A single twist is familiar, but the 'safe adaptive cycle' is vague and needs sensing that isn't specified.

title: 23 Done Light Ring
new_elements: DoneLightRing23 (Colored ring around the door that changes when cooking ends.); ColorDoneCue23 (Replaces text and bells with one simple color signal.)
rationale: A color change needs almost no explanation.
judge_comment: A done-light ring is easy to build and understand, but it only covers the end signal, not operation.

title: 24 Shape Recognition Drop
new_elements: ShapeRecognitionDrop24 (Camera and classifier that recognizes cup, plate, or bowl shapes.); DropToCook24 (Sets cooking mode from the food container shape.)
rationale: Recognizing common shapes is easier than configuring the appliance.
judge_comment: Camera-based shape recognition removes setup but adds cost and complexity, and shape doesn't determine food or time.

title: 25 Picture Dial
new_elements: PictureDial25 (Dial with photos of common foods instead of minutes.); PicturePresetCooking25 (Starts the correct recipe by selecting a picture.)
rationale: Pictures are faster to understand than technical controls.
judge_comment: A picture dial is clear and practical, but food-picture presets are an established idea with limited coverage.

title: 26 Big Red Button
new_elements: BigRedButton26 (Oversized single start button for children and older users.); AccessibilityOnePress26 (One press triggers a safe default.)
rationale: A large obvious button removes almost all learning.
judge_comment: A big start button is simple and effective for usability but is an obvious, non-radical change with little substitution of parts.

title: 27 Sensor Fusion Done
new_elements: SensorFusionDone27 (Combines temperature, steam, weight, and camera signals.); MultiSenseCompletion27 (Decides doneness automatically.)
rationale: Sensing replaces manual timing and tuning.
judge_comment: Multi-sensor auto-doneness removes the need for any input, but it is costly and complex and not a cheaper substitution.

title: 28 Last Memory Start
new_elements: LastMemoryStart28 (Small memory module storing the last successful preset.); RecallDefaultStart28 (Restarts the previous good setting with one action.)
rationale: Repeating a known success is easier than setting anything new.
judge_comment: Last-setting recall is cheap and easy to build but only helps on repeat use, so it is not truly zero-learning.

title: 29 User Calibrated Time
new_elements: UserCalibratedTime29 (Learns from accepted results for a household profile.); LearnedUserTiming29 (Adapts presets to the household without new input.)
rationale: The user chooses once and the machine handles later decisions.
judge_comment: A household-learned profile reduces future decisions, but the mechanism is vague and the first use still needs input.

title: 30 Adaptive Duty
new_elements: AdaptiveDuty30 (Magnetron driver that adjusts power automatically.); AutoPowerTuning30 (Removes manual power selection.)
rationale: Automatic power tuning replaces a confusing multi-step control.
judge_comment: Auto power tuning removes the power-level choice and is plausible, but it is a modest and fairly well-known change.

title: 31 Palm Wave Door
new_elements: PalmWaveDoor31 (Infrared sensor that opens the door with a hand wave.); WaveToOpen31 (Replaces a button or handle with a natural gesture.)
rationale: A hand wave is easy to try and needs no labels.
judge_comment: Wave-to-open is easy to grasp and technically simple, but it only covers opening the door, not setting time or power, and it adds a sensor rather than substituting a cheaper part.

title: 32 Handle Start Tag
new_elements: HandleStartTag32 (Detachable handle tag that triggers cooking when tapped.); HandleTapStart32 (Uses the door handle as the only switch.)
rationale: The handle already attracts the user hand so starting becomes obvious.
judge_comment: Using the handle as the single start trigger removes controls and is intuitive, but cook time and power are left undefined and a detachable tag could get lost.

title: 33 Lamp Ring Status
new_elements: LampRingStatus33 (Ambient ring light showing running or finished.); AmbientCookingStatus33 (Communicates state without text or dials.)
rationale: Light status is immediately understandable.
judge_comment: An ambient light ring is simple and easy to build, but it only shows status, is common, and doesn't replace an input control.

title: 34 Hourglass Insert
new_elements: HourglassInsert34 (Slot that reads a physical hourglass duration.); HourglassTime34 (Sets time from a familiar object instead of controls.)
rationale: People already understand an hourglass as a time signal.
judge_comment: Using a physical hourglass to set time is a wild but intuitive substitution for a dial, though reading arbitrary hourglasses is awkward and it offers limited time options.

title: 35 Pop-Up Plate
new_elements: PopUpPlate35 (Turntable that rises slightly when cooking ends.); PlateRiseDone35 (Turns doneness into a physical surprise.)
rationale: A visible pop-up explains completion without instructions.
judge_comment: A plate that rises when cooking ends signals completion physically, but it adds mechanical complexity and does nothing for input.

title: 36 Magnetic Turntable
new_elements: MagneticTurntable36 (Magnetic drive that rotates food without manual adjustment.); AutoRotationNoSettings36 (Provides consistent rotation automatically.)
rationale: Automatic consistent motion removes another thing users must manage.
judge_comment: Turntables already rotate automatically, so a magnetic drive barely changes the user's operation and is only a minor substitution.

title: 37 Frozen Preloaded Mode
new_elements: FrozenPreloadedMode37 (Front drawer loaded with known frozen meals.); OneButtonFrozenStart37 (Starts the selected meal with one button.)
rationale: The food library does the thinking so operation stays trivial.
judge_comment: A preloaded frozen-meal drawer with one-button start strongly reduces operation effort, though it limits food variety and the mechanism is vague.

title: 38 Foot Pedal Start
new_elements: FootPedalStart38 (Pedal that starts or stops cooking.); HandsFreeStart38 (Makes starting a simple step.)
rationale: A step is one of the easiest actions to teach.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is easy to build but replaces a button with something no simpler, and it does not remove the need to set time or power.

title: 39 Thermochromic Plate
new_elements: ThermochromicPlate39 (Plate with color-changing rim detected by a sensor.); PlateColorStop39 (Uses plate color to decide when to stop.)
rationale: A color-changing surface is simpler than reading a dial.
judge_comment: A color-changing plate that signals when to stop is inventive, but it needs special plates and the sensing is unreliable in a microwave.

title: 40 Cup Volume Sensor
new_elements: CupVolumeSensor40 (Optical sensor that estimates liquid volume.); AutoDrinkVolume40 (Automatically sets time for a cup.)
rationale: For drinks, placing a cup can replace all manual settings.
judge_comment: Placing a cup and having the microwave set the time removes all settings for drinks, but the scope is narrow and optical volume sensing is imperfect.

title: 41 Bag Pouch Reader
new_elements: BagPouchReader41 (Reader that recognizes pre-scored microwave pouches.); PouchAutoStart41 (Reads the pouch and launches its cycle.)
rationale: The pouch tells the machine what to do so users need no training.
judge_comment: A pouch-reading auto-start (barcode or RFID) is plausible and cuts the learning curve, though it only works for compatible pouches and is not radically new.

title: 42 Touch Door Frame
new_elements: TouchDoorFrame42 (Capacitive frame around the door.); TouchToOpen42 (Opens the door with a simple touch anywhere on the frame.)
rationale: A large touch area is easier than finding a small button.
judge_comment: A touch-to-open door frame is easy to build but only simplifies opening, not cooking operation, and it is a weak substitution.

title: 43 Presence Auto Start
new_elements: PresenceAutoStart43 (Combines food detection and user presence sensing.); PresenceBasedStart43 (Starts the intended mode without pressing anything.)
rationale: If the appliance senses the situation, the user has nothing to learn.
judge_comment: Zero-input auto-start would remove the learning curve, but inferring intent reliably is hard and unintended starts are a safety risk; the mechanism is vague.

title: 44 Gesture Ring Start
new_elements: GestureRingStart44 (Wearable ring that sends a start signal.); GestureRingCook44 (Starts the microwave with a gesture.)
rationale: The gesture can be repeated instantly without studying controls.
judge_comment: A wearable ring adds a device to learn, pair and own, which works against the no-learning-curve goal.

title: 45 Scent Card Preset
new_elements: ScentCardPreset45 (Odor-coded cards representing common foods.); ScentCardAuto45 (Inserting a card launches its food preset.)
rationale: A card is a single-object control that avoids menus.
judge_comment: A single-object card control is simple, but odor coding is odd and unreliable, and a plain RFID card would do the job better.

title: 46 Smart Plate Rim
new_elements: SmartPlateRim46 (Conductive rim that signals plate type to sensors.); PlateRimCookStart46 (The plate itself defines the cooking mode.)
rationale: The object the user already holds becomes the interface.
judge_comment: Plate rim signaling cook mode removes controls and substitutes the plate for the interface, though microwave-safe conductive rims are a real technical hurdle.

title: 47 Package Thermochip
new_elements: PackageThermochip47 (Temperature-sensitive chip on food packages.); ThermalChipAuto47 (Reads package readiness and stops cooking.)
rationale: The package knows when it is done, so the user does not need to.
judge_comment: Package-embedded thermal chips that stop cooking automatically eliminate user input, and similar smart-package concepts are plausible but need ecosystem adoption.

title: 48 Soft Done Cue
new_elements: SoftDoneCue48 (Vibration and glow instead of a sharp bell.); GentleDoneCue48 (Signals completion in a calm obvious way.)
rationale: A simple gentle cue helps first users understand finishing without reading a display.
judge_comment: A gentler completion cue is easy to build but only marginally addresses operation simplicity.

title: 49 Control-Free Shell
new_elements: ControlFreeShell49 (Appliance front without visible buttons, dials, or screens.); ControlFreeStart49 (Operation is fully carried by food, tag, or gesture.)
rationale: If there is nothing to look at, there is nothing to learn.
judge_comment: Removing all visible controls is radical, but it risks discoverability problems and the operation mechanism is vague.

title: 50 Self-Learning Defaults
new_elements: SelfLearningDefaults50 (Tiny model that records accepted outcomes.); LearnedDefaultStart50 (Turns past success into the next automatic default.)
rationale: The appliance becomes easier with use instead of requiring training.
judge_comment: Learned defaults reduce effort over time, but the first use still needs setup and the mechanism is loosely defined.

title: I01 Squeeze Shell
new_elements: Pressure-sensitive microwave shell (Soft conductive skin around the body that detects a single squeeze.); Squeeze-to-cook operation (One squeeze starts a default short heat cycle.)
rationale: Replaces buttons and knobs with a pressure skin, so a single squeeze starts cooking with no learning curve.
judge_comment: A single squeeze is very simple, but accidental activation, safety concerns and a fixed default cycle limit it; a soft skin is also awkward on a microwave body.

title: I02 Door-Only Start
new_elements: Door magnet control module (Magnetic door sensor that treats opening and closing as the only controls.); Open-close cook operation (Opening selects mode and closing starts heat.)
rationale: Replaces the door button, timer, and power knobs with door actions, so users only need to open and close.
judge_comment: Door-only control is cheap and feasible, but how opening 'selects mode' works is unclear and could add a learning curve.

title: I03 RFID Tray Cook
new_elements: RFID tray sensor (Reader under the turntable detects encoded food trays.); Tag-to-recipe operation (The tray tag automatically chooses time and power.)
rationale: Replaces manual dial settings with a tray RFID, so placing food and closing door starts the correct program.
judge_comment: Tag-driven programs remove settings entirely and RFID is cheap, but it only works with proprietary tagged trays, which limits general use.

title: I04 Gesture Halo
new_elements: Gesture camera and IR emitter (Small camera above the door that recognizes hand waves.); Wave-to-program operation (One wave starts a default heat cycle.)
rationale: Replaces knobs with a universal gesture, so users start cooking without reading labels.
judge_comment: A wave is intuitive, but it is discoverability-dependent, offers only a default cycle, and the camera adds cost and privacy concerns.

title: I05 Steam-and-Weight Auto
new_elements: Weight and steam sensor (Scale plus humidity detector infers food state.); Food-state auto operation (Microwave starts and stops based on food condition.)
rationale: Replaces user timing with sensing, so the food itself decides when heating is complete.
judge_comment: Having food state decide the cook time removes all user input, though reliable doneness detection across foods is hard and sensor-based auto-cook already exists.

title: I06 NFC Cook Card
new_elements: NFC cooking card reader (Reader on door edge accepts simple recipe cards.); Card-tap operation (Tapping a card sets the cooking program.)
rationale: Replaces time and power knobs with one tap of a card, so the recipe is selected by physical touch.
judge_comment: Tap-a-card is simple and easy to build with NFC, but it requires owning cards and is limited to preset recipes.

title: I07 QR Plate Scan
new_elements: QR label scanner (Small scanner inside door frame reads plate or package QR codes.); Scan-to-heat operation (QR code selects default time and power.)
rationale: Replaces manual settings with a scanned food label, so users do not learn the microwave.
judge_comment: Scanning package codes removes settings entirely, but it depends on packaged foods carrying compatible codes and a scanner that works with steam and splatter.

title: I08 Color Preset Ring
new_elements: Color-preset ring encoder (Physical ring with colors instead of numbers or power levels.); Color-dial operation (Selecting a color chooses a simple preset mode.)
rationale: Replaces clock and 5-step power knobs with one color choice, reducing comprehension to visual matching.
judge_comment: Color presets are easy to understand but resemble existing preset buttons, and they offer little control or meaning without labels.

title: I09 Pull-Cord Minutes
new_elements: Pull-cord mechanical timer (Lamp-style cord where each pull adds one minute.); Pull-to-set operation (Number of pulls equals minutes.)
rationale: Replaces electronic controls with a familiar pull action, so setting time feels like turning on a light.
judge_comment: A pull-cord that adds a minute per pull is instantly familiar and mechanically simple, though it has no power control and is awkward for long times.

title: I10 Handle Squeeze Power
new_elements: Squeeze handle variable actuator (Door handle with pressure and duration sensing.); Handle-pressure cooking operation (Harder or longer squeeze selects more cooking.)
rationale: Replaces separate power and time controls with one intuitive hand action.
judge_comment: Squeeze-to-cook is radical and a single gesture, but it is imprecise, tiring for long cooks, and raises safety concerns.

title: I11 Smart Plug Only
new_elements: Smart plug trigger relay (Microwave has no controls, only a smart outlet trigger.); Remote schedule operation (External timer starts and stops power.)
rationale: Replaces microwave controls with a simple power switch, so operation is learned once outside the appliance.
judge_comment: A smart plug with no controls is technically easy, but it moves complexity to an app and gives no power-level or time control, so it arguably adds a learning curve.

title: I12 Smart Cooking Bag
new_elements: Smart cooking bag seal (Sealed bag with heat-response indicator and sensor contact.); Bag-triggered cook operation (Bag contact starts and stops the cycle.)
rationale: Replaces user timing with the cooking bag itself, so the food package controls the process.
judge_comment: A package that dictates the cook cycle removes user decisions, and it is plausible with smart-packaging tags, though the bag's sensor contact is vague.

title: I13 Food Slot Classifier
new_elements: Food slot classifier (Shape and material sensors in a narrow loading slot.); Insert-slot cooking operation (Food shape selects a preset cook time.)
rationale: Replaces knob choices with a physical slot, so putting food in is also the program selection.
judge_comment: Inserting food to auto-select a program is intuitive, but classifying food by shape and material in a slot is unreliable and a poor fit for a microwave cavity.

title: I14 Face Profile Cook
new_elements: Face recognition camera (Door camera identifies regular users.); User-profile cook operation (Recognized user launches their preferred preset.)
rationale: Replaces manual settings with recognition, so each user simply appears and the microwave defaults.
judge_comment: Face recognition removes setup for repeat users, but it raises privacy concerns, needs enrollment, and fails for guests or varied foods.

title: I15 Foot Start
new_elements: Foot pedal start switch (Low-force pedal starts default cooking.); Foot-start operation (Foot press replaces all buttons.)
rationale: Replaces the door button and controls with a simple foot press, useful when hands are occupied.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is simple, cheap, and easy to build and helps with full hands, but a single default cook doesn't handle varied foods.

title: I16 Tap Turntable Start
new_elements: Turntable tap sensor (Capacitive glass that detects plate taps.); Tap-to-start operation (Tapping the plate starts default heating.)
rationale: Replaces control panel buttons with tapping the food plate, making cooking feel direct.
judge_comment: Tapping the plate to start is intuitive and removes buttons, though the default heating setting is ambiguous and a capacitive sensor on a rotating glass plate is awkward to build.

title: I17 Say Heat
new_elements: Single-word voice module (Microphone that only understands one command: heat.); Say-heat operation (Voice command starts simple preset cooking.)
rationale: Replaces multi-knob operation with one word, so there is almost no learning required.
judge_comment: A single-word voice command has almost no learning curve and is easy to build, but voice control on microwaves already exists and noise and a fixed preset limit it.

title: I18 Bioluminescent Glow
new_elements: Bioluminescent glow cell (Passive glow panel replaces the interior bulb.); Bulb-free visibility operation (Interior is visible without lamp control.)
rationale: Replaces the lamp with passive glow, removing a component and a possible user question.
judge_comment: A bioluminescent glow only removes a bulb, does little for operation simplicity, and is impractical for lifespan and brightness.

title: I19 Transparent Microwave
new_elements: Fully transparent casing (Whole body made of see-through RF-shielded material.); See-through cook operation (User can watch food without lights or holes.)
rationale: Replaces light and door window complexity with the whole cabinet, making status instantly visible.
judge_comment: A fully transparent RF-shielded body is radical, but it is physically implausible and does not simplify operation.

title: I20 Webcam Window
new_elements: Interior webcam feed (Small camera sends interior view to phone or screen.); Camera-window visibility operation (Remote image replaces direct window inspection.)
rationale: Replaces the interior lamp and holes with a camera, so checking food becomes a simple glance on a screen.
judge_comment: A camera feed is feasible, but it adds a phone or screen and complexity, which works against a no-learning-curve goal.

title: I21 Magnetic Slider
new_elements: Magnetic slider power encoder (Single sliding magnet replaces 5-step power knob.); Single-slide power operation (Slide position chooses simple power level.)
rationale: Replaces the 5-step knob with one slide, reducing settings to a single obvious motion.
judge_comment: A simple slider is easy to use and cheap, but it only simplifies power selection and still needs time input, so it is not radical.

title: I22 Steam Done Stop
new_elements: Done-steam detector (Vapor sensor stops cooking when steam pattern changes.); Auto-done operation (Microwave turns off when food appears ready.)
rationale: Replaces the timer bell and user stop decision with steam detection, so no manual finish is needed.
judge_comment: Steam-based auto-stop removes the need to choose a time and fits the no-learning-curve goal; humidity sensors already exist in some models, but they are reasonably reliable.

title: I23 Container Aware
new_elements: Container material detector (Sensing shelf identifies microwave-safe containers.); Container-aware cooking operation (Container type selects safe power and time.)
rationale: Replaces user guessing with container sensing, so simple operation means just placing the dish.
judge_comment: Container sensing removes a safety worry, but reliably identifying container material is hard and it doesn't set cook time.

title: I24 Meal Clock Auto
new_elements: Clock-based auto mode (Real-time clock chooses meal presets.); Meal-time auto operation (Time of day selects default heating.)
rationale: Replaces manual programming with clock context, so users act based on natural mealtime cues.
judge_comment: Using time of day to pick a preset is easy to build, but it guesses at what the user wants and often gets it wrong.

title: I25 Plate Size Sensor
new_elements: Plate-size optical sensor (Camera or light grid measures food footprint.); Plate-size cook operation (Larger plates get longer default heating.)
rationale: Replaces time entry with plate size, because users can intuitively see how much food is there.
judge_comment: Plate footprint is an intuitive input, but size says little about food type or density, so heating results would be unreliable.

title: I26 One Push Auto Stop
new_elements: Auto-stop push button (Single big button starts and decides stop.); One-push cook operation (Button press begins auto cook.)
rationale: Replaces multiple knobs with one obvious button, removing all menu navigation.
judge_comment: Single-button auto-cook is very simple to use and easy to build, but it is not radical and the auto-stop mechanism is vague.

title: I27 Smart Glove Tap
new_elements: Smart cooking glove reader (Reader detects tap from simple cooking gloves.); Glove-touch operation (Glove tap starts preset heating.)
rationale: Replaces knobs with tapping using existing kitchen gloves, so the body language is already familiar.
judge_comment: Needing special gloves adds a new object to learn and use, and it is unclear what the glove tap does beyond starting a preset.

title: I28 Food Photo Recognizer
new_elements: External food photo classifier (Door camera identifies common food shapes.); Photo-to-cook operation (Food image selects preset time and power.)
rationale: Replaces manual settings with visual recognition, so users just point the door at the food.
judge_comment: A door camera that recognizes the food and picks settings removes all input and is feasible, though it is error-prone and similar products already exist.

title: I29 Phone Control Relay
new_elements: Phone-only control relay (Microwave has no local controls and only accepts phone commands.); No-panel cooking operation (Phone sets one preset and relay executes it.)
rationale: Replaces microwave panel with phone UI, so users do not learn a second control system.
judge_comment: Phone-only control is easy to build but adds an app and pairing step and fails when the phone is unavailable, which works against zero learning curve.

title: I30 Kitchen Mat Sensor
new_elements: Kitchen mat pressure network (Mat outside microwave detects plate placement.); Mat-place operation (Putting plate on mat starts default cook.)
rationale: Replaces door controls with a natural kitchen habit, so preparing food also triggers the microwave.
judge_comment: Starting the cook when a plate is placed on a mat is a creative zero-interaction idea, but it risks false triggers and it is unclear how the mat knows the food is inside the microwave.

title: I31 Scale Turntable
new_elements: Integrated turntable scale (Turntable measures food mass.); Weight-only cook operation (Mass sets a single default heating time.)
rationale: Replaces manual time and power with scale data, so the food amount alone decides operation.
judge_comment: Weight-based auto time removes input and is plausible with a load cell, though a single default time per mass is crude and ignores food type.

title: I32 Door Angle Power
new_elements: Door-angle potentiometer (Sensor measures how far the door is opened.); Swing-angle power operation (Small opening means low heat, wide opening means high heat.)
rationale: Replaces the 5-step power knob with door motion, because opening wide is a bodily metaphor for more.
judge_comment: Door angle as a power control is quirky and cheap to build, but it is unintuitive, hard to control precisely and probably adds a learning curve.

title: I33 Vibration Alert Pad
new_elements: Silent vibration alert pad (Soft pad under microwave vibrates gently at completion.); Quiet completion operation (Vibration replaces bell and display.)
rationale: Replaces the mechanical bell with a tactile signal, making finished status obvious without interpretation.
judge_comment: A vibration pad makes completion obvious, but it addresses only the end signal and not how the microwave is operated.

title: I34 Hourglass Light
new_elements: Hourglass light animation (Light dots fall through a tube instead of digital numbers.); Visual countdown operation (Countdown is perceived as sand-like motion.)
rationale: Replaces clockwork numbers with a familiar hourglass metaphor, so remaining time is instantly readable.
judge_comment: An hourglass light makes remaining time easy to read, but it only helps the display and does nothing for setting up a cook.

title: I35 Habit Learner
new_elements: Daily pattern learner (Local timer learns repeated cook events.); Habit auto operation (Microwave suggests or starts usual preset at usual times.)
rationale: Replaces manual settings with habit detection, so the user can simply return to their normal routine.
judge_comment: Learning habits could remove settings for routine use, but it fails on first use, risks unattended starts, and gives few details on the mechanism.

title: I36 Open Door Trigger
new_elements: Open-door cooking trigger (Opening door with food inside arms a one-heat cycle.); Open-to-heat operation (Door opening replaces button press for a preset mode.)
rationale: Replaces the start button with the natural act of opening the door, so no separate control step exists.
judge_comment: Opening the door to start is intuitive and removes a step, but it is awkward and potentially unsafe since the door must be opened to load food, so triggering heat on opening is confusing.

title: I37 Barcode Can Scanner
new_elements: Barcode can scanner (Reader scans common food-can barcodes.); Scan-can operation (Barcode selects preset heat time.)
rationale: Replaces knob settings with product codes already present on food packaging.
judge_comment: Barcode scanning is feasible and cheap, but it only covers canned foods and needs a database, which adds a step rather than removing one.

title: I38 Thermal Stop Camera
new_elements: Thermal camera stopper (Low-cost IR camera measures surface temperature.); Temperature-stop operation (Microwave stops when target warmth is reached.)
rationale: Replaces manual timing with direct temperature sensing, so users do not learn time-to-food mappings.
judge_comment: Temperature-based stopping removes any need to know times and is plausible with low-res IR sensors, though it only measures the surface and the user still has to start it.

title: I39 Self-closing steam vent
new_elements: Self-closing steam vent (Mechanical vent closes when steam drops.); Vent-done operation (Vent closure signals completion and stops power.)
rationale: Replaces bell and timer with a mechanical steam cue, so readiness is indicated by the food itself.
judge_comment: A mechanical steam cue is creative and cheap, but it works only for foods that steam and stopping power mechanically is unreliable.

title: I40 Traffic Light LED
new_elements: Two-color LED ring (Red means not ready, green means start.); Traffic-light operation (Color status replaces dial and display settings.)
rationale: Replaces numerical settings with universal red-green cues, making operation understandable instantly.
judge_comment: A red-green LED is simple and easy to build, but it merely signals status and doesn't set heating parameters, so it doesn't replace the controls.

title: I41 Magnetic Pull Handle
new_elements: Magnetic pull handle (Handle magnet detects pulling motion as both open and start.); Pull-cook operation (Pulling handle arms or begins simple heating.)
rationale: Replaces the push-release button with pulling, combining door use and control use into one action.
judge_comment: Pulling the handle to open and start in one action is intuitive and plausible, though it risks accidental starts and the cooking time or power is unclear.

title: I42 Solar Thermal Start
new_elements: Solar-thermal heat converter (Simple collector supplies a basic heat source instead of electrical controls.); Sun-start operation (Light presence starts a default warm cycle.)
rationale: Replaces electrical control complexity with a radical passive heat trigger, reducing operation to placement and waiting.
judge_comment: Solar heating is wildly impractical and no longer a microwave, and it depends on weather, so it does not deliver simple operation.

title: I43 Fridge Link
new_elements: Fridge companion link (Microwave receives simple cook requests from smart fridge.); Fridge-told cook operation (Fridge selects what should be heated.)
rationale: Replaces microwave settings with fridge intelligence, so the user only follows the fridge prompt.
judge_comment: The fridge could remove the need for settings, but it requires a smart fridge and adds dependency and complexity rather than substituting a simpler part.

title: I44 Handle RFID Tap
new_elements: Handle RFID tap (Handle contains passive RFID target for tap-based starting.); Tap-handle operation (Tapping handle starts default mode.)
rationale: Replaces knobs and buttons with one tap location users already reach for.
judge_comment: RFID tap start is feasible and simple, but it merely replaces a button with a tap and the default mode may not suit all foods.

title: I45 Container Shape Sensor
new_elements: Container-shape capacitive sensor (Shelf senses bowl, mug, or plate shape.); Shape-aware cook operation (Container shape chooses a preset program.)
rationale: Replaces manual selection with shape sensing, because users naturally choose containers by food type.
judge_comment: Auto-selecting a program from container shape removes the need for settings, but capacitive sensing of shape is unreliable and shape poorly predicts the food.

title: I46 Proximity Beacon
new_elements: Kitchen proximity beacon (Phone or wearable beacon detects approach.); Walk-up auto operation (Approach arms a simple default heat mode.)
rationale: Replaces control input with presence, so arriving is the only action required.
judge_comment: Presence-triggered default heating removes input, but safety risks, unclear food loading, and false triggers undermine it, and details are thin.

title: I47 Cold Plate Stop
new_elements: Cold-plate detection stop (Senses plate temperature change to infer warming progress.); Coldness-based operation (Stops heating when expected temperature shift occurs.)
rationale: Replaces the timer with a physical temperature cue, so users can stop worrying about exact minutes.
judge_comment: Stopping on a temperature cue removes timer guesswork, but sensing plate temperature inside a microwave and inferring doneness is unreliable and vague.

title: I48 Touch Talk Button
new_elements: One-touch voice button (Large button says what will happen when pressed.); Touch-talk operation (Touch confirms simple preset before starting.)
rationale: Replaces screen menus with a button that speaks instructions, so users do not have to decode labels.
judge_comment: A talking one-touch button is easy to build and genuinely lowers the learning curve, though it is an incremental idea.

title: I49 Static Heated Floor
new_elements: Static heated floor (Fixed hot floor replaces rotating turntable.); No-turntable cook operation (Users place food anywhere and wait.)
rationale: Replaces the rotating turntable with a stationary cooking surface, removing the question of plate alignment.
judge_comment: A static heated floor removes alignment concerns but it is a different heating principle than microwaves, and does not really simplify operation.

title: I50 Cooking Pod Adapter
new_elements: Sealed cooking pod adapter (Pod holder receives microwave-ready pods.); Pod-cook operation (Pod insertion triggers the only cooking action.)
rationale: Replaces all control choices with a pod slot, so users only insert a food pod like a coffee machine.
judge_comment: A pod slot with automatic cooking eliminates choices entirely and is plausible via barcodes, though it needs an ecosystem of pods.

title: One-Pad Auto Cook
new_elements: OneBigStartPad (A single pressure-sensitive pad starts expert auto-cooking without time or power knobs.); AutoCookFromOnePress (Infers food type, mass, and doneness from a single user action.); MultiSensorFoodState (Combines load-cell mass, steam, and cavity acoustics to close the cooking loop.); FoodStateSensing (Field for measuring food condition inside an appliance.)
rationale: One press removes knob learning for elderly users.
judge_comment: A single press that infers food, mass, and doneness removes the learning curve almost entirely, but reliable sensing is hard and costly, and it is not really a cheaper substitution.

title: Hidden Power Knob
new_elements: TimeOnlyKnob (A single duration knob with no power setting; the machine chooses average power internally.); TimeOnlyCooking (User only needs to set or accept a time, not power.); InferredDutyCycle (Derives magnetron on/off ratio from door, cavity load, and acoustic feedback.)
rationale: Eliminates a second control step and hides power selection from the user.
judge_comment: A time-only knob is simple and plausible, but it is incremental, since many microwaves already work this way, and the inferred duty cycle adds little.

title: Tap-Once Timer
new_elements: TapToStartButton (A large button that starts a sensible default time with one tap.); DefaultCountdown (Provides a no-choice countdown start for common reheating.); MechanicalTapClock (A simple spring-return cam triggered by one push.)
rationale: One tap replaces dial setting and removes the time-learning step.
judge_comment: A one-tap default start is very easy to use and cheap to build, but a fixed default time is not very flexible and the idea is not radical.

title: Door-Twist Handle
new_elements: TwistHandleControl (A door handle that twists to set or start cooking instead of separate knobs.); DoorTwistCooking (Turns door-handle motion into time and power selection.); HandleTorqueSensing (Mechanically or electronically encodes handle twist into cooking settings.)
rationale: Puts operation on the door already being touched, reducing panel learning.
judge_comment: A twist handle is an unusual idea, but an unfamiliar control could add learning rather than remove it, and it makes the door mechanism more complex.

title: See-Through Cavity
new_elements: SeeThroughCavity (A microwave body with a fully visible cavity and no perforated observation holes.); WholeCavityVisibility (Lets the user inspect food from every angle without opening the door.); VisibleDoneCheck (Gives an obvious done/not-done cue from ordinary sight.); RFEdgeSeal (Edge-waveguide, gasket, or material structure that keeps radiation contained while the body stays transparent.)
rationale: Makes checking food trivial and avoids understanding small-window cues.
judge_comment: A fully transparent cavity makes checking food easy, but it does not simplify operation, and containing RF in a transparent body is difficult.

title: Phone-View Door
new_elements: WebcamDoor (Door replaces small visible holes and interior lamp with a camera stream to an external viewer.); ExternalViewCooking (Shows food state on a phone or big nearby display.); CameraDoneCheck (Provides a clearer view for deciding when cooking is finished.); LowPowerInteriorCam (A shielded, heat-tolerant camera for cavity observation.)
rationale: Provides an obvious view without requiring the user to understand microwave window shading.
judge_comment: A camera door helps check doneness but does not simplify operation, and a heat- and RF-tolerant camera is costly and awkward, and it requires a phone.

title: Sandglass Timer
new_elements: VisibleSandTimer (A transparent gravity-fed timer element that visually counts down.); NoGuessTime (Makes remaining time obvious without reading numbers.); GravityVisibleClock (Mechanical time indication using falling grains or beads.)
rationale: Turns time into something naturally understood by anyone watching it.
judge_comment: A sandglass is simple and intuitive to read, but it only shows time and does not remove the need to set it.

title: Weight-Trigger Shelf
new_elements: WeightTriggerShelf (Cavity shelf starts and times cooking from the food mass placed on it.); AutoTimeFromMass (Selects duration and power from weight and load category.); LoadCellCavityFloor (Mechanical or capacitive mass sensing inside the cavity.)
rationale: Places food and closes door, with no explicit time or power setting.
judge_comment: Weight-triggered auto-cooking directly removes settings, though weight alone is a poor guide to the right time and power for different foods.

title: Food-Token Slot
new_elements: FoodTokenSlot (A slot accepts physical tokens or tags that encode a reheating recipe.); TokenSetsCooking (Converts an inserted token into time and power settings.); MechanicalTokenEncoding (Uses token shape, depth, or notches to set simple cooking states.)
rationale: Users pick a food token instead of learning microwave numbers.
judge_comment: Physical tokens make selection simple and are easy to build mechanically, but they add accessories to keep and lose, and the token set limits what it can cook.

title: Color Cavity Zones
new_elements: ColorCavityZones (Colored nonmetal zones inside the cavity indicate food classes and preset power behavior.); ZoneChoosePower (Where food sits chooses the cooking mode.); MoldedRFSafeColorPanels (Cavity inserts that influence loading through visible, food-associated zones.)
rationale: Power becomes a spatial choice that matches common food colors and shapes.
judge_comment: Spatial zones choosing power is novel and intuitive in concept, but microwave field physics makes it implausible and the mechanism is vague.

title: One-Slide Timer
new_elements: SingleSlideTimer (A one-dimensional slider with detents for common times, replacing a rotary clock knob.); SlideToStartStop (Slide direction and detent start cooking without reading a circular scale.); LinearDetentCam (Linear mechanical cam with few positions for common reheating lengths.)
rationale: A slide matches intuitive start-stop motion and removes circular dial reading.
judge_comment: A linear detent slider is simple and intuitive, but it is an incremental swap for a rotary knob rather than a radical idea.

title: Done-by-Heat Switch
new_elements: DoneByHeatSwitch (A simple bimetal or heat switch stops cooking when a target temperature or gradient is reached.); TemperatureEndCooking (Ends time without requiring user-set duration.); BimetalCavitySensor (Mechanical heat sensing that acts as a simple end-of-cooking switch.)
rationale: Replaces learning time with a simple heat-stop behavior.
judge_comment: Removing time setting entirely would be a big gain in simplicity, but a bimetal switch can't reliably sense food temperature in a microwave cavity and could be unsafe.

title: Steam-Reveal Coating
new_elements: SteamRevealCoating (A door coating that becomes clear or colored as steam indicates food is hot enough.); CondensateDoneIndicator (Uses condensation or humidity change as a visible done cue.); HumidityReactingSurface (A material that changes transparency or hue based on moisture.)
rationale: The door shows doneness without requiring settings knowledge.
judge_comment: A door that signals doneness is a creative cue, but it is only an indicator and doesn't control operation, and a humidity-reactive coating on a door is questionable in practice.

title: Magnetic Door Latch
new_elements: MagnetLatchDoor (Door closes with soft magnets and opens with one hand by a pull or tap.); OneHandDoor (Removes push-button timing and latch learning.); SoftMagneticClosure (Low-force magnetic holding plus simple door actuation.)
rationale: Door operation becomes a single familiar open-or-close gesture.
judge_comment: A magnetic latch makes the door easier to use, but it barely addresses the learning curve for cooking operation and is not very radical.

title: Door-Angle Power
new_elements: AnglePowerHinge (Door opening angle controls power level without a separate knob.); PowerByDoorAngle (Small opening gives low power, wider opening gives different heating behavior.); PotentiometerHinge (Hinge position is mapped to duty-cycle settings.)
rationale: Uses the door action already in progress instead of a separate power control.
judge_comment: Setting power by door angle is novel, but it is unintuitive, which adds learning, and it conflicts with safety interlock needs.

title: Vibration End Alert
new_elements: VibratingDoorHandle (Handle vibrates gently when the timer completes instead of relying on a bell.); SilentPhysicalAlert (Delivers a done signal through touch.); SmallMassActuator (Low-cost eccentric motor or piezo actuator integrated into the handle.)
rationale: Done feedback is touch-based and needs no explanation.
judge_comment: Haptic done alert is simple and plausible but only addresses the end signal, not the operation learning curve, and the handle is rarely touched at the moment the cycle finishes.

title: Big LED Ring
new_elements: RingOfLight (A large light ring on the door shows cooking state and remaining intensity.); VisualProgressOnly (Replaces numeric or dial comprehension with light progression.); SegmentedLightRing (Low-cost LEDs driven by timer and duty-cycle cams.)
rationale: A glowing ring makes state obvious without dial reading.
judge_comment: An intuitive light ring for status is feasible and helpful, but it is a common idea and only covers feedback, not input.

title: Push-to-Stop Default
new_elements: PushStopOnly (Press once for a default cycle; press again to stop.); DefaultThirtySeconds (Uses a common short time as the only start choice.); SpringReturnButton (Mechanical one-press switch with a fixed short-duration cam.)
rationale: The first and only control action is start, with no time choice.
judge_comment: A single-button fixed-time start removes all learning and is very easy to build, though a fixed 30 seconds limits usefulness.

title: Auto Door Pop
new_elements: AutoDoorPopButton (A door-release mechanism that ejects the door open after a short press.); HandsFreeOpen (Opens the door with less force and timing judgment.); ElectromagneticPop (Solenoid or magnetic assist for one-action opening.)
rationale: Opening no longer requires understanding the latch button.
judge_comment: Pop-open doors already exist, and this addresses the latch rather than the core operation learning curve.

title: Adhesive Cook Sticker
new_elements: AdhesiveCookSticker (Reusable stickers on food packages encode preset times for common items.); StickToCook (Matches external sticker cues to default microwave settings.); ExternalQRRead (A simple reader or visual code links package type to cooking defaults.)
rationale: Users follow food-pack cues instead of learning appliance controls.
judge_comment: Package-driven cooking cues remove the need to learn controls and are novel, but they need a reader, ecosystem adoption and a clear mechanism, and the idea is muddled between stickers and QR codes.

title: Door-Key Timer
new_elements: DoorKeyTimer (A slot on the door accepts a key or tag that sets cooking duration.); DoorInsertsTime (Time comes from the inserted physical key.); MechanicalKeyHinge (Key shape or depth drives the time cam directly.)
rationale: Time selection becomes a physical key action with no dial learning.
judge_comment: A physical key setting the time is novel and mechanically plausible, but users must still pick and manage keys, which adds a learning step and limits flexibility.

title: Stationary Cavity
new_elements: StationaryCavity (Fixed cavity geometry replaces the rotating turntable and its setup decisions.); NoRattleSetup (Food placement is less sensitive and requires no turntable alignment.); FixedMicrowaveField (Waveguide placement or field shaping provides acceptable heating without a turntable.)
rationale: Removes turntable handling and the learning about food orientation.
judge_comment: Removing the turntable simplifies handling a little but does not address operation of controls, and even heating without it is a known challenge.

title: Hold-to-Cook Bar
new_elements: HoldToCookBar (A large bar that starts and runs while held, then stops after release.); HoldSetsSeconds (Cooking duration is simply how long the user keeps the bar pressed.); PressureTimeCapacitor (Mechanical pressure-to-duration integration using springs or cams.)
rationale: Time is represented by the natural action of holding the start control.
judge_comment: Hold-to-cook is intuitive and needs no learning, though long cook times make holding impractical and it raises ergonomic and safety questions.

title: Place-and-Close Shelf
new_elements: AutoCookShelf (A tray that starts a default cycle when food is placed and the door closes.); PlaceAndClose (Operation reduces to place food and shut door.); WeightSwitchStart (A simple weight or presence switch arms the start relay.)
rationale: The only steps are placing food and closing the door.
judge_comment: Place and close is the ultimate simple operation, but a single default cycle fits few foods and weight sensing is crude.

title: Single Preset Dial
new_elements: OnePresetDial (A dial with only named food presets instead of separate time and power controls.); FoodOnlyDial (Each detent maps a food type to time and power.); PresetCamStack (Mechanical cams convert one dial position into time and duty-cycle settings.)
rationale: Users choose a food type, not microwave numbers.
judge_comment: A food-based preset dial is easy to understand and feasible with cams, but similar to existing auto-cook presets, so it is not very radical.

title: Acoustic Doneness Door
new_elements: CavityAudioTap (A door-mounted listener amplifies cavity sounds to help judge boiling or simmering.); ListenToDoneness (Provides an audible cue for when food seems done.); CavityAcousticTap (Mechanical or piezoelectric sound transfer through the door structure.)
rationale: Sound gives a familiar done cue without settings knowledge.
judge_comment: Novel audio cue, but it adds a judgment task and cavity sound is a weak indicator of doneness, so it only loosely serves a no-learning-curve goal.

title: One-Cable Power Block
new_elements: OneWirePowerBlock (A universal input block eliminates regional plug or frequency confusion.); OneCableSetup (The user only connects one visible power cable anywhere.); WideInputSwitchMode (AC power electronics accept broad mains variants without user awareness.)
rationale: Power setup becomes a no-decision task for the user.
judge_comment: Universal input is feasible and common in electronics, but it addresses setup rather than operation and is not radical.

title: Self-Wiping Door
new_elements: DoorWiperModule (Door frame wipes condensation or residue automatically after cooking.); HandsFreeClean (Reduces maintenance decisions after simple use.); CapillarySpongeWiper (Passive material wiper around the door edge.)
rationale: Cleaning no longer interrupts the simple operation loop.
judge_comment: Passive wiping is plausible but is about cleaning, not operational simplicity.

title: One-Red Start Button
new_elements: OneRedStartButton (A single red button starts a fixed full-donation cycle for common reheating.); OneTouchFullHeat (No time or power choice, only start.); HardwiredFullDuty (Direct switch to magnetron without control selection.)
rationale: A single red button removes all setting choices.
judge_comment: A single start button eliminates all choices and directly serves the need, though full power only is crude and risks overheating.

title: Shape-Mold Tray
new_elements: ShapeMoldTray (Tray shapes or thickness cues tell the microwave how long and how strongly to heat.); ShapeSetsTime (Food geometry determines cooking settings.); MoldedCavityInsert (Simple inserts that encode load shape through mass or mechanical switches.)
rationale: The tray makes choices through shape rather than dial settings.
judge_comment: Mechanically encoding the cooking program in tray shape is clever and requires no learning, but needs multiple trays and is limited in variety.

title: End-Pop Door
new_elements: EndOpenDoor (Door pops open automatically when cooking ends.); DoorPopsWhenDone (Completion is communicated by the door itself opening.); BiStablePopHinge (Latching hinge released by timer cam or end switch.)
rationale: The appliance finishes by opening itself, removing alert-interpretation learning.
judge_comment: Auto-opening door makes completion obvious and is mechanically simple, but it does not address how to start or set a cook, so it only partly serves the no-learning-curve need.

title: Plug-in Start
new_elements: PlugDetectStart (Connecting power starts a very short default cycle or arms the door for immediate use.); PlugInStartsDefault (Operation begins with the most familiar electrical action.); PlugDetectRelay (Simple plug or voltage sensing trigger.)
rationale: Power connection becomes the first operation step instead of learning controls.
judge_comment: Starting a cycle on plug-in is a quirky idea, but it is unsafe and confusing, and it does not help with real operation.

title: Heat-Paint Door
new_elements: ThermalPaintDoor (Door or handle changes color to show whether the cycle is hot, mild, or idle.); HeatLevelVisible (Power state is inferred from color without knob comprehension.); RFResistantThermochromicPaint (Safe heat-responsive coating on external surfaces.)
rationale: Power level becomes a color cue instead of a setting to learn.
judge_comment: A color cue for heat is intuitive, but it is passive, shows the wrong thing, and thermochromic paint inside an RF environment is questionable.

title: Scent-Stop Sensor
new_elements: ScentStopSensor (A simple sensor stops cooking when a target aroma appears.); AromaEndsCooking (Uses smell cues instead of learned times.); FoodOdorChemSensor (Low-cost odor threshold detection for common reheated foods.)
rationale: The appliance stops at a familiar smell cue instead of asking for time.
judge_comment: Cooking until the food smells done removes time entry entirely, which is radical and on-need, but odor sensing is unreliable across foods.

title: Single Cook Lever
new_elements: SingleCookLever (One large lever starts, selects a short default, and returns when done.); LeverStarts (Lever motion replaces knobs and buttons.); LeverDrivenTimePowerCam (A single lever drives both timer and duty-cycle cams.)
rationale: One large motion replaces several unfamiliar controls.
judge_comment: A single large lever driving timer and duty-cycle cams is highly intuitive, cheap, mechanically proven, and fits the substitute operator well.

title: Touch-Door Start
new_elements: TouchDoorStart (Tap the door surface to start a short default cycle.); TapDoorStarts (Uses the door itself as the start control.); DoorCapacitiveSense (A simple touch sensor embedded in the door frame.)
rationale: Start is placed on the door where the user already stands.
judge_comment: Tapping the door to start a default cycle is simple and plausible, but accidental starts and an empty-cavity risk need handling, and it is only a modest substitution.

title: Fading Time Handle
new_elements: FadingHandle (Handle color fades as heat or time decreases, giving a done cue without reading.); HeatFadeTimeLeft (Time left becomes visible through fading material.); ThermalWaxIndicator (Wax or pigment element changes appearance with simple temperature history.)
rationale: Time remaining is visible without dial reading.
judge_comment: A fading handle is a creative done cue, but it only shows time left and doesn't help with operation; a handle is also a poor place for a thermal indicator since microwaves heat food, not the handle.

title: Big Remote Only
new_elements: OneRemoteBigButtons (The appliance has no panel knobs; a large remote with one start button controls it.); RemoteOnlyStart (Operation is a single remote press.); RFRemoteButton (Simple one-way radio link to a mechanical or electronic relay.)
rationale: Remote operation brings controls to hand height and removes panel-learning.
judge_comment: A one-button RF remote is feasible and simple, but it is easy to lose, adds a part, and still needs a way to set time, so it is not very radical.

title: Door-State Power
new_elements: DoorStatePower (Door position and latch engagement set the power behavior.); DoorStateSetsPower (Average power is inferred from door geometry instead of a knob.); MagneticDoorAngle (Magnetic or reed sensing maps door state to duty-cycle control.)
rationale: Door behavior supplies power selection without extra controls.
judge_comment: Using door angle to set power is novel but unintuitive, which adds a learning curve, and the door must be closed during operation, so it is mostly impractical.

title: Self-Determined Cavity
new_elements: SelfDeterminedCavity (Cavity electronics determine time and power from load, temperature, and acoustic cues.); SelfDeterminedCooking (No user settings are required for common tasks.); ThermalImpedance (Uses simple electrical or acoustic impedance changes to infer food condition.)
rationale: The appliance chooses settings, so the user does not learn them.
judge_comment: Auto-detecting load and settings removes the need to learn anything and fits the brief well, but reliable sensing of arbitrary food is hard and the mechanisms are vague.

title: Big Red and Stop Door
new_elements: RedGreenDoorButton (Green door area starts, red handle area stops, using color and position only.); OnlyStartStop (All operation reduces to go or stop.); HighContrastMechanicalButton (Large color-coded mechanical switches integrated into the door.)
rationale: Color-coded start and stop remove any need for dial or menu learning.
judge_comment: Simple color-coded start/stop is easy to learn, but it is a modest change and offers no way to set time or power.

title: Cup Timer Tokens
