new_elements: CupTimerTokens (A cup-like holder accepts beads or discs that drop one at a time to set short cooking periods.); DropInTokens (Counted tokens translate directly to familiar short time units.); GravitationalTokenCounter (Mechanical counting of falling or inserted tokens.)
rationale: Tokens make counting time intuitive without reading a knob.
judge_comment: Tokens that count time are playful and tangible, but they add handling steps and the mechanism is unclear.

title: Portion-Slot Door
new_elements: PortionSlotDoor (Door opening is triggered by a food slot that recognizes a single serving.); InsertPortionOpens (Inserting a portion unlocks the door into the correct cooking mode.); PortionTriggerLever (Mechanical lever or switch driven by container geometry.)
rationale: The door becomes a feeding slot that starts the right cooking mode.
judge_comment: Having the food slot trigger the cooking mode is radical, but container geometry cannot reliably identify what to cook.

title: Open-Stops-All Switch
new_elements: DoorBreakSwitch (Any door opening instantly stops all action in the most obvious way.); OpenStopsAll (No learned pause or cancel sequence is needed.); MechanicalInterlock (Simple door-linked switch or latch break.)
rationale: Stopping becomes a natural door action rather than a learned control.
judge_comment: Opening the door already stops a microwave, so this adds almost nothing new, though it is feasible and intuitive.

title: Food-Scale Plate
new_elements: FoodScalePlate (The plate weighs food and shows or sets a sensible default cycle.); WeighsAndStarts (Weight alone determines a basic cooking plan.); CapacitiveMassPlate (Low-cost plate sensing for common loads.)
rationale: Weight replaces time and power decisions with one natural action.
judge_comment: Weight-based automatic settings remove choices, but weight is a poor proxy for food type and heating needs.

title: Thermo-Fluid Timer
new_elements: ThermoFluidTimer (A sealed fluid expansion element shows a countdown without electrical timers.); BubbleTimeLeft (A visible fluid or bubble indicates remaining simple time.); SealedLiquidExpansion (Thermal expansion mechanism for passive timing cues.)
rationale: Time becomes a visible physical change instead of an abstract number.
judge_comment: A visible physical countdown is intuitive, but a sealed fluid element in a microwave is hard to make work and doesn't clearly replace the timer.

title: Lever Door
new_elements: LeverDoor (A long door lever opens the cavity and, if pushed inward, starts the default cycle.); PullOpenPushStart (Direction of door motion gives open and start behavior.); IntegratedDoorLever (One mechanical lever couples door movement to start switches.)
rationale: A familiar lever action combines open and start without panel learning.
judge_comment: Combining open and start in one lever motion is simple and easy to build, though pushing to start could trigger it by accident and a default cycle may not suit every food.

title: Self-Lighting Cavity
new_elements: SelfLightingCavity (Cavity liner glows safely enough to reveal food without a visible window or separate lamp.); MicrowaveGlowView (Provides a soft visual cue through material luminescence.); PhosphorescentCavityLiner (Low-emission liner that changes brightness with heat or electrical stimulus.)
rationale: A glowing cavity gives visible feedback without understanding a mesh window.
judge_comment: A glowing cavity liner gives feedback but does little for ease of operation, and a phosphorescent liner is questionable in a microwave.

title: Volume-Set Power Cavity
new_elements: VolumePowerCavity (Cavity geometry or reflection estimates food volume and chooses average power.); VolumeSetsPower (Power follows food volume rather than a manual dial.); RFReflectionVolumeEstimator (Simple microwave reflection or cavity loading estimate.)
rationale: Power becomes an automatic consequence of food volume instead of a dial.
judge_comment: Setting power automatically from food volume removes a decision, but RF load sensing is imprecise and the approach isn't entirely new.

title: Drawer Microwave
new_elements: DrawerMicrowave (Whole appliance opens as a drawer rather than a hinged door with latch.); PullCloseCook (Close and pull are the only door operations.); DrawerLatchingMechanism (Rail-based latch that also breaks heating when pulled.)
rationale: A drawer uses an already familiar open-close motion for microwave access.
judge_comment: A drawer is a familiar motion, but it adds little beyond the door and has sealing and spillage problems.

title: One-push automatic cook
new_elements: One-push auto cook lever (A single push lever starts a default reheating cycle and stops when the cavity cools.); Zero-learning push-cycle function (Lets the user cook without dialing time or power.)
rationale: It replaces both knobs with a familiar push motion, serving.
judge_comment: A single push to start a default reheat is very simple, but detecting when the cavity has cooled is vague and unreliable, and one default cycle limits what it can cook.

title: Door-close start latch
new_elements: Magnetic auto-close door latch (Closing the door engages the cook cycle automatically.); Door-close start function (Uses the obvious door action as the start signal.)
rationale: It removes a start button by making closing the door the only instruction, serving.
judge_comment: Starting a cycle by closing the door is intuitive and easy to build, though it risks accidental starts and still needs some way to set the time.

title: Pull-to-set countdown lever
new_elements: Spring-loaded pull timer (The user pulls a lever to 30 seconds, 1 minute, or 3 minutes and it returns automatically.); Pull-to-set timing function (Provides timing with one motion instead of rotational dial reading.)
rationale: It replaces the clockwork knob with a single pull motion, serving.
judge_comment: A spring-return pull lever with three fixed times is concrete and mechanically plausible, and it replaces the dial in a clear way.

title: Warm/Hot two-mode toggle
new_elements: Warm/Hot tactile toggle (A two-position switch selects gentle or full heating without five-step interpretation.); Two-mode power choice function (Offers only the power decisions users actually understand.)
rationale: It simplifies power selection to one obvious binary choice, serving.
judge_comment: A two-position toggle is trivially feasible and easy to understand, but it is incremental rather than radical.

title: Color-coded cook plates
new_elements: Color-coded cook plates (Blue plate runs full power, yellow medium, and orange low; the plate sets the control through a slot.); Plate-driven cycle function (Turns abstract power/time choices into visual food-plate matching.)
rationale: It lets users match a color to food instead of reading knobs, serving.
judge_comment: Color plates that set the cycle through a slot are original and concrete, but handling and matching plates adds a learning step, and keeping track of loose plates is a practical drawback.

title: Transparent RF-safe casing
new_elements: Clear RF-safe casing (A transparent microwave-transparent window and casing replace holes plus bulb.); No-lamp viewing function (Shows food directly under normal kitchen light without illumination controls.)
rationale: It removes the lamp and mesh complexity so the user simply looks, serving.
judge_comment: A transparent casing is hard to make RF-safe (the mesh is what shields) and it does little for operational simplicity, though seeing the food directly is mildly helpful.

title: Phosphorescent ready ring
new_elements: Phosphorescent cavity ring (A glow paint ring around the door marks the running state without electricity.); Passive ready-light function (Gives a low-tech visual signal that needs no bulb.)
rationale: It gives a simple always-visible status cue without learning lamp behavior, serving.
judge_comment: Phosphorescent paint is cheap and feasible, but it glows regardless of running state, so it can't signal that state and adds little to simple operation.

title: Aroma ready strip
new_elements: Heat-activated aroma strip (A tiny scent capsule releases after the cooking cycle ends.); Scent-ready function (Notifies the user through smell instead of reading a bell or timer.)
rationale: It replaces mechanical timing with a natural finish cue, serving.
judge_comment: A scent cue is unusual and needs no learning, but a capsule is single-use, unreliable, and doesn't simplify operating the controls.

title: Wearable vibration pager
new_elements: Wearable ready pager (A cheap coin-sized vibrator pairs with the timer and buzzes when done.); Body-notice function (Delivers end-of-cycle alert where the user can feel it.)
rationale: It removes the need to remember and watch the clock, serving.
judge_comment: A wearable pager is easy to build, but it adds a device to wear, charge, and pair, which cuts against zero learning curve.

title: Pop-up done flag
new_elements: Pop-up done flag (A mechanical flag pops from the fascia at cycle end.); Visual done function (Provides a one-glance finish signal without sound learning.)
rationale: It makes the end state obvious at a glance, serving.
judge_comment: A mechanical pop-up flag is simple, intuitive, and plausible, and it gives a clear finish cue, but it doesn't address how the user sets the cook.

title: Steam-sensing auto stop
new_elements: Steam-sensing auto-stop module (A hygrometer at the vent stops heating when steam production drops.); No-time automatic finish function (Ends cooking without user-set time or power.)
rationale: It eliminates dial settings by using steam as an intuitive done cue, serving.
judge_comment: Steam-based auto stop removes all settings, though vent humidity sensing is imperfect for dry or sealed foods; some microwaves already have similar sensors.

title: Weight-sensing auto time
new_elements: Weight-sensing turntable base (A load cell estimates food mass and chooses a default cycle.); Mass-based cycle function (Sets time and power from the plate weight instead of knobs.)
rationale: It lets the user place food and walk away, serving.
judge_comment: A load cell is easy to add, but mass alone poorly predicts the right cooking cycle, so it is a partial solution.

title: Pack-tag preset reader
new_elements: Pack-tag preset reader (A tiny RFID or barcode slot reads frozen-pack cooking instructions.); Read-and-cook function (Converts package instructions into one automatic cycle.)
rationale: It makes users follow the one familiar action of placing a tagged pack, serving.
judge_comment: Reading pack tags is workable and similar to existing barcode-cooking concepts, but it only helps with tagged products.

title: Big voice button
new_elements: Big voice button (A large press-to-talk button accepts only start, stop, and longer.); Plain-speech control function (Replaces dial reading with natural spoken requests.)
rationale: It uses an already known speech interaction instead of appliance-specific dials, serving.
judge_comment: Voice control is familiar and easy to use but already exists, and noisy kitchens may cause errors; the three-command limit keeps it simple.

title: Slot-in preset stick
new_elements: Slot-in preset stick (A wooden or plastic stick with a code sets time and power when inserted into a slot.); Stick-based cycle function (Provides physical preset choices with no screens.)
rationale: It replaces knobs with one insert action, serving.
judge_comment: A physical coded stick is a quirky, screen-free substitute for knobs, but users must keep and choose sticks, which adds some learning and clutter.

title: Door-handle timing lever
new_elements: Door-handle timing lever (A lever on the handle sets duration while opening or closing the door.); Handle-set timing function (Combines access and timing into the same natural motion.)
rationale: It puts timing on the part the user already touches, serving.
judge_comment: Combining timing with the door handle is intuitive and low-learning, though mapping lever position to duration while opening is mechanically fuzzy.

title: Foot-pedal door start
new_elements: Foot-pedal door/start switch (A pedal opens the door and starts the preset cycle hands-free.); Hands-free start function (Provides cooking control without reaching or dialing.)
rationale: It reduces coordination demands for simple start-and-stop, serving.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is simple and feasible, but it requires a preset cycle and doesn't remove the need to choose time or power.

title: Slide-out cavity drawer
new_elements: Slide-out cavity drawer (The cavity pulls out like a toaster drawer instead of hinging open.); Toaster-like access function (Makes loading and unloading a one-move action.)
rationale: It removes latch and hinge learning by using drawer familiarity, serving.
judge_comment: A drawer-style cavity is familiar in use, but sealing microwaves and containing spills in a drawer is hard.

title: Auto-eject end tray
new_elements: End-of-cycle auto-eject tray (The tray slides or lifts the food at cycle end.); Food-reveal function (Shows done food without the user opening the door to check.)
rationale: It replaces the need to wait, watch, and open with one automatic reveal, serving.
judge_comment: Auto-eject is convenient but adds mechanical complexity and still doesn't address how the cook time is set.

title: Thermal paint cavity
new_elements: Heat-changing cavity paint (The inside wall changes color when food reaches a target temperature.); Color-read finish function (Shows done status visually without lamp or timer.)
rationale: It lets the cavity itself indicate readiness, serving.
judge_comment: Thermal paint in a microwave cavity can't reliably indicate food temperature, since the walls don't reflect it, and it is a poor fit for the need.

title: Passive thermal sink fanless
new_elements: Passive thermal mass sink (A ceramic or aluminum sink absorbs magnetron heat instead of using a fan.); Fanless cooling function (Keeps the machine running without vents or noise the user must learn to avoid blocking.)
rationale: It removes fan and vent decisions, serving.
judge_comment: Passive cooling of a magnetron is questionable at kW heat loads, and users already make no fan decisions, so the link to M6 is weak.

title: Self-discharging HV core
new_elements: Self-discharging HV core (An integrated magnetron supply drains its own high voltage within seconds.); No-residual-charge function (Removes a hidden danger that can confuse service and use.)
rationale: It simplifies safety by making the appliance safe to touch after unplugging, serving.
judge_comment: A bleeder-style discharge is plausible and is already common practice, but it mainly benefits service rather than everyday operation.

title: Resettable thermal breaker
new_elements: Resettable thermal breaker (A push-button breaker replaces the disposable ceramic fuse.); One-click reset function (Turns a confusing fuse failure into a simple push.)
rationale: It removes fuse-reading and replacement learning, serving.
judge_comment: A resettable breaker is highly feasible and concrete, but it is an obvious swap that only touches a rare failure case.

title: Single magnet door sensor
new_elements: Single magnet-reed door sensor (One magnetic sensor detects door closure instead of three microswitches.); One-state safety function (Provides safe door interlock with fewer failure modes.)
rationale: It reduces confusing switch troubleshooting by making door safety self-evident, serving.
judge_comment: A single reed sensor is concrete, but safety standards require redundant interlocks, and users never see the switches anyway.

title: Self-cleaning water pack
new_elements: Self-cleaning water pack (A small sealed cup boiled by a one-touch steam pack loosens spills.); Wipe-clean steam function (Turns cleaning into a simple steam-and-wipe routine.)
rationale: It makes maintenance a one-step action instead of disassembly learning, serving.
judge_comment: A steam-clean cup is feasible and simplifies maintenance, though it is not really a substitution and has little to do with operating the microwave.

title: Removable splash tray
new_elements: Removable splash tray (A dishwasher-safe cover slides out instead of cleaning a fixed mica cover.); Snap-in clean function (Protects the waveguide with a single obvious removable part.)
rationale: It removes the need to understand waveguide covers, serving.
judge_comment: Practical and feasible, but it addresses cleaning rather than operation and is not very radical.

title: Windowless no-peek cavity
new_elements: Windowless sealed cavity (An opaque safe cavity eliminates mesh, lamp, and checking inside.); Trust-the-cycle function (Asks users to rely on one fixed preset instead of watching food.)
rationale: It removes the ambiguous habit of peeking, serving.
judge_comment: Bold removal of the window, but users want to see food and a fixed preset limits utility; operation is only loosely simplified.

title: Coaxial one-knob
new_elements: Coaxial one-knob (A single knob pushes inward for power and pulls outward for time.); One-hand setup function (Compresses two controls into one familiar rotation.)
rationale: It replaces two knobs with one object, serving.
judge_comment: Concrete and buildable, though a push/pull coaxial knob adds a bit of learning and is not very radical.

title: Fixed 45-second reheat mode
new_elements: Fixed 45-second reheat mode (A no-adjust machine has only one optimized reheat cycle.); One-size reheating function (Eliminates all settings for the most common household use.)
rationale: It serves by removing setup entirely, even at the cost of flexibility.
judge_comment: Eliminates learning entirely for the common case and is very simple to build, but it is inflexible and the idea is somewhat obvious.

title: Cup-height drink timer
new_elements: Cup-height drink timer (A mechanical ruler above the turntable times milk by how tall the cup is.); Size-cue drink timing function (Turns the familiar cup size into a simple time setting.)
rationale: It uses an obvious physical cue instead of dial numbers, serving.
judge_comment: A physical cue replaces numbers intuitively and is novel, but calibrating timing to cup height is imprecise, since liquid volume and cup shape vary.

title: Disposable heat pouch
new_elements: Disposable heat pouch (A sealed pouch with food, water, and a thermal stop lets the oven run until it shuts itself.); Pouch-driven cook function (Moves time and power selection into a single food pack.)
rationale: It removes the learning curve by making the package the setting, serving.
judge_comment: Package-encoded cooking removes all settings, but it is similar to existing barcode or steam-valve packaging and locks users into proprietary food.

title: Thermochromic heat strip
new_elements: Thermochromic heat strip (A sticker or plate changes color when the food is hot enough.); Strip-read finish function (Ends cooking by matching a color rather than reading a timer.)
rationale: It gives a one-glance done signal without dial knowledge, serving.
judge_comment: Thermochromic indicators are feasible and intuitive for doneness, but they don't control the oven, so the user still has to set the time.

title: Open-stop/close-resume door
new_elements: Open-stop/close-resume door (The door itself pauses when opened and continues when closed, removing stop buttons.); Door-state control function (Uses the most common action to replace button learning.)
rationale: It maps control directly to door behavior, serving.
judge_comment: Microwaves already pause when the door opens, so this adds little beyond making resume automatic, though it is easy to build.

title: Pull-cord countdown
new_elements: Pull-cord countdown (A shower-style cord starts a timed cycle and a second pull stops it.); Pull-to-run function (Uses a single familiar mechanical action instead of a knob.)
rationale: It replaces dialing with one pull, serving.
judge_comment: A pull cord is simple and familiar, but a fixed countdown ignores food variation and a cord is awkward on a kitchen appliance.

title: Built-in sand timer
new_elements: Built-in sand timer (A rotating sand glass shows duration and releases a switch when empty.); Sand-flow timing function (Provides timing without reading numbers.)
rationale: It uses a familiar household timer cue, serving.
judge_comment: A sand timer is intuitive and mechanical, but fixed durations and a mechanical switch are clumsy, and it is not very radical.

title: Shelf-position power selector
new_elements: Two shelf positions (A low gentle shelf and a high hot shelf replace the power dial.); Shelf-level power function (Turns power choice into obvious object placement.)
rationale: It uses placement instead of dial reading, serving.
judge_comment: Shelf height does not straightforwardly change microwave power, so the mechanism is questionable, though the placement-as-control concept is intuitive and novel.

title: Hand-size decal guide
new_elements: Hand-size decal guide (A printed hand-size chart around the door tells users to press once per minute.); Size-based time cue function (Converts food size into a simple counting pattern.)
rationale: It gives an intuitive physical reference instead of numeric dials, serving.
judge_comment: A printed decal is cheap and easy, but press-once-per-minute counting still requires some learning and is imprecise.

title: Food-shape buttons
new_elements: Food-shape buttons (Buttons shaped like a cup, plate, and bag choose sensible cycles for common foods.); Item-type selection function (Lets users choose what they are heating instead of interpreting power levels.)
rationale: It aligns controls with recognizable food shapes, serving.
judge_comment: Item-shaped preset buttons are easy to build and understand, though similar to existing preset buttons.

title: Transparent shield door
new_elements: Transparent RF-shield door (A microwave-safe transparent panel replaces the perforated mesh window.); Direct-view door function (Shows the cavity plainly without lamp or hole interpretation.)
rationale: It makes viewing obvious and removes mesh/light confusion, serving.
judge_comment: A transparent RF shield is plausible with conductive films, but it addresses viewing rather than operation, so it barely serves the no-learning-curve need.

title: Self-opening end latch
new_elements: Self-opening end latch (The latch releases and swings the door open at cycle end.); End-of-cycle auto-open function (Provides access exactly when food is ready without user decisions.)
rationale: It removes the need to remember to open the door, serving.
judge_comment: A motorized door release is feasible and removes one step, but it does not simplify setting the cook cycle and could be a safety issue.

title: Door halo alert light
new_elements: Door halo alert light (A ring around the door flashes gently when cooking finishes.); Light alert function (Replaces mechanical bell with a simple visible cue.)
rationale: It gives an unambiguous end cue without learning bell tones, serving.
judge_comment: Easy to build and clear, but it only improves the end-of-cycle cue and does little for operating the oven, and it isn't radical.

title: Plug-as-switch cord
new_elements: Plug-as-switch cord (Inserting the mains plug starts a fixed default cycle; removing it stops the oven.); Insert-to-start function (Uses an existing familiar action to replace controls.)
rationale: It removes a panel by making plug insertion the only operation, serving.
judge_comment: Plug-in-to-start is radical and needs no learning, but a single fixed cycle fits few foods, and starting when plugged in and running unattended raises safety problems.

title: Solid-state cooking core
new_elements: Solid-state RF cooking core (A sealed RF module replaces the magnetron transformer-capacitor-diode set.); No-HV-service function (Reduces scary high-voltage complexity and failure states.)
rationale: It serves by removing hazardous and confusing electronics behind one sealed unit.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF is a real technology, but it is costly and high-power units are immature, and it does little to simplify the user's operation.

title: Twist-handle start
new_elements: Twist-handle start (Rotating the door handle 30 degrees sets the default cycle while opening or closing.); Twist-to-cook function (Uses the natural handle motion to eliminate dials.)
rationale: It folds timing into a familiar twist, serving.
judge_comment: Twisting the handle is an intuitive, novel control, but a single default cycle is limiting and the door interlock mechanics are tricky.

title: Press-to-stop ready button
new_elements: One-button stop-confirm (A single button stops and acknowledges the cycle, replacing bell and knobs.); Press-to-done function (Provides a clear endpoint with no timing judgment.)
rationale: It gives one obvious endpoint action, serving.
judge_comment: A single stop button is simple and workable, but it's an incremental change and leaves open how cooking starts.

title: Colored time spoon
new_elements: Colored time spoon (The user stirs once for red, twice for blue, or thrice for green to set 1, 2, or 3 minutes.); Stir-to-set function (Converts timing into a kitchen ritual.)
rationale: It uses cooking gestures rather than appliance reading, serving.
judge_comment: Playful gesture-based timing, but sensing stirs and color-coding is implausible and the spoon is an extra item to learn and keep track of.

title: Food-pressure auto plate
new_elements: Food-pressure auto plate (Pressing the turntable to seat the plate starts a size-based cycle.); Press-and-place cycle function (Combines loading and starting into one action.)
rationale: It removes extra start steps, serving.
judge_comment: Load-and-start in one action is intuitive, but plate-size sensing and accidental starts are concerns.

title: Silent door-thump ready
new_elements: Magnetic door-thump mechanism (The door latch snaps into a tuned cavity plate, replacing the bell with one physical thump.); Mechanical thump function (Produces a simple ready signal with fewer parts.)
rationale: It gives a minimal single-part ready cue, serving.
judge_comment: A mechanical ready cue replaces the bell, but it barely helps ease of operation and may be unclear or too quiet.

title: Haptic door knob
new_elements: Haptic door knob (The handle vibrates once at cycle end and releases for opening.); Touch-ready function (Tells users when to open without sound or dials.)
rationale: It places feedback on the object users already use, serving.
judge_comment: A vibrating handle is feasible and gives intuitive feedback, but it only addresses the end-of-cycle signal.

title: Single-latch kitchen control
new_elements: Single-latch kitchen control (All start, stop, and time are integrated into the door latch; no fascia remains.); No-panel operation function (Leaves one obvious control on the door.)
rationale: It removes an entire control panel to leave a single intuitive motion, serving.
judge_comment: A single door-latch control is a radical simplification, though setting time and power through one latch is ambiguous.
